title: Scoring clarity findings
schema: Edit only label/helpText/option.description/pearls. Do not change calculate() or option.value.

findings.name: New Ballard Score (Gestational Age)
findings.current: Neuromuscular items give angles or terse posture phrases with no exam maneuver. Heel-to-ear includes 'Moderate resistance (1)'. Genitals are 'Very premature / Early / Developing / Maturing / Near term / Term'. Eye/ear fuses 'Lids fused loosely (−1) / tightly (−2)' into one option valued −1.
findings.problem: A bedside examiner cannot administer the neuromuscular items or score genitals from the UI. Official New Ballard is pictorial and sex-specific: male scores use scrotum/testes/rugae; female scores use clitoris vs labia minora/majora. Combined 'very premature…term' labels require recalling the chart. Maneuvers (supine rest posture; wrist square-window pressure; 5-second flex then release for arm recoil; thigh-to-abdomen popliteal; scarf draw; heel-to-ear without forcing) are unstated. Arm recoil '<110° (3)' and '<90° (4)' overlap. Tightly fused lids (−2) cannot be selected.
findings.suggested_change: Keep existing numeric values. Add helpText with official maneuvers (BallardScore.com monograph): posture — infant supine, wait for preferred rest posture; square window — straighten fingers, gentle dorsum pressure, angle palm-to-forearm; arm recoil — supine, flex then briefly fully extend and release, measure elbow recoil; popliteal — thigh beside abdomen, extend until resistance, angle behind knee; scarf — draw arm across chest, note elbow vs midline/nipple/axilla; heel to ear — draw foot toward ipsilateral ear without forcing. Replace genitals option labels/descriptions with official paired M/F findings per point: −1 scrotum flat smooth / clitoris prominent labia flat; 0 scrotum empty faint rugae / prominent clitoris small minora; 1 testes upper canal rare rugae / prominent clitoris enlarging minora; 2 testes descending few rugae / majora and minora equally prominent; 3 testes down good rugae / majora large minora small; 4 testes pendulous deep rugae / majora cover clitoris and minora. Split eye/ear lids into official tightly fused (−2) vs loosely fused (−1) options. Replace overlapping arm-recoil bins with exclusive official ranges (180 / 140–180 / 110–140 / 90–110 / <90). Expand heel-to-ear 'Moderate resistance' to positional official language.
findings.research: Ballard JL et al. J Pediatr 1991; New Ballard Score sheet and neuromuscular monograph at ballardscore.com (scoresheet PDF; Genitals-Male/Female articles)
findings.do_not_change: calculate() domain sum, total-score mode, weeks interpolation table, option point magnitudes except adding the missing official −2 lids option

findings.name: Bedside PEWS (Pediatric Early Warning)
findings.current: HR, RR, SBP options are 'Normal for age (0) / Mildly abnormal (1) / Moderately abnormal (2) / Severely abnormal (3)' with no bpm or mmHg. Respiratory effort is 'Normal / Mild / Moderate / Severe / impending failure'.
findings.problem: Bedside PEWS cannot be scored without the Parshuram age-band vital tables. 'Mildly/moderately/severely abnormal' has no operational cutoff; a 2-month-old HR of 160 is not the same band as a 10-year-old. User must recall or open an external PEWS card (exactly the NIHSS/CIWA failure mode). Pearls already admit 'Apply age-band vital norms from your hospital PEWS chart.'
findings.suggested_change: Do not change 0/1/2/3 values (official Bedside PEWS uses 0/1/2/4 — leave that mapping). Add helpText (and/or option.description) with Parshuram age-band cutoffs for HR, RR, and SBP, e.g. HR <3 mo: 110–149 = 0; ≥150 or ≤110 = 1; ≥180 or ≤90 = 2; ≥190 or ≤80 = 3 (educational). Repeat for 3–12 mo, 1–4 y, 5–12 y, ≥12 y from the published table. RR and SBP same source. For respEffort, use official anchors: Normal; Mild increase; Moderate increase; Severe increase or any apnea. Optional: one-line helpText 'Cap refill scored at the bedside; use institutional age table if it differs.'
findings.research: Parshuram CS et al. Bedside PEWS appendix (Pediatr Child Health 2011 Appendix B; PMC3077313); original item table PMC2750193
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–3, calculate() sum, escalation bands 0–2 / 3–4 / 5–6 / ≥7

findings.name: Pediatric Asthma Score (PAS)
findings.current: Respiratory rate options: 'Normal for age (1) / Mildly elevated (2) / Markedly elevated (3)'. Other PAS items have operational findings (SpO2 numbers, wheeze location, retraction sites, speech).
findings.problem: Published PAS pathways score RR with age-specific breaths/min, not 'mildly/markedly elevated'. A bedside user cannot choose 1 vs 2 vs 3 without an external age table (common 2–3 y ≤34/35–39/≥40; 4–5 y ≤30/31–35/≥36; 6–12 y ≤26/27–30/≥31; >12 y ≤23/24–27/≥28).
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1/2/3. Add helpText listing age-band RR cutoffs used by common PAS pathways (quote a single published table, e.g. Kelly/Children's Mercy / FPNotebook). Example: '2–3 y: ≤34 = 1, 35–39 = 2, ≥40 = 3; 4–5 y: ≤30 / 31–35 / ≥36; 6–12 y: ≤26 / 27–30 / ≥31; >12 y: ≤23 / 24–27 / ≥28. Use hospital PAS chart if it differs.'
findings.research: Kelly CS et al. Ann Allergy Asthma Immunol 2000; Children's Mercy PAS table; FPNotebook Pediatric Asthma Score
findings.do_not_change: 1–3 item values, 5–15 total, mild ≤7 / moderate 8–11 / severe 12–15 bands

findings.name: Neonatal Infant Pain Scale (NIPS)
findings.current: Single-word stems: Relaxed/Grimace; No cry/Whimper/Vigorous cry; Relaxed/Change in breathing; Restrained/relaxed vs Flexed/extended; Sleeping/awake quiet vs Fussy.
findings.problem: Official NIPS operational findings are missing, so items are easy to mis-score. 'Flexed/extended' looks like any flexion scores 1; official 1 is tense/rigid/rapid flexion-extension, while 0 is no rigidity (including restrained). 'Change in breathing' does not list irregular, faster, gagging, breath-holding. Grimace is not described (tight muscles, furrowed brow/chin/jaw). Intubated silent cry (mouth/face movement = vigorous cry) is only in pearls, not on the cry item.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/2 values. Put official Lawrence descriptors on option.description or expanded labels: Face 0 restful/neutral, 1 tight muscles furrowed brow chin jaw; Cry 0 quiet, 1 mild intermittent moan, 2 loud shrill continuous; Breathing 0 usual pattern, 1 indrawing/irregular/faster/gagging/breath-holding; Arms/legs 0 no rigidity, occasional random movement (restrained OK), 1 tense straight rigid rapid flex/extend; Arousal 0 quiet sleep or settled alert, 1 alert restless thrashing. Cry helpText: 'If intubated, silent cry with obvious mouth/face movement scores as vigorous cry (2).'
findings.research: Lawrence J et al. Neonatal Netw 1993; NIPS tool reprints (Mosby/CHEO descriptors)
findings.do_not_change: 0–7 sum, item point maxima (cry 0–2, others 0–1)

findings.name: N-PASS (Pain / Agitation / Sedation) Simplified
findings.current: Domain labels are fairly detailed (−2 to +2) but crying +2 is only 'High-pitched / inconsolable'. No prematurity adjustment input. No intubated silent-cry rule on the crying item.
findings.problem: Official N-PASS crying includes silent-continuous cry if intubated (+2) and intermittent silent cry (+1). Without that, ventilated neonates are under-scored. Hummel implementations add +1 to the pain score if <30 weeks (some later tools use +2/+3 by GA). Interpretation mentions prematurity only as a footnote after scoring, so the user cannot apply it.
findings.suggested_change: Keep −2..+2 values. Expand crying option.description: +1 'If intubated — intermittent silent cry'; +2 'High-pitched or inconsolable; if intubated — silent continuous cry'. Add helpText on crying: 'Painful stimuli examples: needle stick, ETT/nares suction, caregiving.' Add helpText on the form or a yesNo/GA note: 'If <30 weeks corrected, add +1 to pain subtotal (Hummel) — do not change domain values.' Optional: one-line helpText that assessment is over a care interval, not a single glance.
findings.research: Hummel P et al. N-PASS (J Perinatol 2008); N-PASS visual tool (Hummel & Puchalski) scoring criteria
findings.do_not_change: −2 to +2 domain values, pain vs sedation subtotal logic in calculate()

findings.name: Downes' Score (Neonatal Respiratory Distress)
findings.current: Air entry: 'Normal / Mildly decreased / Markedly decreased'. Retractions: 'None / Mild / Moderate–severe'. RR, cyanosis, and grunting already have operational cutoffs.
findings.problem: Air entry and retractions use mild/marked without auscultation or visual anchors. Official Downes air entry is 'clear / delayed or decreased / barely audible'. Retractions 'mild vs moderate–severe' is the published wording but still not operational compared with Silverman (just visible vs marked).
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/2. Expand airEntry labels to official auscultation: 0 Clear; 1 Delayed or decreased; 2 Barely audible. Add option.description on retractions if a local teaching definition exists (e.g. 1 = just visible intercostal; 2 = marked including xiphoid/suprasternal) without changing points. RR/cyanosis/grunt labels are already scorable.
findings.research: Downes JJ et al. Clin Pediatr 1970 (RDS score); common Downes teaching tables
findings.do_not_change: 0–2 item values, 0–10 total, mild ≤3 / 4–5 / ≥6 bands

findings.name: Bronchiolitis Clinical Severity Bands
findings.current: RR: 'Normal–mildly elevated for age / Moderately elevated / Markedly elevated or irregular / apneas'. WOB, feeding, O2, behavior have more operational findings.
findings.problem: No age-specific breaths/min, so 'moderately elevated' cannot be chosen reliably for a 6-week-old vs an 18-month-old. AAP bronchiolitis severity is clinical, but this calculator still asks the user to pick a numbered RR band.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/2. Add helpText with a single cited pediatric RR-for-age reminder (e.g. PALS/AAP ranges) mapping to 0/1/2, or 'Use local bronchiolitis pathway RR cutoffs by age; this item is not a validated numeric scale.' WOB labels (flaring, grunting, head bobbing) are already usable.
findings.research: Ralston SL et al. AAP bronchiolitis CPG Pediatrics 2014; PALS/AAP age-normal RR tables
findings.do_not_change: 0–2 domain values, apnea override, sum bands

findings.name: Pediatric Asthma Exacerbation Severity
findings.current: WOB: 'Minimal / Moderate / Severe retractions / Silent exhaustion'. HR: 'Normal–mildly elevated / Moderately elevated / Markedly elevated' (age-relative, no bpm). Speech, wheeze, SpO2 are operational.
findings.problem: NAEPP/GINA-style grading needs accessory-muscle detail and age-specific HR. 'Moderate' WOB and 'moderately elevated' HR cannot be scored from the UI. Speech/wheeze/SpO2 are already scorable.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values. Expand wob labels toward GINA/NAEPP: 0 little or no accessory use; 1 moderate retractions (intercostal ± subcostal); 2 severe (suprasternal, tracheal tug, nasal flaring); 3 silent chest / poor effort / exhaustion. Add hr helpText with pediatric age-relative tachycardia bands from the same GINA/NAEPP table used by the pathway (RESEARCH exact pediatric HR cutoffs from EPR-3/GINA acute-asthma figure).
findings.research: NHLBI EPR-3 acute asthma severity; GINA report acute exacerbation table
findings.do_not_change: item values, life-threatening override (altered / speech 3 / silent chest / WOB 3), sum bands

findings.name: SNAPPE-II (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: Labels are 'Lowest MAP / temp / PaO2/FiO2 / pH' with no epoch. Seizures is a 0–1 number: 'Multiple seizures (count as yes if ≥1 multiple episode cluster)'.
findings.problem: Official SNAPPE-II uses the worst physiology in the first 12 hours of life. Without that window, users may enter later NICU nadirs. Seizures wording is circular; official item is multiple seizures (yes/no) in that 12 h window.
findings.suggested_change: Add helpText to physiologic fields: 'Worst value in the first 12 hours of life (SNAP-II epoch).' Clarify seizures helpText: '1 = multiple seizures in first 12 h; 0 = none or a single seizure.' SGA helpText can stay 1 = yes, 0 = no; optional note official SGA is <3rd percentile.
findings.research: Richardson DK et al. J Pediatr 2001 SNAP-II / SNAPPE-II (first 12 h worst values)
findings.do_not_change: educational point bands in calculate(), input units

findings.name: Pediatric KDIGO AKI Stage (Creatinine)
findings.current: Baseline and current creatinine only. Stage 1 includes ratio ≥1.5 or absolute rise ≥0.3 mg/dL with no 48 h / 7 d question.
findings.problem: KDIGO Stage 1 absolute criterion is ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours; the 1.5× criterion is within 7 days. A 0.3 rise over weeks is not AKI. The UI will stage AKI whenever current − baseline ≥ 0.3 even if the user is comparing an old baseline.
findings.suggested_change: Add helpText on currentCr: 'Stage 1: ≥0.3 mg/dL rise within 48 h, or ≥1.5× baseline within 7 days (KDIGO). Use a creatinine from that window as baseline/current.' Optional helpText on baselineCr: 'Prior nadir or documented baseline; not an unrelated historical value.' Dialysis and eGFR <35 labels already state cutoffs.
findings.research: KDIGO AKI 2012 creatinine staging (48 h / 7 d windows)
findings.do_not_change: fold-change thresholds 1.5 / 2 / 3, Cr ≥4, RRT, eGFR <35 logic

findings.name: PECARN Blunt Abdominal Trauma (Simplified)
findings.current: One yes/no fuses 'abdominal wall trauma / seat-belt or handlebar injury or abdominal tenderness'. Vomiting has no post-injury qualifier. GCS ≤13 or altered mentation.
findings.problem: Holmes 2013 treats abdominal wall trauma/seat-belt sign and abdominal tenderness as separate predictors; fusing them makes isolated tenderness easy to miss. Vomiting in the rule is vomiting after the injury, not any lifetime vomiting. 'Altered mentation' may flag GCS 14, whereas the rule predictor is GCS <14 (low-risk if GCS 14–15).
findings.suggested_change: Keep yes/no values. Split or expand abdominalWall helpText: 'Yes if ANY: abdominal wall trauma, seat-belt sign, handlebar mark, OR abdominal tenderness (Holmes treats wall trauma and tenderness as separate predictors; either fails very-low-risk).' Vomiting helpText: 'Vomiting after the injury.' gcsLow helpText: 'GCS ≤13 (rule uses GCS <14); GCS 14–15 is the low-risk mental-status band.' Peritoneal/distracting items can stay as extra clinical flags with helpText that they are not in the published 7-variable rule.
findings.research: Holmes JF et al. Ann Emerg Med 2013 PECARN blunt abdominal injury rule (7 history/exam predictors)
findings.do_not_change: very-low-risk = no listed predictors logic, point chips

findings.name: PECARN Febrile Infant Rule (Simplified Age Bands)
findings.current: Positive urinalysis (LE, nitrite, or WBC per rule definition) — cutoff not stated.
findings.problem: User cannot mark UA positive without the PECARN definition. Kuppermann 2019: any leukocyte esterase, any nitrite, or >5 WBC/HPF (trace LE counts).
findings.suggested_change: Change uaPos label or helpText to: 'Positive UA: any LE (including trace), any nitrite, or >5 WBC/HPF (Kuppermann/PECARN).' ANC and PCT are raw numbers (tool applies ≤4090 and ≤1.71) — leave as-is; optional helpText reminding those cutoffs are applied automatically.
findings.research: Kuppermann N et al. JAMA Pediatr 2019; ALIEM/PECARN UA definition (LE, nitrite, >5 WBC/HPF)
findings.do_not_change: ANC 4090 and PCT 1.71 logic, age-band split, ill-appearing gate

findings.name: Incomplete Kawasaki Disease Lab Helper
findings.current: Clinical features helpText lists five names only. Anemia for age has no Hb. Echo positive cites 'Z-score criteria' without numbers. Other labs already have numeric cutoffs in the yes/no labels.
findings.problem: AHA principal features are specific: nonexudative bulbar conjunctival injection; cracked lips/strawberry tongue/injected pharynx; rash (not vesicular); extremity erythema/edema or periungual peel; cervical node ≥1.5 cm usually unilateral. 'Anemia for age' needs the age-specific lower limit of normal. Echo positive is Z ≥2.5 on LAD or RCA, aneurysm, or ≥3 supportive echo features.
findings.suggested_change: Expand clinicalFeatures helpText with AHA principal-feature bullets including lymphadenopathy ≥1.5 cm. anemia helpText: 'Yes if Hb below lab age-specific lower limit of normal (AHA “anemia for age”).' echoPos helpText: 'Yes if LAD or RCA Z ≥2.5, coronary aneurysm, or ≥3 supportive findings (LV dysfunction, mitral regurgitation, pericardial effusion, or Z 2–2.5).' CRP/ESR/plt/albumin/WBC/UA labels already scorable.
findings.research: McCrindle BW et al. Circulation 2017 AHA KD statement (incomplete algorithm + echo definition)
findings.do_not_change: inflam gate, ≥3/6 supplemental labs, fever <5 and ≥4-feature branches

findings.name: Philadelphia Criteria (Febrile Infant)
findings.current: Band-to-neutrophil ratio (or enter bands %/100), helpText 'Low-risk if band:neutrophil ratio <0.2 (classic)'.
findings.problem: Users confuse I:T (immature:total neutrophils) with band percentage/100. Entering 12% bands as 0.12 is not the Philadelphia BNR. Age eligibility (classically 29–56 days) is only in whenToUse, not on the form. WBC/UA/CSF are raw labs (tool applies cutoffs) and are fine.
findings.suggested_change: Replace bands helpText with: 'Enter immature:total neutrophil ratio (bands+other immature / total neutrophils). Example: 8 bands and 40 segs → 8/48 = 0.17. Do not enter band % as 0.xx unless that equals the I:T ratio. Low-risk if <0.2.' Add helpText on wellAppearing: 'Apply only in the intended age band (classic Philadelphia 29–56 days); ill-appearing infants are never low-risk.'
findings.research: Baker MD et al. N Engl J Med 1993 Philadelphia criteria (WBC 5–15k, BNR <0.2, UA <10, CSF <8)
findings.do_not_change: low-risk gate cutoffs in calculate() (WBC 5–15, BNR 0.2, UA 10, CSF 8)

findings.name: Gestational Hypertension Diagnostic Helper
findings.current: New BP ≥140/90 after 20 weeks on ≥2 occasions; severe-range ≥160/110 confirmed. No interval between readings.
findings.problem: ACOG diagnosis requires two occasions at least 4 hours apart for non-severe HTN. Severe-range BP is confirmed over a short interval (about 15 minutes), not 4 hours — waiting 4 h delays treatment. Protein/end-organ labels already include numeric cutoffs.
findings.suggested_change: after20 helpText: 'SBP ≥140 or DBP ≥90 on two occasions ≥4 hours apart after 20 weeks, previously normal BP (ACOG).' severeBp helpText: 'SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110 confirmed within ~15 minutes; do not wait 4 hours to treat.' Optional endOrgan helpText repeating the listed criteria is unnecessary if the label stays.
findings.research: ACOG Practice Bulletin 222 (2020) gestational HTN / preeclampsia diagnostic timing
findings.do_not_change: classification branches (chronic vs gestational vs preeclampsia)

findings.name: AVPU Responsiveness Scale
findings.current: A — Alert / V — Responds to voice / P — Responds to pain only / U — Unresponsive. Pearls mention recording the pain stimulus; the control does not.
findings.problem: How to apply voice vs pain, and what counts as Alert in an infant, are not on the options. Pain stimulus (trapezius squeeze or nail-bed) is an exam maneuver only in pearls.
findings.suggested_change: Add helpText: 'A = eyes open, interacting (crying infant can be Alert). V = any response to spoken/shouted voice. P = response only to pain (record trapezius or nail-bed stimulus). U = no response to voice or pain.' Keep A/V/P/U values.
findings.research: PALS/APLS AVPU teaching; APLS stimulus convention
findings.do_not_change: A/V/P/U mapping and GCS-band details

findings.name: WHO Dehydration Classification
findings.current: Skin pinch: Goes back quickly / slowly / very slowly (≥2 s). Condition, eyes, thirst already match WHO IMCI wording.
findings.problem: Result bins are official, but the maneuver (where and how to pinch) is unstated. Malnutrition false-positives are only in pearls.
findings.suggested_change: skin helpText: 'Pinch abdominal skin halfway between umbilicus and flank; release and watch. Very slow = ≥2 s (WHO). Unreliable in severe wasting — interpret with other signs.'
findings.research: WHO IMCI / diarrheal-disease treatment chart (four signs; Plan A/B/C)
findings.do_not_change: severe vs some sign counts, Plan A/B/C logic

findings.name: Estimated Fetal Weight (Hadlock Simplified)
findings.current: BPD/HC/AC/FL labeled in cm with typical cm defaults (e.g. BPD 8.5). No reminder that ultrasound reports are often in mm.
findings.problem: Entering 85 mm as 85 cm blows up EFW. Unit mix-up is the main bedside ambiguity on an otherwise pure formula.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on each biometric: 'Centimeters, not millimeters (divide machine mm by 10: 85 mm → 8.5 cm). Hadlock coefficients expect cm.'
findings.research: Hadlock FP et al. AJOG 1985 (measurements in cm)
findings.do_not_change: Hadlock log10 formulas or formula-set switch

findings.name: Clock Drawing Score (0–5)
findings.current: Options: 5 perfect; 4 minor visuospatial errors; 3 inaccurate time / moderate errors; 2 moderate number disorganization; 1 severe disorganization; 0 no reasonable clock. helpText only notes other scales. 11:10 is in pearls, not on the form.
findings.problem: User cannot administer the test: Shulman CDT requires the command to put numbers in and set hands to 10 past 11. Score 3 is wrong 11:10 with preserved layout, not generic moderate errors. Score 4 is unanchored.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: Give a blank page (or pre-drawn circle). Say: 'Draw a clock. Put in all the numbers. Set the hands to 10 minutes past 11 (11:10).' option.description: 5 circle+numbers+hands at 11:10 with longer minute hand; 4 11:10 correct with minor spacing errors; 3 layout OK but 11:10 wrong; 2 numbers crowded/missing/reversed so 11:10 impossible; 1 numbers not in recognizable sequence; 0 no reasonable clock. Do not change 0–5 values.
findings.research: Shulman KI Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 1993/2000 0–5 clock-drawing scoring; administration '10 past 11'
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–5, calculate() bands (≤3 abnormal), max 5

findings.name: SLUMS Cognitive Score
findings.current: Number entry SLUMS total 0–30 plus education select. Described as interpreter of an already-administered total.
findings.problem: SLUMS is free for clinical use (SLU/VA), not an MMSE/MoCA copyright wall. User still needs the protocol card (orientation, $100 story, 1-minute animals, 5-object recall, reverse digits, clock at ten to eleven, figures, Jill/Jack paragraph). Cannot administer from the UI.
findings.suggested_change: Replace total-only with official 11 SLUMS items as selectInput/numberInput using published point bands (animals 0–4/5–9/10–14/≥15; clock hour markers vs time; story questions). Keep education select for cutoff bands. helpText on delayed recall: the five objects named at registration. RESEARCH official SLU/VA PDF item wording and points; reprint only per SLU permission note.
findings.research: Tariq SH et al. Am J Geriatr Psychiatry 2006; official SLUMS examination PDF (Saint Louis University / VA)
findings.do_not_change: 0–30 total, education-adjusted bands (HS+ 27–30 / 21–26 / ≤20; <HS 25–30 / 20–24 / ≤19)

findings.name: HAM-D Depression Score
findings.current: Number entry HAM-D total 0–52 with helpText 'Usually 17-item total.' Version select is context only.
findings.problem: Original HAM-D (1960) is a clinician-rated anchored interview, not a Pearson form like MMSE. A total box cannot be scored at the bedside: items mix 0–4 and 0–2 with specific probes. User needs an external HAM-D card.
findings.suggested_change: Replace total-only with 17 selectInputs using official Hamilton anchors (do not invent 0–4 wording). helpText: 17-item HDRS; suicide item is clinical, not just a point. If a later copyright review of a structured interview (SIGH-D) forbids reprint, keep total-only and point to the official instrument (then treat as copyright-total-only).
findings.research: Hamilton M. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 1960; APA Handbook 17-item HDRS anchors. Confirm no third-party structured-interview copyright before reprinting.
findings.do_not_change: 17-item interpretation bands (≤7 / 8–13 / 14–18 / 19–22 / ≥23), version field as context only

findings.name: HAM-A Anxiety Score
findings.current: Number entry HAM-A total (0–56) with helpText '14 items scored 0–4.'
findings.problem: HAM-A items are 0–4 on 14 named symptom clusters (anxious mood, tension, fears, insomnia, somatic muscular/sensory, CV, respiratory, GI, GU, autonomic, behavior at interview). A total box requires the protocol card. Original 1959 scale is not a Pearson instrument.
findings.suggested_change: Add 14 selectInputs with Hamilton 0–4 anchors and official item titles. helpText: Rate the past few days; behavior at interview is observed, not reported. Same copyright fallback as HAM-D: if reprint not allowed, keep total-only with a pointer to the official form.
findings.research: Hamilton M. Br J Med Psychol 1959; standard HAM-A 14-item anchor reprints

findings.name: Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS)
findings.current: Number entry YMRS total (0–60) with helpText '11 items; some double-weighted (0–8).'
findings.problem: YMRS cannot be scored from a total. Four items are 0–8 (irritability, speech, thought content, disruptive-aggressive) and seven are 0–4, each with operational anchors. User needs the YMRS card.
findings.suggested_change: Replace with 11 selectInputs using Young 1978 anchors; keep 0–4 vs 0–8 weighting on the official double-weighted items. helpText: Based on interview + observation over the past 48 hours unless the form specifies otherwise. RESEARCH copyright (BJP/Royal College); if reprint is not allowed, keep total-only and point to the official instrument.
findings.research: Young RC et al. Br J Psychiatry 1978 YMRS item anchors
findings.do_not_change: 0–60 total, double-weight items, pragmatic bands ≤12 / 13–19 / 20–25 / ≥26

findings.name: PCL-5 PTSD Checklist
findings.current: Number entry PCL-5 total (0–80) with helpText '20 items scored 0–4 (Not at all → Extremely).'
findings.problem: PCL-5 is public domain (National Center for PTSD) — not a copyright-total-only exception. The 20 DSM-5 symptom stems and 0–4 labels are missing, so the patient cannot be scored from the UI. Cluster rule is only in evidence text.
findings.suggested_change: Add 20 selectInputs with NCPTSD PCL-5 stems and options Not at all (0) / A little bit (1) / Moderately (2) / Quite a bit (3) / Extremely (4). helpText: Past month. Rate how much you have been bothered. Optional details line for cluster counts. Official stems are free to reproduce.
findings.research: NCPTSD PCL-5 (Blevins 2015; https://www.ptsd.va.gov/professional/assessment/adult-sr/ptsd-checklist.asp). Public domain.
findings.do_not_change: 0–4 item values, 0–80 total, provisional cutoff band ~31–33

findings.name: Hoehn and Yahr Stage
findings.current: Stage labels name unilateral/bilateral/pull-test recovery/wheelchair. Pearl says pull test defines stage 3 but the form does not say how to do it or how many steps count as recovery vs failure.
findings.problem: Modified H&Y 2 vs 2.5 vs 3 is an exam maneuver (retropulsion/pull test). Without stance, warning, force of pull, step count, and catching a fall, a non-movement-disorder clinician cannot stage from the UI.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on stage: Pull test (retropulsion): patient stands, feet comfortably apart, eyes open. Warn that you will pull the shoulders backward and they may take steps. Stand behind, ready to catch. After a gentle demonstration pull, deliver one brisk pull. 0–2 steps = recovers (stage ≤2 if otherwise bilateral); ≥3 steps but recovers unassisted = modified 2.5; would fall if not caught = stage 3. Stage 1.5 = unilateral plus axial (neck/trunk) involvement. Optional option.description repeating the step-count rule on 2 / 2.5 / 3.
findings.research: Hoehn MM, Yahr MD. Neurology 1967; modified H&Y; MDS-UPDRS postural-instability pull-test method
findings.do_not_change: stage values 0 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 / 3 / 4 / 5, calculate() bands

findings.name: HEART Score for Major Cardiac Events
findings.current: History is only Slightly / Moderately / Highly suspicious. ECG is Normal / Non-specific repolarization disturbance / Significant ST deviation. Risk-factor helpText lists HTN, HLD, DM, obesity, smoking, positive family history without BMI or FHx age.
findings.problem: History has no typical vs nonspecific elements, so 0 vs 1 vs 2 is gestalt and needs a HEART card. ECG 1-point officially includes LBBB, paced rhythm, LVH strain, and digoxin effect — not named. Significant ST deviation has no mm criterion. Obesity and family history have published cutoffs (BMI >30; parent/sibling CVD before 65) that are hidden.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/2 values. option.description on history: 0 nonspecific features predominate (pleuritic, positional, well-localized sharp, reproducible); 1 mix of typical and nonspecific; 2 mostly typical ACS (retrosternal pressure, exertion, radiation to arm/jaw, diaphoresis, nausea, NTG relief). ECG: 0 normal; 1 LBBB, RV paced, LVH with strain, digoxin, or nonspecific ST-T without significant ST deviation; 2 significant ST depression or elevation (typically ≥1 mm). Expand risk helpText: HTN; hypercholesterolemia; DM; obesity (BMI >30); current or recent smoking; FHx = parent or sibling with CVD before age 65. Known CAD / MI / PCI-CABG / CVA / PAD = 2 points even if <3 risk factors.
findings.research: Six AJ et al. Neth Heart J 2008; Backus HEART flyer (heartscore.nl) risk-factor list (BMI >30, FHx); original ECG categories including LBBB/PM
findings.do_not_change: 0–2 per domain, 0–10 total, MACE bands 0–3 / 4–6 / 7–10, troponin ×ULN bins

findings.name: Wells Criteria for DVT
findings.current: Calf swelling ≥3 cm vs asymptomatic leg with no measurement site. Active cancer has no time/palliative rule. Localized tenderness along deep venous system does not say which veins. Recently bedridden ≥3 days or major surgery within 12 weeks omits anesthesia.
findings.problem: The calf item is a tape-measure exam: official rule is ≥3 cm difference 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity. Active cancer in Wells is treatment ongoing, within 6 months, or palliative. Tenderness is along femoral/popliteal/posterior tibial distribution. Major surgery is surgery requiring general or regional anesthesia.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on calf: Measure both calves 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity; Yes if symptomatic side is ≥3 cm larger. If both legs symptomatic, use the more symptomatic side. cancer: Treatment ongoing, treated in the past 6 months, or palliative. tenderness: Palpate along the deep veins (femoral canal groin-to-mid-thigh, popliteal fossa, posterior calf) — not superficial or varicose-vein pain. bedridden: Bedridden ≥3 days, or major surgery within 12 weeks requiring general or regional anesthesia. Boolean fields: use helpText (option.description is not rendered on yesNo).
findings.research: Wells PS et al. Lancet 1997; NEJM 2003 revised Wells DVT model (12-week anesthesia wording; 10 cm landmark)
findings.do_not_change: +1 items, −2 alternative diagnosis, two-tier ≤0 vs ≥1 logic

findings.name: HIT-6 Headache Impact Test
findings.current: Item 2 is 'How often do headaches limit your usual daily activities?' Official HIT-6 specifies household work, work, school, or social activities. Likert labels and items 1/3–6 are otherwise close. HIT-6 is QualityMetric-copyrighted and is reprinted here.
findings.problem: Dropping the activity list changes what patients count as limited. If the license does not allow reprint, these stems should not be on the form at all (total-only + pointer), analogous to MMSE/MoCA.
findings.suggested_change: If license allows, restore official item-2 stem: How often do headaches limit your ability to do usual daily activities including household work, work, school, or social activities? Optional helpText: items 1–3 are about headaches in general; 4–6 are the past 4 weeks. If license does not allow reprint, convert to numberInput total 36–78 with helpText pointing to the official QualityMetric HIT-6.
findings.research: Kosinski M et al. Qual Life Res 2003; HIT-6™ © QualityMetric / GSK; ePROVIDE HIT-6 page
findings.do_not_change: Likert values 6/8/10/11/13, 36–78 range, impact bands ≤49 / 50–55 / 56–59 / ≥60

findings.name: MIDAS Migraine Disability Assessment
findings.current: Day-count labels are shortened. Only Q1 says '(3 mo)'. Q3 is 'Days no household work due to headache' without examples. Q2/Q4 mention exclude-Q1/Q3 but not the 3-month window again.
findings.problem: Official MIDAS is five questions over the last 3 months. Omitting the window on Q2–Q5 invites 1-month or usual-month×3 guesses. Household work officially includes housework, home repairs, shopping, and caring for children/relatives.
findings.suggested_change: Expand labels to official 3-month stems. Q1: On how many days in the last 3 months did you miss work or school because of headaches? Q2: …was productivity at work/school reduced by half or more? (Do not count Q1 missed days.) Q3: …did you not do household work (housework, repairs, shopping, caring for children/relatives)? Q4: household productivity ≤50%, exclude Q3 days. Q5: missed family/social/leisure days in the last 3 months. Optional pain helpText: 0 = no pain, 10 = worst possible (item B is not in the sum).
findings.research: Stewart WF / Lipton RB MIDAS questionnaire (Cephalalgia 1999; Neurology 2001). Generally free for clinical use.
findings.do_not_change: sum of Q1–Q5 only, Grade I–IV cutoffs, items A/B excluded from the sum

findings.name: ICHD Migraine Without Aura Helper
findings.current: C1–C4 and D1–D2 are bare yes/no. C4 is aggravation by routine physical activity with no example. D2 is Photophobia and phonophobia. No on-form note that C needs ≥2/4 and D needs ≥1/2 (only in the result).
findings.problem: Hidden C/D sub-cutoffs mean users may think every C feature is required. D2 is AND (both light and sound), not either. ICHD C4 operationalizes routine physical activity as walking or climbing stairs.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on first C item: Criterion C is met if ≥2 of these 4 features are Yes. helpText on aggravation: e.g. walking or climbing stairs, or avoidance of that activity. helpText on photoPhono: Requires BOTH photophobia AND phonophobia during the headache (not either alone). helpText on D group: Criterion D is met if nausea/vomiting OR (photophobia AND phonophobia).
findings.research: ICHD-3 (Cephalalgia 2018) 1.1 Migraine without aura criteria A–E
findings.do_not_change: C≥2 and D≥1 logic, A ≥5 attacks, B 4–72 h, E not-other-diagnosis

findings.name: EDSS (Simplified Select)
findings.current: Steps 1.0–3.5 use minimal/mild/moderate disability in one/several FS with FS never defined. Steps ≥4 have walking-distance anchors.
findings.problem: Formal EDSS 0–3.5 is Neurostatus Functional Systems (pyramidal, cerebellar, brainstem, sensory, bowel/bladder, visual, cerebral), not a gestalt mild disability. A user cannot assign 2.0 vs 3.0 from the UI without the FS card. Ambulation steps are scorable as labeled.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: 0–3.5 require Kurtzke/Neurostatus Functional Systems scores (not just a global mild/moderate word). ≥4 are gait-distance ± aid as labeled (500 / 300 / 200 / 100 m; 6.0 unilateral aid 100 m; 6.5 bilateral aid 20 m; ≥7 wheelchair). This selector is for an already-known EDSS or rough ambulation stage — not a substitute for Neurostatus training.
findings.research: Kurtzke JF. Neurology 1983 EDSS; Neurostatus EDSS training materials
findings.do_not_change: step values 0–10 including half-steps, interpretation bands

findings.name: DN4 Neuropathic Pain Score
findings.current: Interview items 1–3 are pain characteristics. 4–7 are Tingling / Pins and needles / Numbness / Itching without 'same area.' Exam: Hypoesthesia to touch/pinprick in pain area; Brushing elicits or increases pain (allodynia) with no method.
findings.problem: Official interview Q2 is associated symptoms in the same area as the pain. Exam is cotton/soft-brush touch vs control; pinprick vs control; light moving brush (not pressure) for allodynia. Pressing the skin false-positives item 10.
findings.suggested_change: Prefix q4–q7 labels with 'In the same area as the pain:'. helpText on q8: Light touch with cotton or a soft brush on the painful area vs a contralateral/control area; Yes = decreased sensation. q9: Pinprick (or von Frey) vs control area; Yes = decreased prick sensation. q10: Light moving brush or fingertip — not pressure — over the painful area; Yes if that causes or increases pain. Use helpText (yesNo does not render option.description).
findings.research: Bouhassira D et al. Pain 2005 DN4; HAS/French DN4 form (interview vs examination blocks)
findings.do_not_change: 10 binary items, cutoff ≥4, 7+3 interview/exam split

findings.name: AUDIT (Full 10-Item)
findings.current: Q4 includes '(past year)'; Q5–Q8 do not. Q2 is How many standard drinks on a typical drinking day? with no definition of a standard drink.
findings.problem: Official WHO AUDIT Q4–Q8 are during the last year. Dropping that on Q5–Q8 mixes lifetime vs 12-month reporting. Standard drink is 10 g ethanol WHO vs ~14 g US — patients under/over-count Q2–Q3 without a gloss.
findings.suggested_change: Append '(past year)' to Q5–Q8 labels to match Q4. helpText on q2 (and q3): Agree a standard drink first. WHO ≈ 10 g ethanol; US common teaching ≈ 14 g (12 oz beer, 5 oz wine, 1.5 oz spirits). Keep Q9–Q10 0/2/4 options.
findings.research: Babor TF et al. WHO AUDIT 2nd ed. 2001 (WHO-MSD-MSB-01.6a)
findings.do_not_change: 0–4 item values, Q9–Q10 0/2/4, 0–40 total, WHO zones 0–7 / 8–15 / 16–19 / ≥20

findings.name: DAST-10 Drug Abuse Screening
findings.current: Ten yes/no stems. No past 12 months. Q3 rewritten as 'Not always able to stop… (original reverse item)'. Q10 medical problems as a result of your drug use has no examples.
findings.problem: DAST-10 is a 12-month screen (alcohol excluded). Lifetime reading inflates the score. Item 10 officially exemplifies memory loss, hepatitis, convulsions, bleeding. Item 3 rewrite is directionally correct but still easy to double-reverse.
findings.suggested_change: q1 helpText: Past 12 months. Do not count alcohol (use AUDIT). Include nonmedical use of prescription drugs. helpText on q3: Yes = cannot always stop when they want to (original reverse-scored item; already oriented so Yes = 1). q10 helpText: e.g. memory loss, hepatitis, jaundice, convulsions, bleeding, or other drug-related medical problems.
findings.research: Skinner HA. Addict Behav 1982 DAST; DAST-10 12-month instructions (Yudko reviews / CAMH form)
findings.do_not_change: 10 binary items, Yes=1 including item 3 as currently oriented, bands 0 / 1–2 / 3–5 / 6–8 / 9–10

findings.name: CAGE-AID Questionnaire
findings.current: Cut down / Annoyed / Guilty / Eye-opener stems without 'Have you ever.'
findings.problem: CAGE-AID is a lifetime (ever) screen. Without ever, some users score only the current week and under-detect.
findings.suggested_change: Prefix each label with Have you ever. C: Have you ever felt you should cut down on your drinking or drug use? A: Have people ever annoyed you by criticizing your drinking or drug use? G: Have you ever felt bad or guilty about your drinking or drug use? E: Have you ever used a drink or drug first thing in the morning to steady your nerves or get rid of a hangover?
findings.research: Brown RL, Rounds LA. Wis Med J 1995 CAGE-AID; Ewing JA CAGE 1984
findings.do_not_change: 4 binary items, ≥1 vs ≥2 cutoff discussion in interpretation

findings.name: ASRS-v1.1 Adult ADHD Screen (Part A)
findings.current: Six abbreviated stems; Never–Very often options. No past 6 months. Shading rule (Q1–3 positive only at Often/Very often; Q4–6 at Sometimes+) lives in calculate/details, not on the options.
findings.problem: Official ASRS-v1.1 Part A is how you have felt and conducted yourself over the past 6 months. Missing window changes screening. Stems drop How often do you / When you have a task. Marking which frequencies are screen-positive would match the official shaded form.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: Rate the past 6 months. Restore official stems (only slightly longer). Optional option.description marks: Q1–3 shaded/screen-positive on Often and Very often; Q4–6 on Sometimes, Often, Very often. Do not change 0–4 values or the shaded-count rule.
findings.research: Kessler RC et al. Psychol Med 2005; WHO/Harvard ASRS-v1.1 6-question screener PDF (6-month instruction; shaded boxes)
findings.do_not_change: shaded-positive logic (Q1–3 ≥3; Q4–6 ≥2), cutoff ≥4/6, raw 0–24 as details only

findings.name: HAS-BLED Score
findings.current: Bleeding history or predisposition with no what-counts. Other HAS-BLED items already carry cutoffs (SBP >160, Cr ≥2.26, TTR <60%, ≥8 drinks/week).
findings.problem: Predisposition is the hidden criterion (anemia, bleeding diathesis, prior major bleed). Two clinicians will disagree on remote epistaxis vs hospitalization for GI bleed. This item is 1 of 9 and drives the ≥3 high-risk flag.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on bleed: Prior major bleeding (ICH, bleed requiring hospitalization, ≥2 g/dL Hb drop, or transfusion) or a predisposition such as anemia or a known bleeding diathesis — not trivial resolved epistaxis.
findings.research: Pisters R et al. Chest 2010 HAS-BLED (B = bleeding history or predisposition)
findings.do_not_change: 9 binary points, drugs and alcohol as separate points, ≥3 high-risk threshold

findings.name: TIMI Risk Score (STEMI)
findings.current: Killip II–IV with no class findings. Time to treatment > 4 hours does not say from when to what.
findings.problem: Killip is an exam (rales/S3/JVD vs pulmonary edema vs shock). Time to treatment >4 h in TIMI STEMI is symptom onset to reperfusion (lytic or balloon), not door-to-needle or last medical contact.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on killip2: II = S3, rales <½ lung fields, or JVD; III = frank pulmonary edema; IV = cardiogenic shock (typically SBP <90 with hypoperfusion). Any of II–IV = Yes. helpText on time4: From symptom onset to reperfusion (fibrinolysis or balloon inflation) >4 hours.
findings.research: Morrow DA et al. Circulation 2000 TIMI STEMI (InTIME II); Killip & Kimball 1967
findings.do_not_change: age 2 vs 3 mutual logic, other weights, 30-day mortality table

findings.name: Wells Criteria for PE
findings.current: Clinical signs/symptoms of DVT unspecified. Immobilization ≥3 days or surgery in past 4 weeks does not say anesthesia.
findings.problem: Official Wells PE DVT item is not any leg complaint: minimum of leg swelling AND pain with palpation of the deep veins. Surgery is typically surgery under general anesthesia in the past 4 weeks.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on dvt: Yes only if clinical DVT signs: leg swelling AND pain on palpation of the deep veins (not isolated cramp or chronic edema). immob: Bed rest ≥3 days, or surgery under general anesthesia in the past 4 weeks.
findings.research: Wells PS et al. Thromb Haemost 2000 PE model
findings.do_not_change: 3 / 3 / 1.5 / 1.5 / 1.5 / 1 / 1 weights, three-tier and two-tier (≤4) interpretation

findings.name: Killip Classification
findings.current: Class I — No clinical HF / II — Mild HF (S3, rales <½ lung fields, JVD) / III — Acute pulmonary edema / IV — Cardiogenic shock.
findings.problem: Class II is well anchored. III and IV are official names without the exam: III is rales throughout / frank alveolar edema. IV is hypotension plus hypoperfusion (oliguria, cool/clammy, cyanosis), not isolated low BP.
findings.suggested_change: Keep class values 1–4. option.description: I — no rales, no S3, no JVD; II — S3 and/or rales occupying less than half the lung fields and/or JVD; III — frank pulmonary edema (rales throughout); IV — cardiogenic shock, typically SBP <90 mmHg with signs of hypoperfusion (oliguria, cyanosis, sweating, cool extremities).
findings.research: Killip T, Kimball JT. Am J Cardiol 1967
findings.do_not_change: class 1–4 mapping, interpretation text bands

findings.name: Revised Geneva Score (PE)
findings.current: Surgery or fracture within 1 month; Active malignancy; Pain on lower limb deep venous palpation and unilateral edema. HR bands are clear.
findings.problem: Official surgery/fracture is surgery under general anesthesia or lower-limb fracture within 1 month — not any fracture. Active malignancy is solid/hematologic tumor currently active or considered cured <1 year. Isolated pain without edema should not score the palpation item.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on surgery: Surgery under general anesthesia or fracture of the lower limbs within 1 month (not an upper-extremity fracture alone). cancer: Solid or hematologic malignancy currently active or considered cured for <1 year. painPalp: Yes only if BOTH pain on deep-vein palpation AND unilateral edema.
findings.research: Le Gal G et al. Ann Intern Med 2006 revised Geneva score
findings.do_not_change: item weights (age 1, prior VTE 3, HR 0/3/5, palpation+edema 4, etc.), 0–3 / 4–10 / ≥11 bands

findings.name: PESI (Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index)
findings.current: Altered mental status (60 points) with no definition. O2 sat < 90% does not say on room air vs supplemental.
findings.problem: AMS is the largest single PESI add-on. Official definition is disorientation, lethargy, stupor, or coma — not anxiety. Oxygen is <90% with or without supplemental O2. Mis-scoring AMS moves Class I–II outpatient candidates to Class IV–V.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on ams: Disorientation, lethargy, stupor, or coma (not isolated anxiety or opioid drowsiness you judge unrelated). o2: SpO2 <90% on pulse oximetry, with or without supplemental oxygen.
findings.research: Aujesky D et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2005 PESI derivation (AMS and hypoxemia definitions)
findings.do_not_change: age + sex 10 + item weights, class I–V cut points (≤65 / 66–85 / 86–105 / 106–125 / >125)

findings.name: CLIF-SOFA / CLIF-OF (Simplified Sum)
findings.current: Brain options are HE 0 / HE I–II / HE III–IV with West Haven named but no grade findings. Resp label mentions PaO2/FiO2 or SpO2/FiO2; options list only PaO2/FiO2 >300 / 200–300 / <200 or ventilated.
findings.problem: Cannot assign West Haven grade from the UI (exam findings missing). SpO2/FiO2 CLIF-C OF equivalents are unnamed when no ABG.
findings.suggested_change: option.description on brain with West Haven: 0 none; I trivial unawareness/euphoria/short attention/impaired addition; II lethargy, time disorientation, personality change, asterixis; III somnolence/semistupor, responsive to voice, gross disorientation; IV coma. helpText on resp with SpO2/FiO2 >357 (1), 215–357 (2), ≤214 (3). Do not change values 1/2/3.
findings.research: EASL-CLIF CANONIC / Jalan CLIF-C OF table; West Haven criteria (AASLD/EASL HE); Moreau 2013 Gastroenterology
findings.do_not_change: option values 1–3, failure if score ≥3, ACLF grade logic, liver/kidney/coag/circ cutoffs

findings.name: PNED Score (UGIB Mortality, Simplified)
findings.current: ASA 1–2/3/4 unlabeled; hemodynamic instability, altered mental status, renal failure (Cr >1.5 or known CKD severe), rebleeding, failed endoscopic treatment have no operational anchors.
findings.problem: ASA class meaning, instability, mental status, 'severe CKD', and Marmo rebleed definition are not on screen.
findings.suggested_change: ASA labels: I healthy; II mild systemic disease; III severe systemic disease; IV constant threat to life. helpText instability: SBP <90 / MAP <65 / pressors (RESEARCH educational intent). mental: not oriented or GCS <14. renal: keep Cr >1.5; RESEARCH dialysis or eGFR <30 instead of 'CKD severe'. rebleed: recurrent hematemesis/melena after hemostasis and ≥24 h stability with shock or Hb drop ≥2 g/dL. failedEndo: persistent bleeding despite index endoscopic therapy.
findings.research: Marmo R et al. Am J Gastroenterol 2010 PNED; ASA Physical Status classification
findings.do_not_change: point weights, calculate() sum, educational-simplification scope (do not add missing original items such as age ≥80)

findings.name: Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS)
findings.current: Migration of pain (no origin/destination). Cough/percussion/hopping tenderness names maneuvers but not method. Anorexia unlabeled for children.
findings.problem: Migration is meant periumbilical/epigastric → RLQ. Hop item is 2 points and needs a one-line how-to. Pediatric anorexia is often refuses favorite food.
findings.suggested_change: Label migration: 'Migration of pain to RLQ (starts periumbilical/epigastric, then moves to RLQ)'. helpText coughHop: pain in RLQ on cough, hop on right foot, or percussion. Optional anorexia helpText: refuses favorite foods / not eating.
findings.research: Samuel M. J Pediatr Surg 2002; MDCalc PAS stems
findings.do_not_change: 1 vs 2 point weights, 0–10 total, fever/WBC/neutrophil cutoffs

findings.name: Tokyo Guidelines Cholangitis Severity
findings.current: Renal = oliguria or Cr >2.0 without oliguria volume/time. Neuro = disturbance of consciousness with no exam gloss. Hypoalbuminemia <0.7× LLN with no example.
findings.problem: Oliguria is a hidden numeric criterion. Consciousness item is official TG18 wording but untestable without a gloss. Albumin needs a worked LLN example.
findings.suggested_change: helpText renal: oliguria ≈ <0.5 mL/kg/h or Cr >2.0 mg/dL. neuro: new disturbance of consciousness (somnolence, disorientation, unresponsiveness). albuminLow: e.g. if LLN 3.5 g/dL then albumin <2.45 g/dL.
findings.research: Kiriyama S et al. Tokyo Guidelines 2018 cholangitis severity
findings.do_not_change: Grade III = any organ dysfunction, Grade II = ≥2 moderate predictors, CV dopamine ≥5 / any NE, WBC/fever/age/bili cutoffs

findings.name: Tokyo Guidelines Cholecystitis Severity
findings.current: CV = hypotension requiring pressors (no dose). Renal = oliguria or Cr >2.0. Cholangitis twin already specifies dopamine ≥5 or any NE.
findings.problem: TG18 Grade III CV failure is dopamine ≥5 µg/kg/min or any norepinephrine, not any pressor. Oliguria has no cutoff.
findings.suggested_change: Align CV label with cholangitis calculator: hypotension requiring dopamine ≥5 µg/kg/min or any norepinephrine. Renal helpText: oliguria ≈ <0.5 mL/kg/h or Cr >2.0 mg/dL.
findings.research: Yokoe M et al. Tokyo Guidelines 2018 cholecystitis severity
findings.do_not_change: Grade III = any organ dysfunction; Grade II = any of WBC >18k / palpable mass / >72 h / marked local inflammation; marked-local list

findings.name: Determinant-Based Pancreatitis Severity
findings.current: Organ failure = none / transient <48 h / persistent >48 h with 'modified Marshall ≥2' named but no table. Necrosis = none / sterile / infected with no infection rule.
findings.problem: Cannot decide Marshall ≥2 without PaO2/FiO2, Cr, and SBP/fluid-responsiveness cutoffs. Infected necrosis is gas on imaging or positive FNA/drain culture.
findings.suggested_change: helpText organFailure: failure = modified Marshall ≥2: resp PaO2/FiO2 ≤300; renal Cr ≥1.9 mg/dL (≥170 µmol/L); CV SBP <90 not fluid-responsive. Transient resolves within 48 h; persistent lasts >48 h. helpText necrosis: infected if gas in necrosis on CT/MRI or positive Gram stain/culture from FNA or drain.
findings.research: Dellinger EP et al. Ann Surg 2012; Banks PA et al. Gut 2013 revised Atlanta modified Marshall table
findings.do_not_change: mild/moderate/severe/critical mapping, 48-hour split, calculate() branches

findings.name: GerdQ Questionnaire
findings.current: Short labels (Heartburn / Regurgitation / Epigastric pain / Nausea / Sleep disturbance / OTC meds). Frequency bins 0 / 1 / 2–3 / 4–7 days are correct.
findings.problem: Published GerdQ uses specific 7-day patient stems; abbreviated labels especially blur epigastric vs heartburn and OTC vs prescribed PPI.
findings.suggested_change: If license allows, put official stems in label/helpText. If copyrighted, do not reprint; helpText: ask official GerdQ 7-day items (Jones 2009); this screen is score entry only. RESEARCH stems: burning behind breastbone; stomach contents to throat/mouth; pain in centre of upper stomach; nausea; sleep difficulty from heartburn/regurg; additional meds other than physician-prescribed. Keep reverse scoring on epigastric/nausea.
findings.research: Jones R et al. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2009 GerdQ; confirm AstraZeneca/instrument copyright before reprinting
findings.do_not_change: 0–3 and reverse 3–0 values, 7-day window, ≥8 cutoff, impact = sleep+OTC

findings.name: KDIGO AKI Staging
findings.current: Stage 1 Cr: ↑Cr ≥0.3 mg/dL in 48h or 1.5–1.9× baseline. No 7-day window on fold-change. UOP hours given without stating mL/kg/h needs measured weight.
findings.problem: KDIGO 1.5×/2×/3× is within 7 days (known or presumed). Omitting 7 days mis-applies old baselines. UOP is weight-based.
findings.suggested_change: Stage 1 Cr label: ↑Cr ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h or 1.5–1.9× baseline within 7 days. Stages 2–3: × baseline within 7 days. helpText uopStage: use mL/kg/h from hourly UOP and current weight. Optional Stage 3: or eGFR <35 if age <18.
findings.research: KDIGO 2012 AKI Clinical Practice Guideline
findings.do_not_change: max(Cr, UOP) staging, values 0–3, UOP hour cutoffs 6–12 / ≥12 / 24 h / anuria ≥12 h

findings.name: ISTH Overt DIC Score
findings.current: Fibrin: No increase (0) / Moderate (2) / Strong (3) with only 'use lab-specific cutoffs'. PT: <3 / 3–6 / >6 seconds prolonged without vs-what.
findings.problem: Cannot choose moderate vs strong fibrin markers without a multiplier or example D-dimer. PT is seconds above mean normal, not INR.
findings.suggested_change: option.description on fibrin: no increase = within reference; moderate ≈ >3× ULN (or ~0.4–4 µg/mL FEU in older cohorts); strong ≈ >7× ULN (or >4 µg/mL FEU); note lab ULN. helpText pt: seconds above laboratory mean normal PT (not INR). Optional fibrinogen helpText: 1.0 g/L = 100 mg/dL.
findings.research: Taylor FB et al. Thromb Haemost 2001; Toh/Hoots ISTH SSC 2007 overview; ISTH SSC 2025 D-dimer ×3 / ×7 ULN proposal
findings.do_not_change: fibrin points 0/2/3 (not 0/1/2), platelet/PT/fibrinogen cutoffs, ≥5 overt threshold

findings.name: MASCC Risk Index (Febrile Neutropenia)
findings.current: No or mild symptoms (5) / Moderate symptoms (3) / Severe symptoms / moribund (0) with no operational definition.
findings.problem: Burden of illness is the largest point swing and is global appearance of this febrile episode, not cancer extent; mild/moderate/severe is unspecified.
findings.suggested_change: option.description: no/mild = looks well aside from fever/chills, self-caring; moderate = significant symptoms but not critically ill; severe/moribund = appears severely ill or dying. helpText: clinician global assessment of this febrile illness, not underlying cancer. Instability overrides a high MASCC.
findings.research: Klastersky J et al. J Clin Oncol 2000 MASCC risk index
findings.do_not_change: 5/3/0 burden points, other item weights, ≥21 low-risk cutoff, inverted No-hypotension/No-COPD scoring

findings.name: Rochester Criteria (Febrile Infant)
findings.current: Previously healthy term infant (no antibiotics, no underlying disease, not prolonged neonatal stay) — prolonged stay undefined; perinatal antibiotics, hyperbilirubinemia, hospitalized longer than mother omitted. Age/fever eligibility not on the form.
findings.problem: Rochester previously-healthy is a checklist, not a single vague phrase. Age ≤60 days and T ≥38°C are eligibility.
findings.suggested_change: helpText previouslyHealthy: term ≥37 wks; no perinatal or current antibiotics; not hospitalized longer than the mother; no unexplained hyperbilirubinemia; no underlying illness. First-input or calculator helpText: historically well-appearing febrile infants ≤60 days with T ≥38°C; not a substitute for AAP 2021/PECARN. Optional well helpText: nontoxic = alert, well-perfused, age-appropriate interaction.
findings.research: Dagan R et al. J Pediatr 1985 Rochester criteria; AAP 2021 febrile infant guideline for the historical-tool caveat
findings.do_not_change: 7-item all-true logic, WBC 5–15k, ABC ≤1500, UA ≤10 WBC/hpf, stool ≤5 WBC/hpf

findings.name: Pediatric Early Warning Score (PEWS, simplified)
findings.current: CV: tachycardia +20 from normal / +30 HR or bradycardia, CRT seconds. Resp: RR normal / >10 / >20 above normal / ≥5 below normal and FiO2 ~30/40/50%. No age-normal HR/RR. Behavior Sleeping (1) vs Playing (0) with no sleep-vs-well cue.
findings.problem: Cannot apply +20/+30 from normal or RR vs normal without age-band vital tables. CRT method unstated. Sleeping=1 is a Monaghan rule people will skip.
findings.suggested_change: helpText cv/resp with compact age-normal HR/RR (Monaghan/Brighton-style): HR neonate 110–160, infant 100–160, 1–3y 90–150, 4–6y 80–140, 7–12y 70–120, ≥13y 60–100; RR neonate 30–60, infant 30–50, toddler 25–35, preschool 20–30, school-age 18–25, adolescent 12–20. CRT: press 5 s on sternum or finger. behavior helpText: sleeping scores 1 even if otherwise well; 3 = lethargic/confused or reduced pain response.
findings.research: Monaghan A. Paediatr Nurs 2005 Brighton PEWS; institutional Brighton age-band vital tables (do not invent a new PEWS)
findings.do_not_change: 0–3 domain points, +2 oxygen item, calculate() sum, 0–2 / 3–4 / ≥5 bands

findings.name: HEMORR₂HAGES Bleeding Risk Score
findings.current: Bare yes/no: hepatic or renal disease, ethanol abuse, reduced platelet count or function including aspirin, uncontrolled hypertension, anemia, excessive fall risk, CYP2C9 if known, prior major bleed, malignancy.
findings.problem: Gage definitions are numeric/operational (anemia without Hb is the contract example). Users guess Cr/AST/Hb/SBP cutoffs.
findings.suggested_change: helpText (keep points): hepatic = cirrhosis, AST or ALP ≥2× ULN, or albumin <3.6 g/dL; renal = CrCl <30. ethanol = abuse history or recent alcohol-related admission. reducedPlt = Plt <75×10⁹/L or scheduled antiplatelet/NSAID. htn = most recent SBP >160. anemia = Hct <30% or Hb <10 g/dL. falls = dementia, Parkinson, schizophrenia, or repeated-fall condition. genetic = CYP2C9*2 and/or *3 if known. rebleeding = prior hospitalization for bleeding. malignancy = recent/metastatic cancer.
findings.research: Gage BF et al. Am Heart J 2006 HEMORR2HAGES factor definitions
findings.do_not_change: 1-point items, rebleeding = 2, calculate() sum, 0–1 / 2–3 / ≥4 bands

findings.name: NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS)
findings.current: All 15 items are terse ordinals only (1b/1c both/one/neither correct; motor Drift/Some effort vs gravity; language Mild–moderate/Severe). No helpText, no option.description, no maneuvers, no UN rules.
findings.problem: Clinician cannot administer NIHSS from the UI. Must recall month+age questions (not where/president), eyes+grip commands, 10 s/90° arm and 5 s/30° leg holds, NIHSS picture/word cards, and exceptions (intubated 1b=1, aphasic 1b=2, amputation=UN not 4, ataxia 0 if paralyzed, dysarthria UN if intubated, item 11 never UN).
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0–4 and 15-item sum (max 42). Do not add a scored UN option. Add helpText + option.description per item. 1a loc helpText: must pick a score if ET tube/language barrier/bandages; 3 only if no movement other than reflex posturing to noxious stimulation. Descriptions: 0 Alert keenly responsive; 1 arousable by minor stimulation to obey/answer/respond; 2 repeated or strong/painful stimulation for non-stereotyped movement; 3 reflex only or flaccid areflexic. 1b locQ helpText: ask month and age; grade first answer only; intubated/severe dysarthria/language barrier → 1; aphasic/stuporous no comprehension → 2. 1c locC helpText: open and close eyes, then grip and release the non-paretic hand; substitute another one-step command if hand unusable; credit unequivocal attempt limited by weakness. 2 gaze helpText: voluntary or oculocephalic, not calorics. 1 Partial gaze palsy not forced deviation; 2 forced deviation or total paresis not overcome by oculocephalic. 3 visual helpText: confrontation upper+lower quadrants; remaining eye if unilateral blindness; any-cause blindness → 3. 4 facial helpText: show teeth or raise eyebrows and close eyes; grimace to pain if stuporous. 1 flattened nasolabial fold/asymmetric smile; 2 near-total lower-face paralysis; 3 absent upper and lower face movement. 5a/5b arm helpText: palms down 90° sitting or 45° supine × 10 s, non-paretic first; drift = falls before 10 s but does not hit bed; amputation/shoulder fusion = UN off-form (do not enter 0 or 4). 6a/6b leg: 30° × 5 s; hip fusion/amputation = UN. 7 ataxia helpText: FNF + heel-shin; score only if out of proportion to weakness; paralyzed or does not understand → 0; amputation = UN. 8 sensory helpText: pinprick (noxious if impaired consciousness); face+arm+leg; 1 aware of touch but dull; 2 unaware of touch. 9 language helpText: cookie-theft picture, naming card, sentence reading; 1a=3 → language 3. 10 dysarthria helpText: repeat Mama, tip-top, fifty-fifty, thanks, huckleberry, baseball player, hula hoop; intubated = UN off-form. 11 extinction helpText: visual+tactile DSS; never UN; aphasia attending both sides → 0. Descriptions: 1 inattention in one modality; 2 profound in more than one modality or does not recognize own hand.
findings.research: NINDS NIH Stroke Scale English instructions (NIH-Stroke-Scale_updatedFeb2024_508.pdf); Brott T et al. Stroke 1989 PMID 2749846; MDCalc NIHSS item help
findings.do_not_change: option values, calculate() 15-item sum, max 42

findings.name: CIWA-Ar (Alcohol Withdrawal)
findings.current: Ten selects with options literally "0"…"7" (orientation "0"…"4"). No prompts, observation instructions, or anchors.
findings.problem: Cannot score without Sullivan 1989 or a pocket card. Official 0/1/4/7 (and all orientation ranks) have mandatory operational anchors and several items have required questions. Intermediates 2/3/5/6 are blank in the official key (interpolation) and can stay unlabeled.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0–7 / orientation 0–4 and 10-item sum (max 67). Add helpText (prompt + observe) and option.description with Sullivan wording. Nausea helpText: Ask 'Do you feel sick to your stomach? Have you vomited?' 0 no nausea and no vomiting; 1 mild nausea no vomiting; 4 intermittent nausea with dry heaves; 7 constant nausea, frequent dry heaves and vomiting. Tremor helpText: arms extended fingers spread. 0 no tremor; 1 not visible but felt fingertip to fingertip; 4 moderate with arms extended; 7 severe even with arms not extended. Sweats: 0 no sweat visible; 1 barely perceptible, palms moist; 4 beads of sweat on forehead; 7 drenching sweats. Anxiety helpText: Ask 'Do you feel nervous?' 0 at ease; 1 mildly anxious; 4 moderately anxious or guarded so anxiety inferred; 7 acute panic as in severe delirium. Agitation: 0 normal activity; 1 somewhat more than normal; 4 moderately fidgety and restless; 7 paces during most of interview or constantly thrashes. Tactile helpText: Ask itching/pins and needles/burning/numbness/bugs crawling. 0 none; 1–3 very mild/mild/moderate itching or paresthesia; 4–6 moderately severe/severe/extremely severe hallucinations; 7 continuous hallucinations. Auditory helpText: Ask about harsh/frightening sounds or hearing things not there. 0 not present; 1–3 harshness/ability to frighten; 4–7 hallucinations as tactile. Visual helpText: Ask if light too bright/color different/hurt eyes/seeing things not there. 0 not present; 1–3 sensitivity; 4–7 hallucinations. Headache helpText: Ask 'Does your head feel different? Band around your head?' Do not rate dizziness. 0 not present through 7 extremely severe. Orientation helpText: Ask 'What day is this? Where are you? Who am I?' 0 oriented and can do serial additions; 1 cannot do serial additions or uncertain about date; 2 disoriented for date by ≤2 calendar days; 3 disoriented for date by >2 calendar days; 4 disoriented for place and/or person.
findings.research: Sullivan JT et al. Br J Addict 1989 PMID 2597811 (CIWA-Ar Appendix A); MDCalc CIWA-Ar
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–7 (orientation 0–4), calculate() sum, max 67

findings.name: ARVC Task Force Criteria (Simplified Count)
findings.current: Each of six domains is None / Minor / Major with no measurements, ECG patterns, PVC counts, or family-history rules.
findings.problem: User cannot decide minor vs major without the 2010 revised TFC worksheet (echo/CMR cutoffs, epsilon vs TAD, VT axis, >500 PVCs/24 h, which relative counts). Same protocol-card failure as NIHSS.
findings.suggested_change: Keep None=0 / Minor=1 / Major=2 and combination logic. helpText: one major OR minor per category; do not double-count. option.description abbreviated 2010 TFC: Imaging major = RV akinesia/dyskinesia/aneurysm PLUS echo PLAX RVOT ≥32 mm (≥19 mm/m²) or PSAX ≥36 mm (≥21) or FAC ≤33%, OR CMR + RVEDV ≥110/100 mL/m² or RVEF ≤40%. Imaging minor = same wall motion with milder cutoffs (PLAX ≥29, PSAX ≥32, FAC ≤40%, RVEDV ≥100/90, RVEF ≤45%). Tissue major = residual myocytes <60% with fibrous replacement of RV free wall. Repolarization major = inverted T V1–V3 or beyond, age >14, no complete RBBB. Depolarization major = epsilon wave V1–V3; minor = SAECG late potentials or TAD ≥55 ms. Arrhythmia major = NSVT/VT LBBB superior axis; minor = RVOT VT (LBBB inferior axis) or >500 PVCs/24 h. Family major = first-degree meeting TFC, autopsy-confirmed, or pathogenic mutation; minor = unconfirmed first-degree, SCD <35 suspected ARVC, or second-degree confirmed.
findings.research: Marcus FI et al. Eur Heart J 2010 PMID 20172912 (2010 revised Task Force Criteria tables)
findings.do_not_change: option values 0/1/2, definite/borderline/possible combination rules

findings.name: EHRA AF Symptom Score
findings.current: IIa Mild (normal daily activity not affected); IIb Moderate (normal daily activity affected); III Severe (normal daily activity discontinued).
findings.problem: Official modified EHRA (ESC) distinguishes IIa vs IIb by whether the patient is troubled while daily activity is still not affected. 'Daily activity affected' is class III; 'discontinued' is class IV. Current labels cause misclassification vs ESC mEHRA.
findings.suggested_change: Relabel to ESC mEHRA; keep values 1–5. I None: no AF-related symptoms. IIa Mild: normal daily activity not affected. IIb Moderate: normal daily activity not affected, but patient troubled by symptoms. III Severe: normal daily activity affected. IV Disabling: normal daily activity discontinued. helpText: score AF-related symptoms (palpitations, dyspnea, fatigue, chest discomfort, dizziness), not stroke risk.
findings.research: 2020 ESC AF Guidelines Hindricks G et al. Eur Heart J 2021 PMID 32860505, modified EHRA table
findings.do_not_change: option values 1–5, calculate() class mapping

findings.name: Child-Pugh Score
findings.current: Ascites None / Mild / Moderate–severe. Encephalopathy None / Grade 1–2 / Grade 3–4. Labs have numeric bands.
findings.problem: Ascites mild vs moderate–severe has no operational definition (diuretic-controlled vs tense/refractory). Encephalopathy assumes unstated West Haven grades, so 1–2 vs 3–4 cannot be assigned from the UI.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1/2/3. Ascites descriptions: 1 none; 2 slight / medically controlled with diuretics; 3 moderate–severe / poorly controlled or tense despite diuretics. Encephalopathy: 1 none; 2 West Haven 1–2 (shortened attention, sleep reversal, lethargy/apathy, asterixis, still arousable); 3 West Haven 3–4 (somnolence/semistupor, gross disorientation, or coma). Optional bili helpText: 2 mg/dL ≈ 34 µmol/L, 3 mg/dL ≈ 51 µmol/L.
findings.research: Pugh 1973 modification of Child-Turcotte; West Haven HE criteria (Ferenci / AASLD-EASL HE guidance)
findings.do_not_change: option values 1–3, 5-item sum, class cutoffs A 5–6 / B 7–9 / C 10–15

findings.name: Glasgow-Blatchford Score (GBS)
findings.current: Hepatic disease and Cardiac failure are bare yes/no. Hb options: Male ≥13 / Female ≥12 (0); Male 12–12.9 / Female 10–11.9 (1); Male 10–11.9 (3); <10 either sex (6).
findings.problem: Original GBS defines hepatic disease and cardiac failure as known history or clinical/lab (or radiographic) evidence. A woman with Hb 10–11.9 belongs in the 1-point band but can easily be scored 3 from the 'Male 10–11.9' option.
findings.suggested_change: liver helpText: known history or clinical/laboratory evidence of chronic or acute liver disease (Blatchford 2000). heart helpText: known history or clinical/radiographic evidence of heart failure. Relabel Hb so sex is unambiguous, e.g. 'Female 10–11.9 or male 12–12.9 (1)' and 'Male 10–11.9 only (3); females in this Hb range use the 1-point option unless Hb <10'.
findings.research: Blatchford O et al. Lancet 2000 PMID 11073021
findings.do_not_change: point values 0/1/2/3/4/6, yes/no points, GBS 0–1 very-low-risk band

findings.name: Rockall Score (Pre-endoscopy)
findings.current: Comorbidity None (0) / Heart failure, IHD, other major (2) / Renal/liver failure or metastatic cancer (3). Age and shock already have HR/SBP anchors.
findings.problem: 'Other major' is undefined, so users may under- or over-score vs the original audit (any major comorbidity comparable to HF/IHD = 2; only renal failure, liver failure, or disseminated malignancy = 3).
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0/2/3. option.description: 0 no major comorbidity; 2 cardiac failure, IHD, or any other major comorbidity of similar severity (e.g. COPD on home O2, CVA with residual deficit); 3 renal failure, liver failure, or disseminated malignancy.
findings.research: Rockall TA et al. Gut 1996 PMID 8675081
findings.do_not_change: option values 0/1/2/3, pre-endoscopy 3-item sum

findings.name: BISAP Score
findings.current: Impaired mental status and SIRS (≥2 criteria) as bare yes/no. BUN >25, age >60, pleural effusion are clear.
findings.problem: Cannot score SIRS without the four criteria. AMS has no operational definition (GCS vs orientation).
findings.suggested_change: Keep binary 0/1. ams helpText: Yes if GCS <15, or disorientation, lethargy, or coma (Wu 2008). sirs helpText: Yes if ≥2 of temperature <36 or >38°C; HR >90; RR >20; WBC <4 or >12 ×10^9/L or >10% bands.
findings.research: Wu BU et al. Gut 2008 PMID 18519429; Bone SIRS criteria 1992
findings.do_not_change: five binary points, ≥3 high-risk cutoff

findings.name: PHQ-9 Depression Screen
findings.current: Clipped stems (Interest/pleasure little; Feeling down/hopeless; Thoughts of self-harm). Frequency options are the official 0–3 labels. No 2-week frame.
findings.problem: PHQ-9 is a 2-week instrument; several stems drop clinically important clauses (item 6 failure/family, item 8 observed psychomotor change, item 9 passive death wish). Cannot administer the official screen from these labels. Pfizer copyright but freely reproducible for clinical use with notice (unlike MMSE/MoCA).
findings.suggested_change: helpText: 'Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?' Expand labels to official PHQ-9 wording (license allows): (1) Little interest or pleasure in doing things; (2) Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless; (3) Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much; (4) Feeling tired or having little energy; (5) Poor appetite or overeating; (6) Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down; (7) Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television; (8) Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual; (9) Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way. Pearl: PHQ-9 © Pfizer; free clinical use from phqscreeners.com — retain copyright notice.
findings.research: Kroenke K et al. J Gen Intern Med 2001 PMID 11556941; https://www.phqscreeners.com
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–3, 9-item sum 0–27, item-9 safety branch

findings.name: GAD-7 Anxiety Screen
findings.current: Short stems (Worrying too much; Restless) and no 2-week frame. Frequency options are official.
findings.problem: Cannot administer as published. Restless omits 'so restless that it is hard to sit still'; Worrying too much omits 'about different things.' GAD-7 is Pfizer-copyrighted but freely reproducible with notice.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: 'Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by the following problems?' Expand labels to official GAD-7: (1) Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge; (2) Not being able to stop or control worrying; (3) Worrying too much about different things; (4) Trouble relaxing; (5) Being so restless that it is hard to sit still; (6) Becoming easily annoyed or irritable; (7) Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen. Pearl: GAD-7 © Pfizer; free clinical use from phqscreeners.com.
findings.research: Spitzer RL et al. Arch Intern Med 2006 PMID 16717171; phqscreeners.com
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–3, 7-item sum 0–21

findings.name: CAGE Questionnaire
findings.current: Four yes/no close to CAGE mnemonics, but lifetime 'ever' is omitted and Eye-opener drops 'to steady your nerves or get rid of a hangover.'
findings.problem: CAGE is a lifetime screen. Without 'ever,' patients may answer about current drinking only. Eye-opener is incomplete vs Ewing 1984.
findings.suggested_change: Keep yes/no 0/1. Labels: C Have you ever felt you should Cut down on your drinking?; A Have people Annoyed you by criticizing your drinking?; G Have you ever felt bad or Guilty about your drinking?; E Have you ever had a drink first thing in the morning to steady your nerves or to get rid of a hangover (Eye-opener)? helpText: lifetime ('ever') questions, not limited to the past year.
findings.research: Ewing JA. JAMA 1984 PMID 6471323
findings.do_not_change: four binary points, ≥2 positive threshold

findings.name: Schwartz LQTS Diagnostic Score
findings.current: Low heart rate for age (+0.5) with no percentile or bpm rule. QTc bands, notched T in 3 leads, stress-related syncope, and TdP are adequately specified.
findings.problem: Official criterion is resting HR below the 2nd percentile for age (Schwartz 2011), not a gestalt 'low.'
findings.suggested_change: Keep +0.5. Relabel/helpText: Resting heart rate below the 2nd percentile for age (Schwartz 2011). In adults roughly <50–60 bpm depending on age tables; use a pediatric percentile chart for children.
findings.research: Schwartz PJ et al. Circulation 1993 PMID 8339437; Schwartz & Crotti 2011 score update (2nd-percentile HR)
findings.do_not_change: point weights, TdP/syncope mutual-exclusion rule, ≥3.5 / 1.5 cutoffs

findings.name: Glasgow Aneurysm Score
findings.current: Shock (hypotension / hemodynamic instability) without a BP number. Myocardial, cerebrovascular, and renal items already name diagnoses or Cr >150 µmol/L.
findings.problem: Original GAS shock is SBP <90 mmHg. 'Hemodynamic instability' invites scoring vasoplegia or relative hypotension the derivation did not count.
findings.suggested_change: Keep +17. Relabel or helpText: Shock = SBP <90 mmHg (original Samy GAS). Vasopressor need to keep SBP ≥90 may be counted as shock present.
findings.research: Samy AK et al. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg 1994 PMID 8049922
findings.do_not_change: point weights (age + 17/7/10/14), calculate() sum

findings.name: Warfarin INR Goal by Indication
findings.current: Option 'Mechanical aortic valve + TE risk factors' does not list which risk factors. calculate() later names AF, prior TE, hypercoagulable state, LV dysfunction, older-generation valve — too late for the input choice.
findings.problem: User cannot choose avr_low vs avr_high without the ACC/AHA TE-risk list on the option.
findings.suggested_change: option.description on avr_high: TE risk factors = AF, prior thromboembolism, hypercoagulable state, LV dysfunction, older-generation (caged-ball/tilting-disc) valve. Mirror on avr_low: bileaflet / current-generation mechanical AVR without those TE risk factors.
findings.research: 2020 ACC/AHA Valvular Heart Disease Guideline, Otto CM et al. Circulation 2021 PMID 33332150
findings.do_not_change: indication keys, INR numeric bounds returned by calculate()

findings.name: ACC/AHA Heart Failure Stages
findings.current: Stage A–D options already have solid descriptions. Optional NYHA is NYHA I / II / III / IV with no activity anchors.
findings.problem: Optional, but if shown it is the classic terse class scale. CCS angina in this same file already demonstrates label + description with operational findings.
findings.suggested_change: Add option.description: I no limitation of ordinary physical activity; II slight limitation, ordinary activity causes HF symptoms; III marked limitation, less than ordinary activity causes symptoms; IV symptoms at rest, any activity increases discomfort.
findings.research: NYHA functional classification; 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA HF Guideline PMID 35363499
findings.do_not_change: stage values 0–3, NYHA values 0–4 (context only)

findings.name: MASES (Enthesitis Score)
findings.current: Single number 'MASES total (tender sites)' with helpText 'Number of tender entheses out of 13 defined sites'. Result details list a partial site set ending in 'etc.'
findings.problem: Clinician cannot administer MASES from the UI. The 13 named sites and 0/1 tenderness rule are not on the input; user still needs a protocol card. This is a bedside exam, not a copyrighted questionnaire total.
findings.suggested_change: Expand helpText on total (keep 0–13 number entry): 'Press each site; score 1 if tender. 13 sites: R+L 1st costochondral, R+L 7th costochondral, R+L ASIS, R+L PSIS, R+L iliac crests, L5 spinous process, R+L Achilles insertions. Do not count other entheses (SPARCC uses different sites).'
findings.research: Heuft-Dorenbosch L et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2003 PMID 12525383; ASAS MASES site diagram; MDCalc MASES
findings.do_not_change: 0–13 range, calculate() clamp, interpretation bands

findings.name: ASDAS-CRP (Axial SpA)
findings.current: Labels cite BASDAI Q2/Q3/Q6 and 'patient global' on 0–10 scales. Only morningStiff has helpText ('0–10 scale, not raw hours'). No question wording and no past-week window.
findings.problem: Cannot administer the four patient domains without the BASDAI/ASDAS stems. Morning-stiffness 0–10 mapping to hours (10 = ≥2 h) and the past-week time frame are missing.
findings.suggested_change: Add helpText: backPain 'BASDAI Q2, past week: overall AS neck, back or hip pain. 0=none, 10=very severe.'; morningStiff 'BASDAI Q6, past week: morning stiffness duration from waking. 0=0 h, 10=2 h or more (VAS, not raw hours).'; ptGlobal 'Past week: how active was your spondyloarthritis? 0=not active, 10=very active.'; peripheral 'BASDAI Q3, past week: pain/swelling in joints other than neck, back or hips. 0=none, 10=very severe.'
findings.research: ASAS ASDAS and BASDAI official forms; Lukas C et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2009; Machado P et al. 2011 cut-offs
findings.do_not_change: formula coefficients, ln(CRP+1), CRP unit mg/L, cutoffs 1.3/2.1/3.5

findings.name: DAPSA (Psoriatic Arthritis)
findings.current: Tender joint count (68), swollen joint count (66), patient pain VAS 0–10, patient global VAS 0–10. CRP already has mg/dL helpText.
findings.problem: No 68/66 joint map (hips tender-only explains 68 vs 66). Pain vs patient-global stems and time window omitted, so the two VAS boxes are easy to swap.
