findings.current: 'High urine specific gravity / osmolality (concentrated)' and 'CK markedly elevated / pigment nephropathy context' with no numbers. FENa/UNa already have cutoffs.
findings.problem: Concentrated urine and 'markedly elevated CK' still require a card. Teaching: SG ≥1.020 or Uosm ≥500 favors pre-renal concentrating ability; rhabdomyolysis-range CK typically >5,000 IU/L.
findings.suggested_change: highSpGrav label: 'Urine SG ≥1.020 or Uosm ≥500 mOsm/kg (concentrated)'. ckRise label: 'CK markedly elevated (typically >5,000 IU/L) / pigment nephropathy'.
findings.research: Standard AKI urine-index teaching; KDIGO AKI; rhabdomyolysis/pigment nephropathy reviews
findings.do_not_change: 7 vs 5 feature counts and delta rule for favor pre-renal / ATN / mixed

findings.name: Smoke Inhalation Severity Checklist
findings.current: 'Large TBSA burns' and 'Known elevated COHb or cyanide concern' with no % or COHb number. Other features are self-explanatory.
findings.problem: 'Large' is not a burn-center number (ABA-style ≥20% TBSA adults, ≥10% children). Elevated COHb is not a smoker 5–10% baseline; many pathways flag COHb >10% plus cyanide concern in enclosed plastic/industrial fires.
findings.suggested_change: largeTbsa: 'Large TBSA burns (≥20% adults; ≥10% children) or burns plus inhalation'. highCo: 'COHb >10% (or above smoker baseline) or cyanide concern (industrial/plastic fire, unexplained lactate)'.
findings.research: ABA burn-center referral criteria; inhalation-injury reviews (soot/voice change + COHb)
findings.do_not_change: 8-item count; airway-threat logic (hoarse OR AMS OR facial+singed)

findings.name: Beta-Blocker Toxicity Checklist
findings.current: QRS widening, hypoglycemia, symptomatic bradycardia — no ms / mg/dL / HR.
findings.problem: Membrane-stabilizing BB toxicity is scored on QRS ≥120 ms. Hypoglycemia should be <70 mg/dL or symptomatic. Symptomatic bradycardia is clinical but a numeric floor (HR <50–60 with hypoperfusion) reduces disagreement.
findings.suggested_change: qrsWide label: 'QRS ≥120 ms (membrane-stabilizing agents, e.g. propranolol)'. hypoglycemia label: 'Hypoglycemia (glucose <70 mg/dL or symptomatic)'. bradycardia helpText: hypoperfusion, usually HR <50–60; atropine-refractory is the separate item.
findings.research: Graudins et al. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2016; poison-center BB/CCB guidance
findings.do_not_change: 7-feature count, agent select values, severe-pattern branching

findings.name: PECARN Cervical Spine Injury Rule
findings.current: High/intermediate stems already include GCS/AVPU splits and 'needs OR or admission'. No examples of substantial injury; no preverbal midline cue; abnormal ABC has no examples.
findings.problem: Mostly scorable. Reliability drops on abnormal ABC and substantial injuries (paper: observation or surgery — skull fracture, pneumothorax, solid-organ injury, pelvic/spine fracture) and posterior midline tenderness in a toddler.
findings.suggested_change: helpText only. abnormalAbc: observed abnormal A/B/C (advanced airway, apnea/hypopnea, shock, CPR). substantial head/torso: Leonard 2024 — injury that warrants observation or surgery (skull fx, pneumothorax, solid-organ, pelvic/spine fx). midlineTenderness: posterior midline; uncooperative preverbal exam ≠ a No.
findings.research: Leonard JC et al. Lancet Child Adolesc Health 2024; PECARN CSI infographic
findings.do_not_change: 3 high-risk + 5 intermediate yes/no; CT vs x-ray vs clear pathway

findings.name: Body Roundness Index (BRI)
findings.current: Waist circumference in cm, no landmark. Pearl mentions iliac crest vs midpoint; helpText empty.
findings.problem: WHO midpoint vs NIH iliac-crest protocols change WC by several cm and therefore BRI.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on waist: standing, end-expiration; state site (WHO midpoint last rib–iliac crest vs NIH iliac crest) and keep it consistent.
findings.research: Thomas 2013 BRI methods; WHO vs NIH waist protocols
findings.do_not_change: BRI formula and quartile-style bands

findings.name: HACOR NIV Failure Score
findings.current: Bare vitals/labs. Pearls say score after ~1 h of NIV; point tables only in evidence/details. GCS is raw 3–15.
findings.problem: Users may enter pre-NIV gases (wrong time window). HACOR is for NIV, not already-intubated patients.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on first field: use values after ~1 hour of optimized NIV (Duan 2017), not the pre-NIV gas. gcs helpText: total GCS 3–15; not for already-intubated patients.
findings.research: Duan J et al. Intensive Care Med 2017 HACOR derivation
findings.do_not_change: point tables or ≥5 failure threshold

findings.name: NUTRIC Score (ICU nutrition risk)
findings.current: hospitalDays and il6 have point-cutoff helpText; age/APACHE/SOFA/comorbidity count do not. Comorbidity inventory unnamed.
findings.problem: Inconsistent with H2FPEF in the same file. Heyland used a simple chronic-condition count (not a published Charlson list); raters diverge unless told ≥2 = 1 point.
findings.suggested_change: helpText mirroring IL-6/days: age 0 if <50, 1 if 50–74, 2 if ≥75; APACHE 0/<15, 1/15–19, 2/20–27, 3/≥28; SOFA 0/<6, 1/6–9, 2/≥10; comorbidities = distinct chronic conditions, ≥2 scores 1.
findings.research: Heyland 2011 Crit Care NUTRIC; modified NUTRIC (no IL-6) high ≥5
findings.do_not_change: point tables, IL-6 ≥400, hospital-days ≥1, risk bands

findings.name: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)
findings.current: Labels only (Spontaneous / To speech / To pain; Oriented / Confused; Localizes / Withdraws). No helpText, no option.description, no untestable path.
findings.problem: Cannot administer GCS from the UI: pain-stimulus method (fingernail-bed vs trapezius/supraorbital; localization = hand above clavicle), what oriented means, two-step motor command, intubated verbal (VT / NT — do not silently assign 1), eyes untestable from swelling (C). 2014 wording is to sound / to pressure.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1–4 / 1–5 / 1–6. Add helpText + option.description with Teasdale 2014 prompts. Do not add a new numeric VT value. Verbal 1 description: record VT if intubated. Eye 1: record C/NT if lids swollen. Motor helpText: two-part command; trapezius/supraorbital for localization; fingernail-bed for flexion vs extension; best arm.
findings.research: Teasdale & Jennett Lancet 1974; GCS 2014 relaunch (glasgowcomascale.org) stimulus method and NT/C/T coding
findings.do_not_change: option values, calculate() E+V+M sum, max 15, risk bands ≤8 / 9–12 / 13–15

findings.name: Pediatric SOFA (pSOFA) Simplified Educational
findings.current: Resp/CV/CNS/renal are Normal/mild/moderate/severe/very severe ordinals. Coag and liver already quote platelet and bilirubin bins.
findings.problem: Cannot assign 1 vs 2 vs 3 vs 4 without the Matics table. Missing PaO2/FiO2 and SpO2/FiO2 cutoffs, age-specific MAP, age-specific creatinine, GCS bands, vasoactive µg/kg/min. Adult sofa in the same app already prints those numbers.
findings.suggested_change: Expand labels (values stay 0–4). Resp: PF ≥400 or SF ≥292 (0); 300–399 / SF 264–291 (1); 200–299 / SF 221–263 (2); 100–199 + support / SF 148–220 + support (3); <100 + support / SF <148 + support (4). helpText: SF only if SpO2 ≤97%. CNS: GCS 15 / 13–14 / 10–12 / 6–9 / <6. CV and renal: helpText with Matics age-MAP and age-creatinine tables plus dopamine/dobutamine/epi/norepi µg/kg/min for scores 2–4.
findings.research: Matics TJ, Sanchez-Pinto LN. JAMA Pediatr. 2017;171(10):e172352 Table 1
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–4, six-domain sum 0–24, interpretation thresholds 3 / 7 / 11 / ≥12

findings.name: Phoenix Sepsis Criteria (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: Coag option is 'Thrombocytopenia / coagulopathy meeting Phoenix-style thresholds (1)' with no numbers. Resp/CV/neuro are mild–moderate/severe, vasoactive or significant lactate/hypotension, GCS reduction, coma.
findings.problem: UI invokes official Phoenix thresholds then withholds them (platelets, INR, D-dimer, fibrinogen, PF/SF, IMV, lactate 5 and 11, age-MAP, GCS ≤10, fixed pupils). Educational 0–2 bins are fine; empty bins are not.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0/1/2 (do not expand to official resp 0–3 / CV 0–6). helpText + option.description mapping: Resp 0 = PF ≥400 or SF ≥292; 1 = PF <400 or SF <292 on any support; 2 = IMV and PF ≤200 or SF ≤220. CV 0 = no vasoactive, lactate <5, MAP above age floor; 1 = 1 vasoactive or lactate 5–10.9 or age-hypotension; 2 = ≥2 vasoactives or lactate ≥11. MAP 0-point floors mmHg: <1 mo >30; 1–11 mo >38; 1–<2 y >43; 2–<5 y >44; 5–<12 y >48; 12–17 y >51. Coag 0 = platelets ≥100k, INR ≤1.3, D-dimer ≤2 mg/L FEU, fibrinogen ≥100; 1 = any one abnormal; 2 = ≥2 abnormal. Neuro 0 = GCS >10 and reactive pupils; 1 = GCS ≤10; 2 = bilateral fixed pupils.
findings.research: Schlapbach LJ et al. JAMA 2024 Phoenix consensus table; Sanchez-Pinto LN et al. JAMA 2024 Table 2
findings.do_not_change: 0–2 domain values, organ sum, sepsis = infection AND organ ≥2, shock = sepsis AND cv ≥1

findings.name: Biophysical Profile (BPP)
findings.current: NST is only Reactive (2) / Nonreactive (0). Movement ≥3 discrete movements without a 30-min window. AFV 'MVP >2 cm (or adequate AFI)' with no AFI number. Breathing already says ≥30 s in 30 min.
findings.problem: Cannot call reactive vs nonreactive without Manning/ACOG acceleration rules (15×15 or 10×10). Movement observation window omitted. Adequate AFI is undefined.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 2/0/−1 values. NST helpText/labels: Reactive = ≥2 accelerations in 20 min, ≥15 bpm × ≥15 s if GA ≥32 wks, ≥10 × 10 s if <32 wks; extend to 40 min before nonreactive. Movement: ≥3 discrete body/limb movements in 30 min. AFV: MVP >2 cm or AFI >5 cm vs MVP ≤2 or AFI ≤5. Optional tone: extension→flexion of limb/spine or hand open-close in 30 min.
findings.research: Manning FA et al. AJOG 1980; ACOG antenatal testing (15×15 / 10×10 NST); standard BPP MVP >2 cm tables
findings.do_not_change: 0/2 component points, NST −1 skip, /10 vs /8 logic, oligohydramnios override

findings.name: Neonatal Late-Onset Sepsis Clinical Checklist
findings.current: Yes/No: temperature instability (hypo/hyperthermia); poor perfusion / prolonged CRT / hypotension; new glucose instability; very/extremely preterm or VLBW; recent broad antibiotics. Other signs (apnea, feeding intolerance) are already concrete.
findings.problem: Hidden cutoffs: hypo/hyperthermia °C, CRT seconds, glucose mg/dL, VPT/EPT/VLBW definitions, what recent means.
findings.suggested_change: helpText only. tempInstab: core <36.5°C or ≥38.0°C or repeated environmental adjustment. perfusion: CRT >3 s; hypotension per GA mean-BP tables. glucose: new hypo/hyperglycemia requiring treatment (many NICUs <45–50 mg/dL). prematurity: <32 wks VPT, <28 EPT, VLBW <1500 g, ELBW <1000 g. priorAbx: e.g. systemic broad-spectrum in past 7–14 days or known resistant colonization.
findings.research: Shane AL et al. Lancet 2017 LOS review; WHO/AAP preterm and VLBW definitions
findings.do_not_change: yes/no keys, weights (perfusion/neuro/apneaBrady = 2), threshold bands

findings.name: qSOFA Score
findings.current: Altered mentation with no operational definition. RR ≥22 and SBP ≤100 already explicit.
findings.problem: Sepsis-3 qSOFA mentation is GCS <15 (any drop from 15), not free-form altered.
findings.suggested_change: Label to 'Altered mentation (GCS <15)' and/or helpText: any GCS <15 or new disorientation/confusion; if baseline dementia score only acute change.
findings.research: Singer M et al. JAMA 2016 Sepsis-3 qSOFA bedside criteria
findings.do_not_change: three binary points, positive ≥2

findings.name: SOFA Score
findings.current: CV: Dopamine ≤5 or dobutamine (2) with no units. Renal: UOP <500 / <200 with no unit. Other domains already numeric.
findings.problem: Pressor doses are µg/kg/min; UOP is mL/24 h. <500 can be misread as mL/h.
findings.suggested_change: Expand labels, keep 0–4. CV: dopamine ≤5 or any dobutamine (µg/kg/min) (2); dopamine >5 or epi/norepi ≤0.1 µg/kg/min (3); dopamine >15 or epi/norepi >0.1 (4). Renal: Cr 3.5–4.9 mg/dL or UOP <500 mL/24 h (3); Cr ≥5.0 or UOP <200 mL/24 h (4).
findings.research: Vincent JL et al. Intensive Care Med. 1996 SOFA table
findings.do_not_change: 0–4 domain values, sum 0–24, ΔSOFA messaging

findings.name: NEWS2 Score
findings.current: SpO2 Scale 1 bins only. Consciousness: Alert (0) vs New confusion / V / P / U (3). No Scale 2, no ACVPU how-to.
findings.problem: Hypercapnic patients with prescribed 88–92% target must use RCP Scale 2; Scale 1 falsely inflates NEWS2. ACVPU letters (Voice/Pain/Unresponsive) and new confusion are unexplained.
findings.suggested_change: Do not add Scale 2 into calculate(). helpText on spo2: Scale 1 target 94–98%; for confirmed hypercapnic failure with prescribed 88–92% target use RCP Scale 2 — not in this tool. Expand consciousness: Alert (A) (0); New confusion (C) or Voice (V) / Pain (P) / Unresponsive (U) (3), with descriptions (C = new disorientation/delirium; V = response to speech; P = pain only; U = none). helpText: new confusion scores 3 even if still 'alert' by old AVPU.
findings.research: Royal College of Physicians NEWS2 2017 chart (Scale 1/Scale 2 and ACVPU)
findings.do_not_change: Scale 1 SpO2 values, O2 +2, other vital bins, total, 0–4 / 5–6 / ≥7 bands. Do not implement Scale 2 without a separate scoring change

findings.name: CURB-65 Score
findings.current: Confusion (new). Urea already has mmol/L and BUN mg/dL; RR/BP/age have numbers.
findings.problem: Lim/BTS define confusion as AMTS ≤8 or new disorientation in person, place, or time. Stem is not administrable.
findings.suggested_change: Label to 'Confusion (new): AMTS ≤8 or new disorientation to person/place/time'. Optional helpText with AMTS items if license allows; otherwise point to BTS/AMTS rather than reprinting a copyrighted instrument.
findings.research: Lim WS et al. Thorax 2003; BTS CAP guidelines; Qureshi/Hodkinson AMTS
findings.do_not_change: five binary points, 0–1 / 2 / 3–5 bands

findings.name: PSI / PORT Score (Pneumonia)
findings.current: Altered mental status; Neoplastic disease; Liver disease; Cerebrovascular disease; Renal disease. Vital/lab yes-nos mostly have cutoffs; Na/glucose lack units.
findings.problem: Fine 1997 AMS is disorientation, stupor, or coma. Neoplasm excludes basal/squamous skin and is active or diagnosed within 1 year. Liver = cirrhosis or chronic liver disease. Those operational definitions are missing.
findings.suggested_change: helpText/longer labels, keep point weights. ams: disorientation to person/place/time, stupor, or coma. neoplasm: any cancer except basal/squamous skin; active or diagnosed within 1 year. liver: cirrhosis or other chronic liver disease. cerebro: stroke, TIA, or known CVD. renal: chronic renal disease or documented insufficiency (not the BUN ≥30 item alone). Add units on na130 (mEq/L) and glu250 (mg/dL).
findings.research: Fine MJ et al. NEJM 1997 PORT/PSI methods appendix
findings.do_not_change: age + sex −10, comorbidity/physical/lab point weights, class I–V cutoffs

findings.name: APACHE II (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: Severe chronic organ insufficiency or immunocompromise with no Knaus definitions. Physiologic bins already numeric. GCS helpText only 'Points = 15 − GCS'.
findings.problem: Chronic-health points require pre-admission Knaus-defined insufficiency (NYHA IV, dialysis, portal HTN, etc.). Ordinary CHF/COPD do not all count.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on chronic: must predate this admission. Liver: cirrhosis + portal HTN, prior variceal bleed, or encephalopathy. CV: NYHA IV. Respiratory: cannot climb stairs or chronic hypoxia/hypercapnia/secondary polycythemia/mPAP >40/ventilator-dependent. Renal: chronic dialysis. Immune: chemo/radiation/immunosuppression/high-dose steroids, or leukemia/lymphoma/AIDS. GCS helpText polish: total GCS 3–15; if intubated document VT rather than guessing verbal.
findings.research: Knaus WA et al. Crit Care Med. 1985 APACHE II chronic-health footnote
findings.do_not_change: age-point bands, 15−GCS, APS select values, chronic + admitType 0/2/5 logic. Do not add omitted APS variables (pH, A-a, temp)

findings.name: Postpartum Hemorrhage Blood Loss Classification
findings.current: Tachycardia; Hypotension / narrow pulse pressure. EBL and delivery route are clear.
findings.problem: No HR or SBP/pulse-pressure numbers. ACOG PPH includes signs of hypovolemia; staged bundles use explicit vital triggers.
findings.suggested_change: helpText, keep booleans. tachycardia: e.g. HR ≥110–120 bpm or marked rise from baseline. hypotension: e.g. SBP <90 mmHg or >40 mmHg drop, or pulse pressure <30 mmHg (local hemorrhage protocol supersedes).
findings.research: ACOG Practice Bulletin 183 (2017) PPH definition; CMQCC/NPMS obstetric hemorrhage stages
findings.do_not_change: 500 vs 1000 mL route logic, stage helper thresholds, hypovolemia-override

findings.name: PFAPA Criteria Helper
findings.current: Recurrent regularly timed fever episodes; duration and interval are bare numbers. calculate() secretly awards a point if episode 2–7 d and interval 2–8 wk.
findings.problem: Regularly timed is not operational. The windows that earn points are invisible on the inputs (Marshall/Thomas clockwork 3–7 d every ~3–8 wk).
findings.suggested_change: helpText on recurrentFever: clockwork recurrences; typical PFAPA 3–7 days of fever every 3–6 (up to 8) weeks, well between. helpText on episodeDays/intervalWeeks: helper awards a point for ~2–7 day episodes and ~2–8 week intervals (educational). Do not reprint a copyrighted criteria set beyond Marshall-style teaching wording.
findings.research: Marshall GS et al. J Pediatr 1987; Thomas KT et al. J Pediatr 1999 PFAPA criteria variants
findings.do_not_change: point weights, cardinal ≥1 + wellBetween + excludeOther classic logic

findings.name: IgA Vasculitis (HSP) EULAR/PRINTO/PRES Criteria
findings.current: Renal involvement (proteinuria, hematuria, or renal insufficiency) with no lab cutoffs. Purpura stem is otherwise close to EULAR.
findings.problem: Ankara/EULAR renal criterion is quantitative: proteinuria >0.3 g/24 h or morning ACR ≥30 mmol/mg, hematuria >5 RBC/HPF or ≥2+ dipstick or RBC casts — not any protein/blood.
findings.suggested_change: Label/helpText: proteinuria >0.3 g/24 h or morning ACR ≥30 mmol/mg (≥30 mg/mmol) or ≥2+ dipstick; and/or hematuria >5 RBC/HPF or RBC casts; and/or renal insufficiency. Optional: strengthen purpura to predominantly lower limbs (official mandatory item).
findings.research: Ozen S et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2010 EULAR/PRINTO/PRES HSP criteria
findings.do_not_change: purpura mandatory + ≥1 extra domain, alternate-diagnosis override

findings.name: Modified Bishop Score
findings.current: Firm/Medium/Soft; Posterior/Mid/Anterior; station −3/−2/−1/0/+1/+2 with no landmark. Dilation, % effacement, and length bins already match Bishop.
findings.problem: Consistency and position are the published words but juniors still need exam anchors. Station is relative to ischial spines (not listed).
findings.suggested_change: helpText: Station = cm above/below ischial spines (−3 to +3). Consistency teaching similes vary (often firm ≈ forehead, medium ≈ nose, soft ≈ lips). Position = posterior/mid/anterior os relative to the vaginal axis. Do not change 0–2 / 0–3 bins.
findings.research: Bishop EH. Obstet Gynecol. 1964; ACOG induction documents reproducing the table
findings.do_not_change: dilation/effacement/length/station/consistency/position values, pct vs length mode, ≤5 / 6–7 / ≥8 bands

findings.name: Modified Duke Criteria (IE Helper)
findings.current: Seven yes/no flags. Major micro = 'Typical organism from 2 separate blood cultures (or equivalent major micro)'. Echo = 'Evidence of endocardial involvement (echo/new regurg)'. Vascular = 'emboli, Janeway, etc.'. Immuno = 'Osler, Roth, GN, RF'. Micro-minor = 'Microbiologic evidence not meeting major'. Only fever ≥38°C is operational. No helpText.
findings.problem: Cannot apply modified Duke from the UI. Missing typical-organism list, persistently positive-culture timing, Coxiella/antiphase I IgG >1:800 as major, echo definitions (oscillating mass/abscess/new prosthetic dehiscence/new regurgitation; changing preexisting murmur is not sufficient), predisposing heart conditions, full vascular list, that RF = rheumatoid factor not rheumatic fever, and what micro-not-meeting-major means.
findings.suggested_change: Keep yes/no and current definite/possible logic. Add helpText on each item with Li 2000 wording: bloodCx typical organisms (viridans strep, S. gallolyticus/bovis, S. aureus, HACEK, community-acquired enterococci without primary focus) plus persistently positive cultures (≥2 ≥12 h apart, or 3/majority of ≥4 with first–last ≥1 h) and Coxiella single culture or antiphase I IgG >1:800; echo oscillating mass/abscess/new partial prosthetic dehiscence/new regurgitation (changing murmur not sufficient); predisposing = prior IE/prosthetic/unrepaired cyanotic CHD/significant native-valve disease or IDU; vascular = major arterial emboli, septic pulmonary infarcts, mycotic aneurysm, ICH, conjunctival hemorrhages, Janeway; immuno = GN, Osler, Roth, rheumatoid factor; microMinor = positive culture not meeting major or serology consistent with IE. Pearl: clinical Li 2000 only, not 2023 ISCVID.
findings.research: Li JS et al. Clin Infect Dis. 2000 PMID 10770721 definitions of terms; AHA endocarditis modified-Duke table; MDCalc Modified Duke
findings.do_not_change: yes/no values; major/minor counts; definite = 2 major OR 1 major+3 minor OR 5 minor; possible = 1 major+1 minor OR 3 minor; fever cutoff already on label

findings.name: Jones Criteria (Acute Rheumatic Fever)
findings.current: Ten yes/no items. Carditis/chorea/erythema/nodules/arthralgia/fever are bare names. Arthritis adds only '(migratory polyarthritis)'. APR = 'Elevated ESR/CRP' with no numbers. Fever has no °C cutoff. No 2015 low- vs moderate/high-risk stratum. No helpText.
findings.problem: Jones 2015 cannot be administered from this checklist. Missing population-risk stratum (changes joint findings and fever/ESR cutoffs), subclinical echo carditis, moderate/high-risk monoarthritis, fever ≥38.5°C vs ≥38.0°C, ESR ≥60 vs ≥30 and CRP ≥3.0 mg/dL, double-counting rules (arthralgia vs arthritis; PR vs carditis), erythema-marginatum and nodule exam descriptions, and that isolated chorea/indolent carditis may not need GAS (UI still gates on strep — do not change calculate()).
findings.suggested_change: Keep 10 yes/no flags and 2-major / 1-major+2-minor initial-ARF logic; do not add a risk-stratum input. helpText: strep remains culture/rapid/ASO/anti-DNase B plus note chorea/indolent carditis exceptions are clinical; carditis = clinical valvulitis and/or subclinical echo carditis; arthritis = low-risk migratory polyarthritis only, moderate/high-risk mono- or polyarthritis; chorea = Sydenham; erythema = evanescent non-pruritic serpiginous truncal rash sparing face; nodules = firm painless over extensor/bony prominences; arthralgia = do not count if arthritis is major; fever = ≥38.5°C low-risk / ≥38.0°C moderate-high-risk; APR = ESR ≥60 or CRP ≥3.0 low-risk, ESR ≥30 moderate-high-risk; prolongedPR = for age, not if carditis is major. Pearl: low-risk = ARF <2/100,000 school-age or RHD ≤1/1000; recurrent ARF 3-minor path not implemented.
findings.research: Gewitz MH et al. Circulation. 2015 PMID 25908771 — confirm fever 38.5 vs 38.0 and ESR 60 vs 30 from the Circulation table (some CDC/WHO secondary tables list 38.5°C for both). MDCalc Jones Criteria.
findings.do_not_change: yes/no values; GAS gate in calculate(); initial-ARF rule 2 major or 1 major + 2 minor; do not add population-risk or recurrence inputs

findings.name: Framingham Heart Failure Criteria
findings.current: pnd = 'Major: PND' only. orthopnea = 'Major: Orthopnea (sometimes minor in variants) / neck vein distention' (fused + confusing variant note). jvd = 'Major: Increased venous pressure / hepatojugular reflux' (two majors fused). cardiomegaly/rales/ankleEdema/vc have no operational anchors. No helpText.
findings.problem: Cannot map a real exam to published Framingham items. PND is an unexplained abbreviation. Two checkboxes fuse distinct findings so the user cannot tell whether to tick for either or both. Official McKee list treats PND or orthopnea as one major and neck-vein distention, CVP >16 cm H2O, and HJR as separate majors — labels do not disclose this helper's grouping. Cardiomegaly is radiographic; ankle edema is bilateral; VC drop is from recorded maximum. Minors should not count if due to another disease.
findings.suggested_change: Do not split/merge inputs (would change calculate() sums). Expand labels + helpText: pnd = 'Major: Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (PND)' with night-time orthopneic awakening; orthopnea = 'Major: Orthopnea OR neck-vein distention' tick once if either; jvd = 'Major: Increased venous pressure (>16 cm H2O) OR hepatojugular reflux' tick once; rales = pulmonary rales/crackles; cardiomegaly = radiographic (CXR CTR >0.5); edemaPulm = acute pulmonary edema; weightLoss already has >4.5 kg in 5 days — add 'in response to HF treatment'; ankleEdema = bilateral; doe = dyspnea on ordinary exertion; vc = vital capacity decreased by 1/3 from maximum recorded; hr120 = tachycardia HR >120. Pearl: count minors only if not explained by another condition; official McKee grouping differs from these fused boxes — do not retune calculate() in this pass.
findings.research: McKee PA et al. N Engl J Med. 1971 PMID 5122894; Ho KK Framingham HF operational definitions (cardiomegaly on CXR, CVP >16 cm H2O, weight loss with treatment); MDCalc Framingham Heart Failure Criteria
findings.do_not_change: the 8 major / 7 minor keys; meets = 2 major OR 1 major + 2 minor; option values

findings.name: FeverPAIN Score
findings.current: 'Fever in past 24h'; 'Purulence'; 'Attend rapidly (illness ≤3 days)'; 'Severely inflamed tonsils'; 'No cough or coryza'. No helpText.
findings.problem: Stems are close to NICE/FeverPAIN but too terse. Purulence does not say pus on tonsils (could be nasal discharge). Severely inflamed tonsils has no operational finding. 'No cough or coryza' officially means absence of both, but English is ambiguous. Fever is 24 h history — FeverPAIN has no °C cutoff (do not invent one).
findings.suggested_change: Expand labels; add helpText; keep 0/1 yes/no and 0–5 sum. fever helpText: documented or patient-reported fever during previous 24 h (no specific °C). purulence label: 'Purulence (pus on tonsils)'. attend3 helpText: symptom onset ≤3 days before this attendance. inflamed helpText: marked tonsillar erythema and swelling, not mild pharyngeal injection. noCough helpText: score Yes only if both cough and coryza (runny/stuffy nose) are absent.
findings.research: Little P et al. BMJ 2013 PRISM PMID 24114306; NICE NG84 FeverPAIN items; SE London ICS FeverPAIN card (purulence = pus on tonsils)
findings.do_not_change: five binary items; thresholds 0–1 / 2–3 / 4–5 and published strep probabilities in interpretation

findings.name: NYHA Functional Classification
findings.current: I No limitation of physical activity; II Slight limitation, comfortable at rest; III Marked limitation, comfortable at rest; IV Symptoms at rest, any activity causes discomfort. No helpText or option.description.
findings.problem: II vs III both say comfortable at rest without the ordinary vs less-than-ordinary activity distinction, so class cannot be assigned from the UI. Slight/marked are undefined. Symptom quality (fatigue, palpitations, dyspnea) omitted.
findings.suggested_change: Expand option.label (or option.description) to NYHA/AHA wording; values stay 1–4. I: No limitation. Ordinary physical activity does not cause undue fatigue, palpitations, or dyspnea. II: Slight limitation. Comfortable at rest; ordinary physical activity causes fatigue, palpitations, or dyspnea. III: Marked limitation. Comfortable at rest; less than ordinary activity causes fatigue, palpitations, or dyspnea. IV: Unable to carry on any physical activity without discomfort. Symptoms of HF at rest; any activity increases discomfort. Optional helpText: classify by symptoms typical of last 1–2 weeks in known HF.
findings.research: NYHA Criteria Committee Nomenclature and Criteria for Diagnosis 9th ed. 1994; AHA Classes of Heart Failure; 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA HF guideline NYHA definitions
findings.do_not_change: values 1–4; interpretation risk bands

findings.name: TDEE (Harris–Benedict × Activity)
findings.current: Sedentary (×1.2) / Light activity (×1.375) / Moderate (×1.55) / Very active (×1.725) / Extra active (×1.9) with no operational definitions.
findings.problem: Lifestyle bands are unlabeled ordinals. Two users will pick different multipliers for the same patient (desk job + 2 gym days vs laborer).
findings.suggested_change: Add option.description; do not change multipliers. Sedentary ×1.2: little or no exercise, desk/sitting job. Light ×1.375: light exercise/sports 1–3 days/week. Moderate ×1.55: moderate exercise/sports 3–5 days/week. Very active ×1.725: hard exercise/sports 6–7 days/week. Extra active ×1.9: very hard exercise daily, physical job, or twice-daily training.
findings.research: Standard Harris–Benedict / FAO-style PAL bands as used with revised HB (Roza–Shizgal 1984); TDEE activity-factor tables (exercise d/week)
findings.do_not_change: multiplier values 1.2–1.9; revised HB BMR coefficients

findings.name: Katch–McArdle BMR
findings.current: Same activity labels as TDEE but terser (Light, Moderate) plus BMR only (×1.0). LBM helpText already adequate.
findings.problem: Optional TDEE multiplier uses undefined ordinals; Light vs Moderate has no operational rule.
findings.suggested_change: Same option.description set as tdee-harris, plus BMR-only = no activity factor, report BMR only. Do not change 370 + 21.6×LBM or ×1.0–1.9 values.
findings.research: Same PAL/activity-factor table as TDEE Harris
findings.do_not_change: BMR equation; activity numeric values

findings.name: Waist-to-Height Ratio (WHtR)
findings.current: Waist circumference (cm) with no measurement site. Sibling relative-fat-mass already has WHO-site helpText.
findings.problem: Waist site (WHO midpoint vs iliac crest vs umbilicus) changes WHtR and can move 0.5/0.6 bands. helpText unused.
findings.suggested_change: Copy RFM helpText onto waist: midpoint between lower rib and iliac crest (WHO), at end-expiration, standing — or a protocol-consistent site.
findings.research: WHO waist-circumference protocol; Ashwell WHtR literature PMID 26975935
findings.do_not_change: WHtR = WC/height; 0.5 / 0.6 bands

findings.name: A Body Shape Index (ABSI)
findings.current: Waist (cm) unlabeled for site.
findings.problem: Same measurement-site ambiguity as WHtR; Krakauer ABSI is sensitive to WC.
findings.suggested_change: Same WHO-site helpText as RFM/WHtR.
findings.research: Krakauer & Krakauer PLoS One 2012 PMID 22815707; WHO WC protocol
findings.do_not_change: ABSI formula or educational bands

findings.name: Conicity Index
findings.current: Waist (cm) unlabeled for site. Pearls already say prefer consistent waist protocol but that is not on the input.
findings.problem: Same as WHtR/ABSI — pearl is easy to miss; field has no helpText.
findings.suggested_change: Same WHO-site helpText on waist.
findings.research: Valdez Int J Obes 1991; WHO WC protocol
findings.do_not_change: C = WC/(0.109×√(W/H)) with SI units

findings.name: Target SpO₂ (COPD vs Normal)
findings.current: Four groups including 'COPD / risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure' and separate 'Known prior hypercapnia on O₂'. No helpText listing who else is at hypercapnia risk. Bands appear only after calculate.
findings.problem: User may pick General acutely ill for OHS, NMD, kyphoscoliosis, or CF and get 94–98% instead of 88–92%. helpText unused on the select.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on population: hypercapnia-risk is not only COPD — also obesity hypoventilation, neuromuscular disease, severe chest-wall deformity, cystic fibrosis, and prior CO2 retention on oxygen. Target 88–92% unless an individualized ABG-based ceiling exists. Never withhold O2 in a crashing airway/hypoxemic emergency. Optional option.description restating 88–92 vs 94–98 so the band is visible before submit.
findings.research: BTS emergency oxygen guideline O'Driscoll Thorax 2017 PMID 28507176 — at-risk-of-hypercapnia list and 88–92 vs 94–98 bands
findings.do_not_change: population values; 88–92 / 94–98 logic; optional SpO2 comparison

findings.name: SIC Score (Sepsis-Induced Coagulopathy)
findings.current: Total SOFA (respiratory + CV + hepatic + renal only) options 0 / 1 / ≥2; helpText only says sum four domains, not the 0–4 tables
findings.problem: User cannot produce 0/1/≥2 without a SOFA card. Each allowed domain is a 0–4 table (PaO2/FiO2±vent, MAP/pressors, bilirubin, Cr or UO). CNS and coagulation are correctly excluded but the remaining tables are off-screen.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/≥2 values. Expand helpText with condensed 4-domain SOFA crib (resp PaO2/FiO2 ≥400/<400/<300/<200+vent/<100+vent; CV MAP≥70 / MAP<70 / dopa≤5 or any dobutamine / dopa>5 or epi/norepi≤0.1 / dopa>15 or epi/norepi>0.1; bili <1.2 / 1.2–1.9 / 2.0–5.9 / 6.0–11.9 / >12; renal Cr <1.2 / 1.2–1.9 / 2.0–3.4 / 3.5–4.9 or UO<500 mL/d / Cr>5 or UO<200). Optional option.description: 0 = all four domains 0; 1 = sum 1; ≥2 = four-domain sum ≥2 (SIC caps at 2).
findings.research: Iba T et al. JTH 2019 SIC (PMID 31410983); Vincent 1996 / Singer Sepsis-3 SOFA table
findings.do_not_change: INR 0/1/2 and platelet 0/1/2 bands; positive if total ≥4 AND coag subscore >2; max 6

findings.name: JAAM DIC Criteria (Revised)
findings.current: SIRS criteria met: 0–2 criteria (0 pts) vs ≥3 criteria (1 pt); no list of the 4 SIRS items
findings.problem: JAAM awards 1 point for ≥3 of 4 SIRS criteria. The four items and cutoffs are not on the UI, so the user still needs a SIRS card.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0 vs 1 values. helpText: JAAM SIRS count how many of (1) T >38 or <36 °C; (2) HR >90; (3) RR >20 or PaCO2 <32 mmHg (<4.3 kPa); (4) WBC >12 or <4 ×10^9/L or >10% bands. ≥3 criteria → 1 pt.
findings.research: Gando S et al. Crit Care Med 2006 (PMID 16521260); Bone 1992 SIRS consensus
findings.do_not_change: platelet 0/1/3, PT ratio ≥1.2 = 1, FDP 0/1/3, DIC if total ≥4, fibrinogen omitted

findings.name: HEP Score (HIT Expert Probability)
findings.current: Timing/magnitude/nadir/thrombosis selects have day and % bands. Yes/No: acute systemic reaction after IV heparin bolus; severe infection; newly started non-heparin drug known to cause thrombocytopenia. Onset typical vs rapid is terse. DIC already has fibrinogen <100 and D-dimer >5.
findings.problem: Acute systemic reaction is a specific HIT entity (not any side effect). Severe infection has no operational gloss. Culprit non-heparin drugs unnamed. Typical vs rapid onset is easy to mix (typical = no heparin in ~100 days; rapid = re-exposure after heparin in prior 100 days).
findings.suggested_change: helpText on systemicRxn: typically within ~30 min of IV heparin bolus — fever, chills, tachycardia, hypertension, flushing, dyspnea, chest pain, or rarely arrest (Warkentin-type). severeInfection: clinically severe infection as a competing TCP cause (e.g. septic shock), not every positive culture. newDrug: examples vancomycin, linezolid, piperacillin, GP IIb/IIIa, chemo — only if newly started and plausible. onsetType: typical = no heparin in prior ~100 days (classic day 5–10); rapid = heparin within prior 100 days; fill only the matching timing dropdown.
findings.research: Cuker A et al. JTH 2010 HEP (PMID 20854372); Warkentin acute systemic reaction after IV heparin
findings.do_not_change: point weights including negatives; typical vs rapid timing values; no-other-cause gating in calculate(); cutoffs ~2 and ~5

findings.name: RIETE Bleeding Score
findings.current: Recent major bleeding with no days. Active cancer / malignancy history (per RIETE definition) without stating the definition. Cr >1.2, anemia Hb <13/12, overt PE, age >75 already operational.
findings.problem: Recent and per RIETE definition force a protocol-card lookup. Remote GI bleed or treated-in-remission cancer will be scored inconsistently.
findings.suggested_change: recentBleed helpText: RESEARCH Ruíz-Giménez 2008 methods — commonly major bleed <30 days before index VTE (some RIETE reports <15 days); major ≈ ISTH (Hb drop ≥2, ≥2 U, or critical site). malignancy: replace malignancy history with Active cancer (RIETE) + helpText typically diagnosed last 3 months, metastatic, or currently treated — not remote cured history.
findings.research: Ruíz-Giménez N et al. Thromb Haemost 2008 (PMID 18612534) variable definitions; later RIETE active-cancer / recent-bleed footnotes

findings.name: Febrile Neutropenia Pathway Helper
findings.current: Fever already has IDSA numbers. Symptom burden Mild / Moderate / Severe with no exam anchors. Severe mucositis undefined. Allogeneic transplant or profound expected prolonged neutropenia — profound/prolonged undefined.
findings.problem: Mild/moderate/severe without operational definition is the listed P1 pattern. IDSA/NCCN high-risk FN uses WHO mucositis ≥3 and anticipated ANC ≤100/µL for ≥7 days.
findings.suggested_change: option.description on burden: Mild — comfortable, no limitation; Moderate — some limitation, still talking/eating; Severe — looks unwell, mostly in bed, would not send home. helpText severeMucositis: WHO oral mucositis ≥3 (liquids only) or cannot swallow oral meds. helpText allogeneic: allo-HCT or anticipated ANC ≤100/µL for ≥7 days.
findings.research: Freifeld AG et al. CID 2011 IDSA FN (PMID 21258094); MASCC burden-of-illness; NCCN FN high-risk list
findings.do_not_change: red-flag point weights; ANC <100 extra point; fever/ANC gates; educational (not MASCC/CISNE) disclaimer

findings.name: CAT Score (Cancer-Associated Thrombosis, Simplified)
findings.current: Khorana-style site/BMI/Hb/WBC/platelets have numeric cutoffs. D-dimer elevated (Vienna CATS–style) with helpText only Optional; cutoffs study-specific.
findings.problem: Elevated is not a score. Vienna CATS used a study-specific D-dimer threshold, not any value above local ULN.
findings.suggested_change: Keep +1. Expand helpText: optional Vienna CATS-style enrichment. RESEARCH Ay 2010 cutoff (often ~1.44 µg/mL FEU / 75th percentile in derivation — confirm paper before quoting). Do not treat generic above-ULN as equivalent. Leave No if study cutoff unknown.
findings.research: Ay C et al. Blood 2010 Vienna CATS (PMID 20829374); Khorana Blood 2008 site list already on the select
findings.do_not_change: Khorana core weights; optional D-dimer and prior-VTE +1; educational banding

findings.name: Cairo-Bishop Laboratory TLS
findings.current: Each yes/no lists absolute threshold and 25% change. whyUse mentions day −3 to +7, but no input states the same 24-hour window or treatment-day range.
findings.problem: Laboratory TLS is ≥2 abnormalities in the same 24 hours from 3 days before through 7 days after therapy. Without that on the fields, users mix labs from different days or chronic hyperuricemia.
findings.suggested_change: Same helpText on all four: count only if this abnormality occurred in the same 24-hour period as another TLS lab, during day −3 to +7 of cytoreductive therapy. Isolated chronic values do not count. Keep pediatric phosphorus note already on phos.
findings.research: Cairo MS, Bishop M. Br J Haematol 2004 (PMID 15384972)
findings.do_not_change: four binary criteria; need ≥2; adult P ≥4.5 / Ca ≤7 / K ≥6 / uric ≥8

findings.name: Clinical Tumor Lysis Syndrome
findings.current: Laboratory TLS criteria met (≥2 metabolic abnormalities) with no list of the four labs. Cardiac/AKI/seizure items are reasonably specific.
findings.problem: Used standalone, the user cannot know which two metabolic abnormalities constitute laboratory TLS. Companion tls-cairo is a different ID.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on labTls: Cairo-Bishop laboratory TLS = ≥2 of uric acid ≥8 mg/dL, K ≥6.0 mEq/L, phosphorus ≥4.5 mg/dL (adult; peds often ≥6.5), Ca ≤7.0 mg/dL (or 25% change from baseline) in the same 24 h, day −3 to +7 of therapy.
findings.research: Cairo-Bishop 2004 clinical TLS = laboratory TLS + ≥1 of Cr ≥1.5× ULN, arrhythmia/sudden death, or seizure
findings.do_not_change: requires labTls AND ≥1 clinical domain; AKI/cardiac/seizure values

findings.name: Neutropenic Colitis (Typhlitis) Risk Features
findings.current: Fever with no temperature. Concurrent severe mucositis — severe undefined. ANC is a number. FN pathway in the same file already defines fever ≥38.3 once or ≥38.0 for ≥1 h.
findings.problem: Two calculators in this file disagree on fever. Severe without WHO grade is the P1 ordinal pattern.
findings.suggested_change: Label fever: Fever (≥38.3 °C once or ≥38.0 °C sustained ≥1 h) to match fn-pathway. helpText on mucositis: WHO oral mucositis ≥3 (liquid diet only) or CTCAE ≥3.
findings.research: Nesher/Rolston typhlitis reviews; IDSA FN fever definition; WHO mucositis grades already in mucositis-who
findings.do_not_change: ANC <500 / <1000 point logic; CT + pain/fever highly-consistent branch; C. diff as non-scoring flag

findings.name: Acute Interstitial Nephritis Clinical Likelihood (Educational)
findings.current: Peripheral eosinophilia with no count or %. Culprit drugs, sterile pyuria, WBC casts, and exposure-duration bands already have helpText/examples.
findings.problem: Eosinophilia is a hidden lab cutoff (commonly AEC ≥500/µL or ≥5%).
findings.suggested_change: Expand label to Peripheral eosinophilia (AEC ≥500/µL or ≥5%) or helpText with that cutoff. RESEARCH Moledina/Perazella if they used a different number.
findings.research: Moledina DG, Perazella MA. CJASN 2017 (PMID 28877926); Moledina NDT 2021 (this helper is educational, not the EHR logistic model)
findings.do_not_change: weighted points; duration <3 / 3–7 / ≥8 bands; educational thresholds

findings.name: HCM Prognostic Risk (Educational MAPS-style)
findings.current: NYHA I–IV with no class meaning. NSVT on ambulatory ECG with no beat/rate/duration rule. Family history of SCD attributed to HCM with no relative/age rule. Unexplained syncope with no vasovagal exclusion or recency. LVH and LGE ≥15% helpText already good.
findings.problem: These are the major SCD markers. Without NYHA stems, NSVT ≥3 beats ≥120 bpm <30 s, family-SCD (1st-degree <40 y or 1st-degree with HCM any age), and syncope not neurally mediated (often ≤6 months), the educational % cannot be applied at the bedside.
findings.suggested_change: nyha option.description: I no limitation; II slight limitation of ordinary activity; III marked limitation, comfortable only at rest; IV symptoms at rest. nsvt helpText: ≥3 consecutive ventricular beats at ≥120 bpm lasting <30 s (ESC HCM Risk-SCD). famScd helpText: SCD in ≥1 first-degree relative <40 years, or SCD at any age in a first-degree relative with HCM. syncope helpText: unexplained TLOC judged not neurally mediated; ESC treats recent (often ≤6 months) as the high-impact marker.
findings.research: O'Mahony C et al. Eur Heart J 2014 HCM Risk-SCD (PMID 24126876); 2024 AHA/ACC HCM guideline (PMID 38718139)
findings.do_not_change: educational Cox formula; 5-year % output; disclaimer not official Mayo MAPS or ESC HCM Risk-SCD

findings.name: IMPROVE-DD VTE Risk Score
findings.current: Known thrombophilia with no examples. Immobilization ≥7 days with no bed/chair definition. Current cancer with no active-vs-history window. Age ≥60 already in helpText; D-dimer ≥2× ULN is clear.
findings.problem: IMPROVE operationalizes thrombophilia with examples, immobilization as confined to bed or chair ± bathroom privileges, and cancer as currently active. Bare labels over-call immobilized and miss lupus anticoagulant / FVL.
findings.suggested_change: helpText thrombophilia: congenital or acquired (e.g. factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A, protein C/S or antithrombin deficiency, antiphospholipid / lupus anticoagulant). immobility: confined to bed or chair with or without bathroom privileges for ≥7 days (not admitted but walking). cancer: current/active cancer (not remote treated-and-cured; exclude non-melanoma skin cancer in most IMPROVE implementations).
findings.research: Spyropoulos AC et al. Chest 2011 IMPROVE (PMID 21436241); Gibson IMPROVEDD footnotes on thrombophilia and immobilization

findings.name: Ranson Criteria (Admission + 48-Hour)
findings.current: Ten of eleven items have numeric cutoffs and (48 h) tags. Fluid sequestration >6 L (48 h) does not say how to compute it. Pearls mention biliary cutoffs but admission fields do not.
findings.problem: Fluid sequestration is net positive fluid balance (intake − output) over 48 hours, not looks third-spaced. Gallstone pancreatitis uses different age/WBC/glucose/LDH thresholds; a biliary case scored on these boxes is using the original non-biliary set without an on-field warning.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on fluid: net fluid balance over 48 h (total intake − total output) >6 L. helpText on age: these are the original (non-biliary) Ranson 1974 cutoffs; gallstone pancreatitis uses slightly different age/WBC/glucose/LDH thresholds (Ranson 1982) — this tool does not switch. Do not add a biliary selector.
findings.research: Ranson JH et al. Surg Gynecol Obstet 1974 (PMID 4834279); Ranson 1982 biliary variant cutoffs
findings.do_not_change: 11 binary items; 0–2 / 3–4 / 5–6 / ≥7 bands; 48 h vs admission split in calculate()

findings.name: SAPS 3 (Admission Score)
findings.current: Lowest GCS (admission window) as a raw 3–15 number. Physiology numbers say highest/lowest except Leukocytes. whenToUse states ±1 hour, but that window is not on the Box III fields. No pre-sedation / intubated verbal rule. Oxygenation options already operational.
findings.problem: Official SAPS 3 uses estimated lowest GCS in the ±1 h window and pre-sedation GCS if sedated/paralyzed; intubated verbal is untestable. A raw GCS with no exception rule is the GCS-middling problem. Worst-value window must be on the vitals/labs or users will pull 24-hour APACHE-style extremes.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on gcs: lowest estimated GCS from 1 h before to 1 h after ICU admission. If sedated/paralyzed, use pre-sedation GCS. If intubated, verbal is untestable (VT = 1) or estimate pre-intubation speech — do not guess a normal verbal 5. Box III numbers: worst value in the ±1 hour admission window only (not worst in 24 h). Label wbc: Highest leukocytes (admission window).
findings.research: Metnitz/Moreno Intensive Care Med 2005 SAPS 3 Parts 1–2 (PMID 16132892, 16132893); SAPS 3 admission score sheet (estimated GCS, ±1 h)
findings.do_not_change: 16-point offset; comorbidity single-highest map; Box II reason/site maps; global logit mortality equation; omitted rare reason combinations

findings.name: Hemolysis Lab Pattern Checklist
findings.current: Retic Not increased / Increased; schistocytes yes/no. No numeric anchors.
findings.problem: Polish: a one-line cutoff would stop retic 1.8% and rare fragment arguments. Not P1 — educational lab pattern flags, not a validated score item with a hidden published cutoff.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on retic: increased ≈ reticulocyte % above local ULN (often >2%) or elevated absolute reticulocyte count. schistocytes: significant fragments (often ≥1% RBCs or ≥2/HPF) as for MAHA, not an isolated schistocyte.
findings.research: Standard hemolysis/MAHA teaching (ASH; Brodsky reviews)
findings.do_not_change: weighted educational sum and interpretation bands

findings.name: Hypercalcemia of Malignancy Helper
findings.current: Symptoms of hypercalcemia present with no list. whenToUse mentions polyuria, confusion, constipation, dehydration. Neuro/stupor is a separate box.
findings.problem: helpText unused on a yes/no that upgrades urgency. Classic symptoms are one line.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on symptoms: polyuria/polydipsia, constipation, nausea, anorexia, dehydration, weakness, or milder confusion (use the neuro box for stupor).
findings.research: ASCO/classic HCM reviews; Payne-style correction already in formula
findings.do_not_change: corrected Ca = Ca + 0.8×(4 − albumin); bands 10.5 / 12 / 14

findings.name: Revised Baux Score (rBaux)
findings.current: TBSA % number with no estimation method. Inhalation injury yes/no with no clinical vs bronchoscopic cue.
findings.problem: Polish: Rule of Nines / Lund-Browder reminder and a one-line inhalation definition would help. Age + %TBSA arithmetic is otherwise scorable.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on tbsa: use Lund-Browder (preferred) or Rule of Nines; count only partial- and full-thickness burn, not erythema-only. inhalation: clinical (closed-space fire, facial burns, carbonaceous sputum, stridor) and/or bronchoscopic inhalation injury — as documented for rBaux.
findings.research: Osler T et al. J Trauma 2010 (PMID 20381254); ABA burn-size diagrams
findings.do_not_change: rBaux = age + %TBSA + 17 if inhalation

findings.name: Barthel ADL Index Total
findings.current: Single number 'Barthel Index total (0–100)' with helpText listing 10 ADL domains but no 0/5/10/15 independence rules
findings.problem: Public-domain bedside ADL exam cannot be scored from the UI; clinician still needs the Mahoney/Collin card for feeding/bathing/grooming/dressing/bowels/bladder/toilet/transfers (0–15)/mobility (0–15)/stairs. Not a copyright barrier (unlike MMSE/MoCA).
findings.suggested_change: Prefer 10 selectInputs with official Collin 0–100 labels/option.description (feeding 0 unable / 5 needs help / 10 independent; transfers 0/5/10/15; etc.); calculate() still sums 0–100. If keeping one total, put the 10-item scoring table in helpText/pearls.
findings.research: Mahoney FI, Barthel DW. Md State Med J. 1965 PMID 14258950; Collin C et al. Int Disabil Stud. 1988 (0–100 version)
findings.do_not_change: Item weights, 0–100 range, interpretation bands 0–20 / 21–60 / 61–90 / 91–99 / 100

findings.name: SAPS 3
findings.current: Reason options terse (Focal deficit, Coma/delirium, Intracranial mass effect). Infection None/Nosocomial/Respiratory/Nosocomial respiratory. GCS 'Lowest GCS (admission hour)'. Leukocytes unlabeled highest vs lowest. Vent 'informational if oxygenation set'.
findings.problem: Box II cannot be scored without the official SAPS 3 sheet. Coma/delirium hides coma, stupor, obtunded, vigilance disturbance, confusion, agitation, delirium. Focal deficit not specified as neurologic. Intracranial mass effect has no data-dictionary definition. Infection is additive (4+5=9) with no helpText. GCS should be estimated lowest if sedated/intubated. Leukocytes official sheet says lowest.
findings.suggested_change: Expand option.label + option.description from Moreno/Metnitz score sheet (do not add missing reasons/surgery-site — formula completeness out of scope). Infection helpText: nosocomial and respiratory additive (both=9). GCS helpText: lowest estimated GCS in admission hour; estimate verbal if intubated/sedated. Leukocytes helpText: per official sheet (lowest; ≥15 ×10³/µL = 2). Vent helpText: Yes with default oxygenation assigns ventilated PaO2/FiO2 ≥100 points.
findings.research: SAPS 3 Admission Score Sheet (saps3.org); Moreno RP et al. Intensive Care Med. 2005 PMID 16132893; Metnitz PG et al. PMID 16132892
findings.do_not_change: Point values, 16-point offset, global logit, comorbidity max-of rule

findings.name: OASIS ICU Score (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: Yes/No 'Pre-ICU hospital length of stay prolonged / cancer context (educational flag)'. HR and RR labeled (highest) but calculate() also scores HR <40 and RR ≤6. GCS label 1–15 (min is 3); helpText 'lowest appropriate GCS' with no intubation rule.
findings.problem: Prolonged has no hours/days cutoff (official OASIS uses continuous pre-ICU LOS, no cancer item). Entering highest HR/RR misses bradycardia/bradypnea points the educational map still uses. Intubated verbal (T) omitted.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on cancer: educational flag — not official OASIS; official pre-ICU LOS is hours/days. Relabel HR/RR to most abnormal (high or low) to match temp. GCS helpText: lowest GCS 3–15; if intubated, estimate verbal or record VT and use a numeric estimate.
findings.research: Johnson AE et al. Crit Care Med. 2013 PMID 23660729; MIMIC OASIS table (worst HR/RR/temp including low extremes)
findings.do_not_change: Educational point map; disclaimer that this is not the official OASIS logit

findings.name: PEG-3 Pain Average
findings.current: Pain helpText has 0/10 intensity anchors. Enjoyment and general activity have no anchors. None of the three say past week.
findings.problem: Official PEG is three 0–10 items over the past week. Interference items use 0 = does not interfere, 10 = completely interferes (not intensity anchors). Without the window and E/G anchors the ratings are not the PEG.
findings.suggested_change: helpText with official Krebs stems, keeping three numberInputs 0–10. Pain: What number best describes your pain on average in the past week? 0 = no pain, 10 = pain as bad as you can imagine. Enjoyment: During the past week, how much has pain interfered with your enjoyment of life? 0 = does not interfere, 10 = completely interferes. Activity: same stem for general activity.
findings.research: Krebs EE et al. J Gen Intern Med. 2009 PMID 19418100; BPI interference anchors (Cleeland)
findings.do_not_change: Average of three items; 0–10 range; ~1-point MCID note

findings.name: NOSE Scale (Nasal Obstruction)
findings.current: Sum of 5 NOSE items (0–20) with helpText naming congestion, blockage, breathing trouble, trouble sleeping, air through nose during exercise. No Likert anchors; no time window. Scaled internally ×5.
findings.problem: Cannot administer from the UI. Official NOSE is past 1 month, each item 0–4: Not a problem / Very mild / Moderate / Fairly bad / Severe. Same file itemizes PEG-3; NOSE is only five items and is freely used clinically.
findings.suggested_change: Smallest: expand helpText with the five Stewart stems, 0–4 anchors, and over the past 1 month. Better: five selectInputs with those labels/descriptions; calculate() still does raw × 5.
findings.research: Stewart MG et al. Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 2004 PMID 14990910

findings.name: EAT-26 Eating Attitudes Total
findings.current: Yes/No Behavioral flags present (binge, purge, laxatives, extreme exercise, weight loss >20 lb / high concern). Total 0–78 is score-entry-only.
findings.problem: Official EAT-26 behavioral questions are time-bounded and operational. Extreme exercise and high concern are not the instrument. Any one positive item should flag independent of total. Attitude total correctly remains copyright-total-only.
findings.suggested_change: Keep yes/no; expand label/helpText to official five (do not reprint 26 attitude items): binge with loss of control in past 6 months; vomiting to control weight/shape; laxatives/diet pills/diuretics; exercise >60 min/day to control weight; lost 20 lb (9 kg) in past 6 months. HelpText: Yes if any official behavioral item is positive — evaluate even if total <20.
findings.research: Garner DM et al. Psychol Med. 1982 PMID 6961471; eat-26.com behavioral questions
findings.do_not_change: Total 0–78 interpretation; ≥20 cutoff; BMI overlay. Do not reprint copyrighted EAT-26 attitude stems.

findings.name: TWIST Score (Testicular Torsion)
findings.current: Yes/No Hard testis, Absent cremasteric reflex, High-riding testis, Testicular swelling with point chips. No how-to or laterality.
findings.problem: Cremasteric maneuver not stated (stroke ipsilateral inner thigh; watch for testis elevation; compare contralateral; warm room). Hard = firm vs contralateral. High-riding = elevated vs contralateral. Findings apply to the painful side.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: swelling = affected testis enlarged vs contralateral; hard = firm vs contralateral rubbery consistency; cremasteric = stroke inner thigh from pubis down, present = ipsilateral elevation, score Yes if absent on painful side (confirm contralateral if possible); high-riding = affected testis higher in scrotum than contralateral.
findings.research: Barbosa JA et al. J Urol. 2013 TWIST; AAFP POCG testicular torsion (cremasteric how-to)
findings.do_not_change: Point weights 2/2/1/1/1; bands 0–2 / 3–4 / 5–7

findings.name: CHOKAI Score (Ureterolithiasis)
findings.current: Yes/No Hematuria (3). Other items already have cutoffs (CRP ≤0.5 mg/dL, age ≤60, hydronephrosis on US).
findings.problem: Original CHOKAI O is occult blood in urine (dipstick), not unspecified hematuria. Dipstick vs microscopy vs gross changes who clicks Yes.
findings.suggested_change: Relabel to Hematuria / occult blood on UA (dipstick ≥trace or microscopy) with helpText: Fukuhara occult blood; gross counts. Absence does not exclude stone.
findings.research: Fukuhara H et al. Am J Emerg Med. 2017 PMID 28633903; CHOKAI acronym occult blood
findings.do_not_change: Point weights (hydro 4, hematuria 3, CRP 2, others 1); cutoff ≥6

findings.name: QRISK3-style 10-year CVD risk (educational)
findings.current: Family history of premature CAD; Severe mental illness; Regular corticosteroid tablets; On antihypertensive treatment; Atypical antipsychotic. Townsend and ED already have helpText.
findings.problem: Formula tool but labels hide QRISK3 Box 1 definitions. Premature CAD is often AHA 55/65, not QRISK3 1st-degree relative <60 with angina or MI. SMI includes schizophrenia, bipolar, or moderate/severe depression. Steroids are current regular oral or parenteral glucocorticoids. Treated HTN is diagnosis plus at least one antihypertensive.
findings.suggested_change: helpText only (do not change coefficients). fhCad: angina or heart attack in a 1st-degree relative before age 60 (not AHA 55/65). smi: schizophrenia, bipolar affective disorder, or moderate/severe depression (not mild depression alone). steroids: currently taking regular oral or injected glucocorticoids. treatedHtn: hypertension diagnosis AND at least one antihypertensive. antipsychotic: current atypical (olanzapine, risperidone, quetiapine, aripiprazole, clozapine).
findings.research: Hippisley-Cox et al. BMJ 2017 PMID 28536104 Box 1; qrisk.org question list
findings.do_not_change: Educational LP; not-licensed / use qrisk.org disclaimer

findings.name: House–Brackmann Facial Nerve Grade
findings.current: I–VI labels plus option.description for eye closure, synkinesis, rest symmetry. Already usable at the bedside.
findings.problem: Official table also grades forehead (II moderate–good, III slight–moderate, IV none) and rest vs motion. III vs IV is mostly complete vs incomplete eye closure (already stated); forehead-none is the other IV discriminator and is missing.
findings.suggested_change: Append to option.description (House 1985): II forehead moderate–good; III forehead slight–moderate, rest normal; IV no forehead motion, incomplete eye closure, rest tone normal; V barely perceptible motion, rest asymmetric. Inspect rest then forehead / eye / mouth.
findings.research: House JW, Brackmann DE. Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 1985 PMID 3921901
findings.do_not_change: Grade I–VI mapping or interpretation

findings.name: Vanderbilt ADHD Positive Criteria Helper
findings.current: Count fields after the NICHQ form; helpText cites parent items 1–9 / 10–18 and performance 4 or 5. Thresholds ≥6/9 and ≥1 performance are stated.
findings.problem: Intended as a count helper. Users without the form still need rating anchors: symptoms Never / Occasionally / Often / Very often; performance 1 Excellent … 4 Somewhat of a problem / 5 Problematic.
findings.suggested_change: One-line helpText: Count items marked Often or Very often (not Never/Occasionally). Performance: count items scored 4 (somewhat of a problem) or 5 (problematic) on the 1–5 academic/behavioral section. Point to NICHQ Vanderbilt rather than reprinting 18 stems.
findings.research: NICHQ Vanderbilt Assessment Scales / AAP ADHD toolkit
findings.do_not_change: ≥6/9 + ≥1 performance positivity rule

findings.name: Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS)
findings.current: Nine options are titles only (1 Very fit … 9 Terminally ill); no helpText or option.description. Operational descriptors appear only in calculate() after a grade is chosen.
findings.problem: Cannot distinguish CFS 5/6/7/8/9 from titles alone (IADL help vs bathing/house vs complete dependence vs approaching death vs terminal <6 months without severe frailty). Two-week pre-illness baseline rule is only in pearls.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1–9. helpText: score usual function ~2 weeks before this acute illness (CFS 9 is the exception). Put CFS v2.0 descriptors in option.description (Robust/exercises regularly; Fit/seasonal activity; Managing well/walks only; Very mild/slowed up not dependent; Mild/needs high-order IADLs; Moderate/help all outside activities + bathing; Severe/complete personal-care dependence but stable ~6 months; Very severe/could not recover from minor illness; Terminally ill/<6 months and not otherwise severely frail).
findings.research: Rockwood CFS v2.0 (Rockwood & Theou Can Geriatr J 2020); Dalhousie GMR CFS card and Guidance on the Clinical Frailty Scale; CMAJ 2005. Complete Dalhousie Permission for Use if commercially reprinting official wording/pictographs.
findings.do_not_change: option values 1–9; calculate() score passthrough; CFS ≥5 frail note

findings.name: Fried Frailty Phenotype
findings.current: Five yes/no. Weight loss has ≥10 lb/≥4.5 kg in past year. Exhaustion/weakness/slowness/low activity name CES-D, grip, 15-ft walk, and kcal cutoffs but do not state questions, maneuvers, or numbers.
findings.problem: Cannot apply CHS phenotype without the two CES-D stems and 3–4 day cut, sex/BMI grip-kg table, sex/height 15-ft walk times, and sex-specific weekly kcal cuts.
findings.suggested_change: Add helpText only (keep yes/no). Exhaustion: CES-D ‘everything I did was an effort’ and ‘I could not get going’; positive if either is moderate amount of the time (3–4 days) or most of the time in the last week. Weakness: RESEARCH exact Jamar kg table from Fried 2001 appendix (men ≤29/30/30/32 kg by BMI; women ≤17/17.3/18/21 kg). Slowness: timed 15-ft usual-pace walk; men ≤173 cm ≥7 s (taller ≥6 s); women ≤159 cm ≥7 s (taller ≥6 s). Activity: <383 kcal/week men, <270 women (Minnesota LTPA).
findings.research: Fried LP et al. J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci. 2001;56:M146 (CHS phenotype + appendix). MDCalc Fried Frailty item help.
findings.do_not_change: five binary criteria; robust 0 / pre-frail 1–2 / frail ≥3; weight-loss label cutoff

findings.name: Berlin Questionnaire (Sleep Apnea Screen)
findings.current: Snoring and sleepiness items have frequency anchors and 0/1 chips. BMI has no helpText. Category 3 (HTN or BMI >30) is only in calculate() details.
findings.problem: Bedside user entering BMI cannot see that BMI >30 kg/m² (as coded) makes Category 3 positive. Category 1/2/3 grouping is not on the form.
findings.suggested_change: bmi helpText: Category 3 is positive if BMI >30 kg/m² or diagnosed/treated hypertension. Optional helpText on snore: Category 1 (snoring/apneas) positive if ≥2 points from the next five items.
findings.research: Netzer NC et al. Ann Intern Med. 1999;131:485-491. Berlin Questionnaire scoring (categories 1–3).
findings.do_not_change: item 0/1 values; cat1/cat2 ≥2 and cat3 ≥1 rules; high risk if ≥2 categories; bmi > 30 comparison as coded

findings.name: GINA Symptom Control (Checklist)
findings.current: Four yes/no stems without ‘past 4 weeks’. Reliever is ‘SABA reliever needed more than twice/week?’ with no for-symptoms / pre-exercise / MART footnote (only in pearls).
findings.problem: GINA Box 2-2 is a past-4-week checklist. Without the window, night waking or activity limitation can be scored as lifetime. Reliever should count SABA for symptoms, exclude pre-exercise-only doses, and not count ICS-formoterol MART/AIR extra doses.
findings.suggested_change: Prefix each label with ‘In the past 4 weeks:’ keeping existing twice/week cuts. reliever helpText: Count SABA used for symptoms, not doses taken only before exercise. Do not count ICS-formoterol used as MART/AIR reliever (GINA footnote).
findings.research: GINA strategy Box 2-2 / Table 2 (2024–2026): In the past 4 weeks, four items; SABA-reliever footnote.
findings.do_not_change: 0 well / 1–2 partly / 3–4 uncontrolled logic; yes = 1 each

findings.name: Elixhauser Comorbidity Count (Simplified)
findings.current: 28 named comorbidity yes/no, no helpText. CHF/cancer-style diagnoses are self-explanatory. Obesity and weight loss have no operational definition.
findings.problem: Elixhauser obesity maps to ICD obesity / adult BMI ≥30 (Z68.30+). Weight loss maps to coded malnutrition/abnormal weight loss, not voluntary diet. Hidden cutoffs on those two items.
findings.suggested_change: obesity helpText: present if clinically/ICD obese; adult BMI ≥30 kg/m² is the usual equivalent. weightLoss helpText: coded/clinical malnutrition or abnormal weight loss, not voluntary diet. Do not add ICD pick-lists to every row.
findings.research: Elixhauser A et al. Med Care. 1998. AHRQ Elixhauser Comorbidity Software ICD-10 obesity (E66, Z68.30+) and weight-loss (E40–E46, R63.4, R64) lists.
findings.do_not_change: 28 binary flags; unweighted sum; collapsed HTN/DM as in pearls

findings.name: Morse Fall Scale
findings.current: History, secondary diagnosis, ambulatory aid, IV are scorable. Gait is Normal / Weak / Impaired with no observation rules. Mental status is Oriented to own ability vs Overestimates/forgets limits with no prompt.
findings.problem: Weak vs impaired is an observed transfer/gait exam (head position, shuffle, chair-rise, need to grasp support). Mental status is not person/place orientation; it is whether the patient overestimates ability to walk to the bathroom.
findings.suggested_change: option.description on gait: Normal = head erect, arms swinging, stride without hesitation (or bedrest/immobile); Weak = stooped but lifts head without losing balance, short steps, may shuffle; Impaired = difficulty rising from chair (pushes/bounces), head down watching ground, shuffles, grasps furniture/person/aid and cannot walk without support. Wheelchair: score gait used when transferring. mental helpText: ask ‘Are you able to go to the bathroom alone or do you need help?’; if they claim independence but need assistance, score overestimates/forgets limits.
findings.research: Morse JM et al. Soc Sci Med. 1989;28:81-86. Morse Fall Scale administration guides (gait and mental-status operational definitions).

findings.name: Hendrich II Fall Risk Model
findings.current: Altered elimination unlabeled beyond the name. Symptomatic depression omits treated-and-controlled exception. Get-up-and-go options describe the rise but not how to administer (chair rise, not timed TUG).
findings.problem: Elimination is incontinence/nocturia/frequency/urgency/diarrhea/cathartics/toileting deficit; a quiet Foley does not count. Controlled depression should not score. Get-up is rise-from-chair with palms on thighs.
findings.suggested_change: elimination helpText: incontinence, nocturia, frequency, urgency/stress incontinence, diarrhea or cathartics, or toileting self-care deficit; Foley counts only if those symptoms occur while in place. depression helpText: current symptomatic depression; do not score if in therapeutic control. getup helpText: not timed TUG; sit in chair (preferred) or on side of bed, palms on thighs, stand without assistance.
findings.research: Hendrich AL et al. Appl Nurs Res. 2003. Hendrich II / AHI of Indiana instructions (LOINC 104028-6 panel: altered elimination and get-up-and-go coding text).
findings.do_not_change: weights 4/2/1/1/1/2/1 and get-up 0/1/3/4; high-risk cutoff ≥5

findings.name: ADO Index (COPD Prognosis)
findings.current: mMRC option stems are operational. Grade 4 label ends with (4) like a points chip; calculate() then caps dyspnea at min(3, mmrc).
findings.problem: User can pick the correct mMRC grade from the wording, but the chip implies 4 ADO points when updated ADO credits 3.
findings.suggested_change: mmrc helpText: Updated ADO dyspnea points equal mMRC 0–3; mMRC 4 is capped at 3 points. Optionally relabel the last option (mMRC 4 → 3 ADO pts). Do not change the cap.
findings.research: Puhan MA et al. updated ADO index (0–14). MRC dyspnea scale (mMRC) official grade wording.
findings.do_not_change: age 0–5 and FEV1 0–6 maps; Math.min(3, mmrc); 0–14 total

findings.name: Boston Syncope Rule (Simplified)
findings.current: Yes/No labels such as 'risk factors constellation per rule', 'worrisome conduction disease', 'persistent abnormal vital signs', 'volume depletion / profound anemia concern' — no cutoffs or original category lists
findings.problem: Cannot score several Boston categories without the Grossman paper. Vital signs have no HR/SBP/RR thresholds; conduction and ACS items are unanchored; family sudden death has no first-degree qualifier.
findings.suggested_change: Add helpText with published category contents. persistentAbnVitals: SBP <90, HR <50 or >100, RR >24 (persistent in ED). conduction: VT/VF, pacemaker/ICD, pause ≥2 s, 2nd/3rd-degree AVB, or HR <50. volume: GI bleed, dehydration, or Hct ≤30%. historyCad: prior CAD, CHF, VT, or cardiomyopathy — not a general risk-factor count. familyHx: first-degree sudden death. acsSigns: chest pain, ischemic ECG, or unexplained ischemic dyspnea. Do not change any-positive admit logic.
findings.research: Grossman SA et al. Boston Syncope Criteria (J Emerg Med / Ann Emerg Med 2007); MDCalc Boston Syncope Rule item notes
findings.do_not_change: Any-positive admission logic, 8-category structure, calculate() sum

findings.name: EuroSCORE II
findings.current: Bare yes/no or class labels for critical state, extracardiac arteriopathy, COPD, active endocarditis, poor mobility, NYHA I–IV, CCS 4, urgency, and procedure weight. Age/CrCl/LVEF/recent MI already have helpText.
findings.problem: Official EuroSCORE II variable definitions are not on the form. User cannot decide critical preoperative state, arteriopathy, COPD, urgency, or NYHA/CCS class without Nashef Table 2 / euroscore.org.
findings.suggested_change: Add helpText and option.description with official wording. critical: VT/VF or aborted SCD, cardiac massage, ventilation, inotropes, IABP/VAD, anuria/oliguria <10 mL/h this admission. extracardiac: claudication, carotid occlusion or >50% stenosis, amputation for arterial disease, previous/planned intervention on aorta/limb/carotids. copd: long-term bronchodilators or steroids. endocarditis: still on antibiotics at surgery. poorMobility: severe impairment. prevCardiacSx: prior operation opening pericardium. NYHA I–IV activity descriptions. ccs4: angina at rest or any activity. Urgency: elective routine admission; urgent cannot go home this admission; emergency before next working day; salvage CPR en route/before induction. Procedure: count of major procedures (CABG+valve = 2). Do not change β coefficients.
findings.research: Nashef et al. Eur J Cardiothorac Surg 2012 EuroSCORE II definitions; euroscore.org / MDCalc EuroSCORE II footnotes
findings.do_not_change: Logistic intercept and β values, age Xi coding, dialysis vs CrCl bands, VSD original-coefficient handling, calculate() math

findings.name: STEMI Equivalent Patterns Checklist
findings.current: Named-pattern yes/no. Wellens and posterior have one-liners; Sgarbossa/Smith-modified, de Winter, hyperacute T, and aVR/LM have no millimetre or lead rules.
findings.problem: User cannot decide positivity from the ECG without a criteria card. Worst is Sgarbossa/Smith-modified (concordant STE, concordant STD V1–V3, ST/S ratio). Wellens needs Type A/B, leads, isoelectric ST. Posterior needs V7–V9 ≥0.5 mm.
findings.suggested_change: Keep checklist; add helpText with operational ECG rules. sgarbossa: Smith-modified concordant STE ≥1 mm, concordant STD ≥1 mm V1–V3, or ST/S ≤ −0.25. wellens: pain-free biphasic (A) or deep inverted (B) T in V2–V3, STE <1 mm, preserved R waves. deWinter: 1–3 mm upsloping J-point STD V1–V6 into tall peaked T ± aVR 0.5–1 mm. posterior: V1–V3 STD ± tall R; confirm V7–V9 STE ≥0.5 mm. hyperacute: broad bulky T often taller than QRS with reciprocal change. lmain: aVR STE with widespread STD. rvMi: inferior OMI plus V4R STE ≥1 mm.
findings.research: Sgarbossa 1996 / Smith-modified Sgarbossa; de Winter NEJM 2008; Wellens T-wave criteria; AHA/ESC posterior-lead recommendations; Fourth Universal Definition of MI
findings.do_not_change: Yes/no flags, hard-OMI grouping in calculate(), 9-item checklist

findings.name: HEART Pathway
findings.current: History Slightly/Moderately/Highly suspicious with no typical features. ECG Normal / Non-specific repolarization / Significant ST deviation with no mm. Risk helpText lists HTN, HLD, DM, obesity, smoking, family history without BMI, recency, or degree/age.
findings.problem: Slightly vs highly suspicious is mild/moderate/severe without operational anchors. Significant ST deviation has no millivolt cutoff. Risk-factor counting will vary.
findings.suggested_change: Add option.description: History 0 mostly atypical (pleuritic/positional/reproducible); 1 mixed; 2 mostly typical (exertional pressure, radiation, diaphoresis, NTG relief). ECG 0 entirely normal; 1 LBBB/LVH strain/digoxin/RV pacemaker/unchanged known repolarization; 2 new or unknown ST depression often ≥0.5 mm or ACS-pattern elevation. Expand risk helpText: treated HTN, hyperlipidemia, DM, BMI >30, current/recent smoking, first-degree CAD/MI/SCD before 65; known atherosclerotic disease scores 2 regardless of count.
findings.research: Six et al. HEART score Neth Heart J 2008; Mahler HEART Pathway; MDCalc HEART item notes
findings.do_not_change: 0–2 point values, HEART sum, pathway logic (HEART ≤3 + negative serial trop + initial trop 0)

findings.name: Primary Care Rule for DVT (Oudega)
findings.current: Vein distension; Calf circumference difference ≥3 cm; Abnormal D-dimer — no measurement site, laterality, or assay cutoff
findings.problem: Calf difference is not scorable without where to measure (10 cm below tibial tuberosity vs contralateral). Vein distension is easily confused with varicose veins; original is collateral non-varicose superficial veins. D-dimer abnormal has no assay/cutoff.
findings.suggested_change: calf3 helpText: Measure 10 cm below the tibial tuberosity; ≥3 cm vs the asymptomatic calf. veinDistension: Collateral (non-varicose) superficial vein distension of the symptomatic leg. ddimerPos: Positive/abnormal on the local assay (derivation used qualitative point-of-care D-dimer).
findings.research: Oudega et al. Ann Intern Med 2005; Toll primary-care validation; AAFP Wells vs Dutch primary-care rule table
findings.do_not_change: Point weights (calf +2, D-dimer +6, others +1); ≤3 vs ≥4 threshold; surgery time-window (already formula-audited)

findings.name: VTE-BLEED Score
findings.current: Active cancer; Male with uncontrolled hypertension; History of bleeding. Anemia already has Hb helpText; renal already has CrCl 30–60.
findings.problem: Original definitions missing: cancer timing/treatment/skin-cancer exclusion; uncontrolled HTN is SBP ≥140 at baseline in men; bleeding includes prior major or CRNMB, rectal bleeding, frequent epistaxis, or hematuria.
findings.suggested_change: cancer helpText: Diagnosed within 6 months before the VTE (exclude BCC/SCC skin), recently recurrent/progressive, or anticancer treatment within 6 months. maleHtn: Male with SBP ≥140 mmHg at baseline; women do not score this item. priorBleed: Prior major or CRNMB, rectal bleeding, frequent epistaxis, or hematuria.
findings.research: Klok et al. Eur Respir J 2016; VTE-BLEED variable footnotes in Br J Haematol / RPTH tables
findings.do_not_change: Point weights 2 / 1 / 1.5 / 1.5 / 1.5 / 1.5; <2 vs ≥2 split

findings.name: EGSYS Syncope Score
findings.current: Heart disease and/or abnormal ECG (+3); Autonomic prodromes (nausea/warmth) (−1). Precipitating factors already have examples.
findings.problem: Abnormal ECG and heart disease have published lists. Without them scoring of trivial ECG variants will vary. Autonomic prodrome originally includes sweating.
findings.suggested_change: heartOrEcg helpText: Heart disease = ischemic, valvular, cardiomyopathy, congenital, or HF. Abnormal ECG = sinus bradycardia, AV block, BBB, acute or old MI, SVT/VT, ventricular pacing, LVH/RVH, pre-excitation, long QT, or Brugada — not isolated minor nonspecific ST-T change. autonomic label: Autonomic prodromes (nausea, warmth, sweating) (−1).
findings.research: Del Rosso et al. Heart 2008 (EGSYS); MDCalc EGSYS footnotes
findings.do_not_change: Weights +4/+3/+3/+2/−1/−1; cutpoint ≥3

findings.name: OESIL Syncope Risk Score
findings.current: History of cardiovascular disease; Abnormal ECG — no lists
findings.problem: Same ECG/CVD look-up problem as EGSYS. 'Any heart history' and 'any ECG not perfectly normal' will mis-score.
findings.suggested_change: cvHistory helpText: Prior MI, CAD, HF, significant valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, PVD, or stroke/TIA. abnormalEcg helpText: AF, sinus bradycardia, sinoatrial block/pause, AV block, bundle-branch block, LVH, or old/new Q-wave MI — not isolated minor ST-T nonspecific change.
findings.research: Colivicchi et al. Eur Heart J 2003 (OESIL)
findings.do_not_change: Four binary +1 items; ≥2 higher-risk cut

findings.name: Vienna Prediction Model (Simplified VTE Recurrence)
findings.current: D-dimer after anticoagulation qualitative helper: Low/negative, Intermediate, High/positive — no numeric bands
findings.problem: Vienna uses quantitative D-dimer. Intermediate vs high cannot be assigned from the UI. Educational disclaimer does not make the ordinal scorable.
findings.suggested_change: Add option.description with explicit FEU bands (and DDU reminder). RESEARCH official post-treatment tertiles from Eichinger nomogram; if paper cut-points differ, educational map e.g. low/negative below local cutoff (~500 µg/L FEU), intermediate cutoff–~1000, high above that. Keep educational label.
findings.research: Eichinger et al. Circulation 2010 Vienna nomogram (quantitative D-dimer); MDCalc Vienna Prediction Model
findings.do_not_change: Educational ordinal weights for sex/location/D-dimer; do not replace with the full continuous equation

findings.name: ABC Stroke Score (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: NT-proBNP and hs-Tn as Low / Moderately elevated / Markedly elevated. HelpText only says educational tertile proxy.
findings.problem: No ng/L or pg/mL anchors. Two clinicians will split moderate vs marked differently. Age and prior-stroke items are fine.
findings.suggested_change: Replace vague labels with numeric tertile-style bands from Hijazi ABC-stroke or the official calculator axes. RESEARCH exact knots; example structure: NT-proBNP low / ~300–1000 / markedly high pg/mL; hs-Tn low near LoD / around URL / several-fold URL. Keep educational disclaimer.
findings.research: Hijazi et al. Eur Heart J 2016 ABC-stroke; official ABC calculator biomarker axes
findings.do_not_change: Educational point scheme; do not implement unpublished continuous coefficients

findings.name: ABC Bleeding Score (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: Hemoglobin Normal / Mild anemia / Moderate–severe anemia with no g/dL. hs-Tn and GDF-15 Low / Moderately / Markedly elevated.
findings.problem: Anemia bands are undefined. GDF-15 is research-only and has no ng/L anchors.
