findings.suggested_change: Give numeric Hb bands (WHO: normal ≥13 men / ≥12 women; mild 11–12.9 / 11–11.9; moderate–severe <11) or RESEARCH Hijazi ABC-bleed hemoglobin knots. Same for hs-Tn and GDF-15 tertiles; keep GDF-15 optional.
findings.research: Hijazi et al. ABC-bleed Lancet 2016; WHO anemia grades if ABC knots unavailable
findings.do_not_change: Educational domain points; do not withhold-OAC messaging in recommendations

findings.name: FeverPAIN Score (Full)
findings.current: Severely inflamed tonsils as a naked yes/no. Other items already have time windows or findings.
findings.problem: Severely is an unanchored ordinal. Disagreement on moderate vs severe erythema/swelling flips the 2–3 vs 4–5 antibiotic band.
findings.suggested_change: inflamed helpText: Marked tonsillar erythema and swelling (beyond everyday pharyngitis redness) — original FeverPAIN 'severely inflamed tonsils'.
findings.research: Little et al. BMJ 2013 FeverPAIN/PRISM; NICE sore-throat antimicrobial guidance item wording
findings.do_not_change: Five binary +1 items; 0–1 / 2–3 / 4–5 interpretation bands

findings.name: Ottawa SAH Rule
findings.current: Limited neck flexion on examination with no maneuver. Thunderclap already defined as instantly peaking.
findings.problem: Perry defined limited flexion as inability to touch chin to chest, or if supine inability to raise the head 8 cm off the bed. Without that, stiff-neck history gets double-counted with the separate neck-pain item.
findings.suggested_change: limitedFlexion helpText: Cannot touch chin to chest, or cannot raise the head 8 cm off the bed if supine (exam finding — distinct from reported neck pain). Optional applicability reminder: alert ≥15 y, new severe atraumatic headache peaking ≤1 h; exclude new deficit, prior aneurysm/SAH/tumor, ≥3 similar headaches over ≥6 months.
findings.research: Perry et al. JAMA 2013 methods (chin-to-chest / 8 cm head raise); Ottawa SAH inclusion/exclusion box
findings.do_not_change: Any-positive investigate logic; six criteria

findings.name: Tisdale QTc Prolongation Risk Score
findings.current: 1 QTc-prolonging medication (+3) and ≥2 QTc-prolonging medications (+6 total) with no definition of which drugs count. Pearls mention CredibleMeds after the fact.
findings.problem: Scoring 3 vs 6 points requires a drug list the UI does not provide. Users omit conditional-risk agents or double-count loop diuretic as both a loop and a QT drug.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on both drug items: Count drugs with known/possible TdP risk on CredibleMeds (crediblemeds.org). Do not reprint the full list. Select 1 OR ≥2 — not both (calculate() already prefers ≥2). Loop diuretic is a separate +1 — do not also count it here unless independently QT-listed.
findings.research: Tisdale et al. Circ Cardiovasc Qual Outcomes 2013; CredibleMeds / AZCERT
findings.do_not_change: Weights including +6 total for ≥2 drugs; 0–6 / 7–10 / ≥11 bands

findings.name: ATRIA Stroke Risk Score
findings.current: Proteinuria yes/no with no dipstick/ACR threshold. Age bands, eGFR <45/ESRD, and prior-stroke age-weight helpText are already clear.
findings.problem: ATRIA derived proteinuria from urine dipstick (positive vs none/trace), not an unspecified clinical impression. ACR vs dipstick 1+ will be scored inconsistently.
findings.suggested_change: proteinuria helpText: Urine dipstick ≥1+ (ATRIA: none/trace = no). ACR ≥30 mg/g is a reasonable equivalent if dipstick unavailable.
findings.research: Singer et al. J Am Heart Assoc 2013 ATRIA methods (urine dipstick proteinuria)
findings.do_not_change: Age-by-prior-stroke point table; +1 non-age factors; 0–5 / 6 / ≥7 categories

findings.name: de Winter T-Wave Pattern Helper
findings.current: Upsloping STD already has 1–3 mm at the J point in V1–V6; aVR STE has 0.5–1 mm. Tall peaked symmetric T waves has no height comparator. No frank STEMI criteria assumes millimetre STEMI rules.
findings.problem: Tall vs hyperkalemic or nonspecific peaked T is not operational. Frank STEMI criteria is an external-memory item (sex/age/lead cutoffs).
findings.suggested_change: tallT helpText: Tall, positive, symmetric T waves in the same leads as the upsloping STD (T waves continue from the depressed J point — not hyperkalemia’s narrow peaked T). noOvertSte helpText: Precordial STE does not meet conventional STEMI millimetre criteria (e.g. ≥1 mm in two contiguous leads; V2–V3 ≥2 mm men ≥40, ≥2.5 mm men <40, ≥1.5 mm women).
findings.research: de Winter RJ et al. NEJM 2008; Fourth Universal Definition of MI STE thresholds
findings.do_not_change: Core = upslope STD AND tall T; support scoring; reperfusion interpretation

findings.name: Lyme Disease Pretest Probability Helper
findings.current: Endemic Non-endemic / Possible exposure / Highly endemic + outdoor exposure with no geography. Season consistent with local transmission with no months. EM already has ≥5 cm expanding.
findings.problem: Educational helper still asks the user to know CDC endemicity and local season without stating them.
findings.suggested_change: endemic helpText: High = Northeast, mid-Atlantic, upper Midwest (and known highly endemic counties) with outdoor/tick exposure; Possible = travel through those areas; Non-endemic = no geography/travel risk. summer helpText: US Ixodes transmission typically late spring–summer (often May–August); use local epidemiology. emRash helpText: Expanding erythematous patch ≥5 cm, often with central clearing; early serology often negative — treat classic EM.
findings.research: IDSA/AAN/ACR 2020 Lyme guideline (Lantos et al.); CDC Lyme surveillance maps/seasonality
findings.do_not_change: Educational weights; EM+exposure short-circuit to treat-without-serology

findings.name: ROSE Rule (Syncope)
findings.current: ECG Q wave (not in lead III). Other BRACES items already have numeric cutoffs.
findings.problem: Isolated Q in III is excluded, but pathologic Q morphology (duration/depth) is not stated, so minor septal Qs get over-called.
findings.suggested_change: qWave helpText: Pathologic Q (typically ≥40 ms or ≥25% of R-wave height) in a lead other than III.
findings.research: Reed et al. JACC 2010 ROSE; standard pathologic Q criteria
findings.do_not_change: Any-positive BRACES logic; listed cutoffs (BNP, HR, Hb, SpO2)

findings.name: Bacterial Meningitis Score (Nigrovic)
findings.current: Five items have excellent numeric cutoffs. Applicability (not neonates; not critically ill/purpura; CSF pleocytosis; pretreated cultures) lives only in whenToUse/pearls.
findings.problem: A user can enter BMS = 0 on a neonate or pretreated child and read very low risk. Items themselves are scorable; this is unused helpText polish.
findings.suggested_change: Shared or first-field helpText: Apply only to non-neonatal children with CSF pleocytosis who are not critically ill and do not have purpura. Antibiotic pretreatment blunts Gram stain/culture — do not use BMS 0 to stop therapy in those cases.
findings.research: Nigrovic et al. JAMA 2007 methods/exclusions
findings.do_not_change: Five +1 items; Gram-stain override; 0 vs ≥1 banding

findings.name: ASTCT ICANS Grade
findings.current: ICE is a 0–10 number. helpText only 'Orientation 4 + naming 3 + following commands 1 + writing 1 + attention 1'. No prompts. Consciousness/seizure/motor/ICP labels already match ASTCT.
findings.problem: Cannot administer ICE from the UI. Missing year/month/city/hospital orientation, 3-object naming, command examples, standard sentence, serial 7-equivalent (100 by 10). Untestable rule omitted: ICE 0 because unarousable = grade 4, not the arousable ICE 0–2 band (grade 3). Entering ice=0 alone yields ICE-component 3.
findings.suggested_change: Keep one 0–10 numberInput. Expand helpText with ASTCT ICE card: Orientation year/month/city/hospital (1 each, 4); name 3 objects e.g. clock, pen, button (3); 'Show me 2 fingers' or 'Close your eyes and stick out your tongue' (1); write a standard sentence e.g. 'Our national bird is the bald eagle' (1); count backwards from 100 by 10 (1). If unarousable and unable to perform ICE: enter 0 and set consciousness to unarousable (grade 4). Optional motor description: deep focal weakness only, not mild weakness or isolated CN palsy.
findings.research: Lee DW et al. Biol Blood Marrow Transplant. 2019 ASTCT ICE tool and ICANS table (ICE 0 unarousable = grade 4)
findings.do_not_change: ICE 10→0 / 7–9→1 / 3–6→2 / 0–2→3 banding; max() across domains; consciousness/seizure/motor/ICP option values

findings.name: BCLC HCC Stage Helper
findings.current: ECOG options are literally 0 / 1 / 2 / ≥3. Child-Pugh A/B/C titles only. Tumor burden options already name size/number/invasion. Same file iperformance has full ECOG labels.
findings.problem: PS 0 vs 1 vs 2 is the fork to BCLC 0/A/B vs C. Cannot assign ECOG from numbers alone (CIWA-style). Child-Pugh A/B/C is a 5-item score not shown.
findings.suggested_change: Expand PS labels, values stay 0/1/2/3: '0 — Fully active, no restriction'; '1 — Restricted in strenuous activity; ambulatory, light/sedentary work OK'; '2 — Ambulatory, all self-care; unable to work; up >50% of waking hours'; '≥3 — Limited self-care or worse; bed/chair >50% of waking hours'. liver helpText: Child-Pugh A 5–6 / B 7–9 / C 10–15 from bilirubin, albumin, INR, ascites, encephalopathy (use Child-Pugh calculator).
findings.research: Oken MM et al. Am J Clin Oncol. 1982 ECOG PS; Reig M et al. J Hepatol. 2022 BCLC update; Pugh Child-Turcotte-Pugh variables
findings.do_not_change: PS 0/1/2/3 values; Child A/B/C keys; tumor very_early/early/intermediate/advanced mapping; D if PS≥3 or Child C; C if advanced or PS 1–2

findings.name: ASTCT CRS Grade (CAR-T)
findings.current: Fever ≥38.0 °C required (helpText: required for CRS diagnosis). Hypotension tiers match vasopressors. Hypoxia grade 2 is 'Low-flow nasal cannula (≤6 L/min)' only.
findings.problem: ASTCT: after antipyretics/tocilizumab/steroids, fever is no longer required to grade subsequent CRS. Tool returns 'No CRS' without fever and will under-grade treated patients. Grade 2 hypoxia officially includes blow-by O2.
findings.suggested_change: Do not change the fever gate. fever helpText: onset fever ≥38.0 °C not solely infection; after antipyretics, tocilizumab, or steroids fever is no longer required — grade remaining hypotension/hypoxia; this tool still gates on fever so ignore 'no fever = no CRS' in that setting. Hypoxia grade 2 label: 'Low-flow nasal cannula (≤6 L/min) or blow-by'. Optional hypotension G2 description: IV-fluid–responsive, no vasopressors (no SBP cutoff in ASTCT).
findings.research: Lee DW et al. Biol Blood Marrow Transplant. 2019 ASTCT CRS table footnotes (fever after anticytokine therapy; low-flow NC ≤6 L/min or blow-by)
findings.do_not_change: Fever required in calculate(); hypotension 0/2/3/4; hypoxia 0/2/3/4; grade = max(1, hypo, ox); vasopressin-exclusion on grade 4

findings.name: Lund–Browder TBSA (Simplified)
findings.current: Each field is % of region burned. Only head has helpText (100 = entire region). No first-degree exclusion. Age-band region % only after calculate.
findings.problem: TBSA for Brooke/Parkland is 2nd-degree and deeper; first-degree erythema is excluded. Users can enter %TBSA instead of % of region. Collapsed whole-arm/whole-leg vs classic chart is unlabeled beyond 'Simplified'.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on every region field: enter % of this anatomic region that is 2nd- or 3rd-degree — not first-degree erythema; 100 = entire region; do not enter % of whole-body TBSA. Optional: helper collapses arm (upper+forearm) and whole-leg (thigh+leg+foot); use full Lund–Browder chart when precision matters.
findings.research: Lund CC, Browder NC. Surg Gynecol Obstet. 1944; ABA TBSA = partial+full thickness; JTS Adult Lund–Browder form (1st° not in TBSA)
findings.do_not_change: lundBrowderPercents() age bands; region weights (trunk 13/13, arm 7, perineum 1, leg = thigh+leg+3.5); 0–100 fraction math

findings.name: FLIPI (Follicular Lymphoma)
findings.current: Yes/No 'More than 4 nodal areas' with no map. Age >60, Ann Arbor III–IV, Hb <12, LDH >ULN already explicit.
findings.problem: FLIPI nodal areas are a specific mannikin, not Ann Arbor stage or PET stations. Without the list, >4 vs ≤4 cannot be scored.
findings.suggested_change: nodal helpText, keep yes/no: FLIPI areas = cervical, axillary, inguino-crural (count left and right separately), para-aortic/iliac, celiac/mesenteric, other ancillary. Positive if >4 involved areas (≥5). Spleen is extranodal, not a nodal area.
findings.research: Solal-Céligny P et al. Blood. 2004;104:1258 methods + Figure 1 mannikin
findings.do_not_change: Five binary points; low 0–1 / intermediate 2 / high ≥3

findings.name: IPI (Aggressive NHL)
findings.current: More than one extranodal site; ECOG performance status ≥ 2. Age >60, LDH >ULN, Ann Arbor III–IV explicit.
findings.problem: Classic IPI extranodal count treats spleen as extranodal and counts distinct organs (BM, GI, liver, lung, bone, CNS, skin) — not extra nodes. ECOG ≥2 has a cutoff but no Oken definition; PS 1 vs 2 changes the point.
findings.suggested_change: extranodal helpText: >1 distinct extranodal organ/site (BM, GI, liver, lung, bone, CNS, skin). Spleen counts as extranodal in classic IPI. Contiguous extension from a nodal mass is not extra sites. ecog helpText: ECOG ≥2 = all self-care, unable to work, up >50% of waking hours, or worse (bed/chair >50% or disabled).
findings.research: International Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Prognostic Factors Project. N Engl J Med. 1993 (Shipp IPI); Oken ECOG PS 1982
findings.do_not_change: Five binary points; low 0–1 / LI 2 / HI 3 / high 4–5

findings.name: NCCN Distress Thermometer
findings.current: Distress thermometer (0–10), helpText '0 = no distress, 10 = extreme distress'. Five collapsed problem-domain yes/nos. No time window.
findings.problem: Official NCCN stem is distress in the past week including today. Without that window, scores mix today-only vs chronic. Full problem list is copyrighted and correctly not reprinted.
findings.suggested_change: score helpText: patient self-report of distress in the past week, including today (0 = none, 10 = extreme). NCCN commonly uses ≥4 as referral cut-off. Do not reprint the official NCCN problem list. Keep five domain flags as high-level pointers; complete official list on paper/EHR if screening positive.
findings.research: NCCN Guidelines: Distress Management (thermometer stem 'past week including today'; ≥4 threshold). Copyright: NCCN Distress Thermometer and Problem List — score-entry only for the full list
findings.do_not_change: 0–10 passthrough; ≥4 / ≥7 bands; five domain booleans (they do not change the numeric score)

findings.name: Gail Model (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: First-degree relatives with breast cancer 0 / 1 / ≥2. Prior breast biopsies 0 / 1 / ≥2. Menarche and first-live-birth bands already numeric.
findings.problem: Official BCRAT/Gail counts mother, sisters, and daughters only — not father, not second-degree. Including grandmothers/aunts over-scores. Biopsy count is prior breast biopsies (typically core/excisional); atypia is already a separate item.
findings.suggested_change: relatives helpText: female first-degree only (mother, sisters, daughters). Do not count father or second-degree relatives. Strong hereditary pattern → genetic counseling / Tyrer-Cuzick, not this educational tally. Optional biopsies helpText: count prior breast biopsies (typically core or excisional). Do not reprint NCI BCRAT equation.
findings.research: Gail MH et al. JNCI 1989; NCI Breast Cancer Risk Assessment Tool (BCRAT) first-degree relative definition
findings.do_not_change: Educational point weights (relatives ×2, atypia +2); age-band points; unused race display; not-official-5-year-% interpretation

findings.name: Brooke Burn Fluid Formula (Modified)
findings.current: TBSA burned as % with no depth qualifier. Weight clear. Output already splits first 8 h / next 16 h and compares Parkland.
findings.problem: Modified Brooke and Parkland use 2nd-degree and deeper %TBSA. First-degree erythema inflates 24 h volume.
findings.suggested_change: tbsa helpText: partial- + full-thickness %TBSA (2nd-degree and deeper). Do not include first-degree/erythema-only. Use Lund–Browder when age-sensitive.
findings.research: ABA burn resuscitation teaching; modified Brooke 2 mL × kg × %TBSA; same TBSA convention as Parkland
findings.do_not_change: 2 × kg × %TBSA; half in first 8 h from injury; Parkland 4 mL comparator in details

findings.name: BASDAI (Ankylosing Spondylitis)
findings.current: Six 0–10 inputs labeled Q1 Fatigue / Q2 Spinal pain / Q3 Peripheral joint pain/swelling / Q4 Enthesitis / Q5 Severity of morning stiffness / Q6 Duration of morning stiffness. Only Q6 has 0=0 h, 10=2 h helpText. No past-week window.
findings.problem: BASDAI is a patient questionnaire. Cannot administer from 'Q1 Fatigue'. Missing last-week window; Q2 is neck/back/hip pain not generic spinal; Q3 is joints other than neck/back/hips; Q4 is tender-to-touch discomfort not the word enthesitis. Same class of defect as NIHSS 1b.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–10 values and 0.2×(Q1+Q2+Q3+Q4+(Q5+Q6)/2). Shared helpText: all 6 items = PAST WEEK, 0 none to 10 very severe except Q6. Labels: Q1 overall fatigue/tiredness; Q2 overall AS neck, back, or hip pain; Q3 pain/swelling in joints OTHER THAN neck, back, or hips; Q4 discomfort from areas tender to touch or pressure; Q5 LEVEL of morning stiffness from waking; Q6 keep 0=0 h / 10=2 h or more. If copyright review of Bath indices forbids reprint, keep numeric entry and point to the official sheet.
findings.research: Garrett S et al. J Rheumatol. 1994 PMID 7699630; NASS/RheumInfo BASDAI form (THE PAST WEEK)
findings.do_not_change: 0–10 ranges, stiffness mean (Q5+Q6)/2, 0.2 weighting, ≥4 active-disease band

findings.name: Glasgow Outcome Scale–Extended (GOS-E)
findings.current: Eight options titles only (1 Death … 3 Lower severe disability … 8 Upper good recovery). No helpText or option.description. 8-hour / shop-travel / work splits live only in calculate() after a grade is chosen.
findings.problem: Cannot distinguish GOS-E 3 vs 4, 5 vs 6, or 7 vs 8 from the selector. Those splits are why the scale exists. Same pattern as CFS: descriptors appear only after scoring.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1–8. helpText: rate current vs pre-injury with Wilson interview; overall = worst domain. option.description: 2 = not obeying commands and not saying words; 3 Lower SD = dependent, cannot be left alone 8 h; 4 Upper SD = dependent but can be left ≥8 h, cannot shop OR travel locally without assistance; 5 Lower MD = independent at home and can shop/travel but cannot work/study or major social/leisure restriction; 6 Upper MD = reduced work capacity and/or social/leisure less than half as often; 7 Lower GR = residual symptoms still affecting daily life; 8 Upper GR = full return, residuals none or not affecting daily life.
findings.research: Wilson JT, Pettigrew LE, Teasdale GM. J Neurotrauma. 1998 PMID 9726257 structured GOS/GOS-E interview; TBI-IMSOP GOS-E manual
findings.do_not_change: option values 1–8, mapping to classic GOS in details, risk bands ≤2 / 3–4 / 5–6 / 7–8

findings.name: Revised IPI (R-IPI, DLBCL)
findings.current: ECOG performance status ≥ 2 yes/no. Age >60, LDH >ULN, Ann Arbor III/IV, >1 extranodal site are operational. No ECOG scale text.
findings.problem: Cutoff ≥2 is stated but ECOG 1 vs 2 is work-capable vs not, up >50% of waking hours. Rater still needs the Oken card.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on ecog: ECOG 2 = ambulatory, all self-care, unable to work, up and about >50% of waking hours. 0 = fully active; 1 = strenuous activity limited but light work OK; 3 = limited self-care, in bed/chair >50% of waking hours; 4 = completely disabled.
findings.research: Oken MM et al. Am J Clin Oncol. 1982 (ECOG/Zubrod; public domain with citation). Sehn LH et al. Blood. 2007 R-IPI
findings.do_not_change: five binary IPI factors, groups 0 / 1–2 / 3–5

findings.name: CNS-IPI (DLBCL CNS Relapse Risk)
findings.current: Same five IPI yes/nos as R-IPI plus Kidney and/or adrenal involvement. ECOG unlabeled beyond ≥2.
findings.problem: Identical ECOG 1 vs 2 gap as R-IPI. Kidney/adrenal, stage, LDH, extranodal count are scorable.
findings.suggested_change: Same ECOG helpText as r-ipi (Oken 0–4; tick if ≥2). Optional one-liner on extranodal: count distinct extranodal organs/sites (kidney/adrenal also scores its own factor).
findings.research: Oken 1982 ECOG; Schmitz N et al. J Clin Oncol. 2016 PMID 27382100
findings.do_not_change: six binary factors, low 0–1 / int 2–3 / high 4–6

findings.name: DIPSS (Primary Myelofibrosis)
findings.current: Constitutional symptoms (weight loss, night sweats, or fever). Age >65, WBC >25, Hb <10 (helpText 2 points), blasts ≥1% are numeric.
findings.problem: IWG-MRT/DIPSS constitutional symptoms are not any weight loss or a single fever spike. Hidden cutoffs: weight loss >10% of baseline in the preceding year and/or unexplained fever or excessive sweats persisting >1 month.
findings.suggested_change: Expand label or helpText: IWG-MRT: weight loss >10% of baseline in the past year, and/or unexplained fever, and/or excessive (drenching) sweats, persisting >1 month. Fatigue/pruritus/bone pain alone do not count.
findings.research: Passamonti F et al. Blood. 2010 PMID 20008785; Cervantes IPSS / Tefferi How I treat myelofibrosis Blood 2011 constitutional-symptoms footnote
findings.do_not_change: weights (Hb = 2), low 0 / int-1 1–2 / int-2 3–4 / high 5–6

findings.name: DIPSS-plus (Myelofibrosis)
findings.current: Unfavorable karyotype helpText lists complex/+8/−7/7q− etc. Platelets <100 numeric. RBC transfusion need has no definition. DIPSS category: only Low shows 0 DIPSS points; Int-1/Int-2/High omit 1–2 / 3–4 / 5–6.
findings.problem: Cannot tell whether a remote 1-unit transfusion, current need, or WHO transfusion dependence ticks the box. Category labels omit DIPSS point bands so raw DIPSS points can be mis-mapped.
findings.suggested_change: transfusion helpText: tick if the patient currently requires RBC transfusions (typically started for Hb <10 g/dL); do not tick a remote one-off that has resolved. Expand dipssCategory labels (values stay 0/1/2/3): Low (0 DIPSS points) → 0; Intermediate-1 (1–2 points) → 1; Intermediate-2 (3–4 points) → 2; High (5–6 points) → 3.
findings.research: Gangat N et al. J Clin Oncol. 2011 PMID 21149668
findings.do_not_change: DIPSS-category 0–3 plus three +1 factors, groups 0 / 1 / 2–3 / 4–6

findings.name: Durie-Salmon Stage (Simplified)
findings.current: Stage I all low-burden (Hb >10, normal Ca, limited bone disease, low M-protein); Stage III Hb <8.5, Ca elevated, advanced lytic, or high M-protein; Stage II neither. Creatinine A/B already has 2.0 mg/dL. Pearls admit isotype M-protein cutoffs are missing.
findings.problem: Hb numbers present; calcium 12 mg/dL, isotype M-protein grams, urine light-chain 24 h amounts, and limited vs advanced lytic bone scale are not. A patient with IgG 6 g/dL cannot be staged from the UI.
findings.suggested_change: Keep I/II/III values. Expand labels: I ALL of Hb >10 g/dL, serum Ca normal (≤12 mg/dL), bone x-ray normal or solitary plasmacytoma, low M-protein IgG <5 / IgA <3 g/dL / urine LC <4 g/24 h. III ONE or more of Hb <8.5, Ca >12 mg/dL, advanced lytic lesions, high M-protein IgG >7 / IgA >5 / urine LC >12 g/24 h. II neither. RESEARCH: some IMF tables list Stage I Ca <10.5 rather than ≤12 — confirm Durie & Salmon Cancer 1975 before locking Ca.
findings.research: Durie BG, Salmon SE. Cancer. 1975 PMID 1182674; IMF Durie-Salmon table
findings.do_not_change: I/II/III select values, A/B creatinine 2.0 mg/dL logic

findings.name: Binet Staging (CLL)
findings.current: A <3 lymphoid areas Hb ≥10 Plt ≥100; B ≥3 areas same cytopenias; C Hb <10 and/or Plt <100. Five areas (cervical, axillary, inguinal, spleen, liver) and bilateral=one appear only in a code comment and result details after scoring.
findings.problem: Cannot count ≥3 lymphoid areas without the Binet map. Residents double-count bilateral cervical nodes.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on binet: Five lymphoid areas: cervical, axillary, inguinal, spleen, liver. Involvement of both sides of one region counts as ONE area (max 5). Palpable enlargement. Keep A/B/C values and Hb 10 / Plt 100.
findings.research: Binet JL et al. Cancer. 1981 PMID 7237385
findings.do_not_change: A/B/C values, cytopenia thresholds already on labels

findings.name: CLL-IPI
findings.current: IGHV unmutated yes/no with no % identity. Age >65, advanced stage (Rai I–IV or Binet B–C), β2M >ULN, del(17p)/TP53 already specified.
findings.problem: Reports often give % germline identity. Hidden cutoff: unmutated = ≥98% identity to germline (CLL-IPI / ERIC). 97.0–97.9% is mutated on the 98% convention.
findings.suggested_change: Label or helpText: IGHV unmutated (≥98% identity to germline). Mutated = <98%. Optional: use the report’s stated cutoff if the lab uses 97%.
findings.research: International CLL-IPI working group. Lancet Oncol. 2016 PMID 27185642; ERIC IGHV recommendations

findings.name: PIT (Peripheral T-cell Lymphoma)
findings.current: Age >60, ECOG ≥2, LDH >ULN, bone marrow involvement. No ECOG descriptors.
findings.problem: Same ECOG 1 vs 2 gap as IPI family.
findings.suggested_change: Same Oken ECOG helpText as r-ipi (tick if ≥2).
findings.research: Oken 1982; Gallamini A et al. Blood. 2004 PMID 14645001
findings.do_not_change: four binary factors, groups 0 / 1 / 2 / 3–4

findings.name: Age-Adjusted IPI (aaIPI)
findings.current: LDH >ULN, ECOG ≥2, stage III/IV. Pearl says ≤60 but the form does not.
findings.problem: ECOG 1 vs 2 not operational. Minor: user >60 can still score an age-adjusted index.
findings.suggested_change: ECOG helpText as r-ipi. Optional helpText: original aaIPI is for age ≤60; if >60 use full IPI/R-IPI.
findings.research: Oken 1982; International NHL Prognostic Factors Project. NEJM 1993 PMID 8141877
findings.do_not_change: three binary factors, 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 groups

findings.name: MIPI (Mantle Cell Lymphoma)
findings.current: Age and WBC bins numeric. ECOG 0–1 (0) vs 2–4 (2) with no scale. LDH/ULN ratio bins numeric but do not say patient LDH ÷ lab ULN.
findings.problem: Cannot assign 0 vs 2 ECOG points without Oken 2 = unable to work, up >50% of day. LDH ratio can be mis-entered as raw IU/L.
findings.suggested_change: ecogPts helpText: Oken 0–1 vs 2–4 (same descriptors as r-ipi). ldhPts helpText: ratio = this patient’s LDH ÷ that lab’s ULN (not raw U/L).
findings.research: Oken 1982; Hoster E et al. Blood. 2008 PMID 18077791 simplified MIPI point table
findings.do_not_change: age 0–3, ECOG 0/2, LDH 0–3, WBC 0–3 values, low 0–3 / int 4–5 / high ≥6. Do not swap in the continuous log MIPI formula

findings.name: CISNE (Febrile Neutropenia)
findings.current: ECOG ≥2 unlabeled. Mucositis NCI grade ≥2 with no CTCAE anchors. COPD and chronic CVD are bare names. Monocytes <200 numeric. Stress hyperglycemia already has example ≥121 mg/dL helpText.
findings.problem: Cannot assign NCI mucositis ≥2 (grade 2 = moderate pain/modified diet, oral intake preserved; grade 3 = intake compromised). ECOG 1 vs 2 same gap. Some CISNE operationalizations require COPD on treatment and a defined chronic heart-disease history.
findings.suggested_change: Keep weights 2/1/1/1/1/2. helpText: ecog Oken ≥2; mucositis NCI-CTC/CTCAE ≥2 = grade 2 moderate pain, modified diet, does not prevent oral intake, grade 3+ severe pain interfering with oral intake; copd COPD on chronic treatment not remote childhood asthma; cvd chronic cardiovascular disease (documented CHF/IHD/arrhythmia), not hypertension alone. RESEARCH exact Carmona-Bayonas 2011 comorbidity footnotes and stress-hyperglycemia mg/dL (helpText 121 vs some secondary tables 250) before locking COPD/CVD/glucose wording.
findings.research: Carmona-Bayonas A et al. J Clin Oncol. 2015 PMID 25559804 and 2011 derivation; NCI CTCAE oral mucositis; Oken ECOG
findings.do_not_change: weights, low 0 / int 1–2 / high ≥3, do not add MASCC items

findings.name: DAS28 (RA Disease Activity)
findings.current: TJC28/SJC28 unlabeled beyond (28). PGA VAS 0–100 helpText only. ESR vs CRP variant and APR unit helpText are good. Pearl notes feet omitted.
findings.problem: Cannot count 28 joints from the UI (which joints, laterality, tender vs swollen). PGA has no stem or time window.
findings.suggested_change: tjc/sjc helpText: 28 joints = bilateral shoulders, elbows, wrists, MCP1–5, PIP1–5, knees (not hips, ankles, or feet). Tender = pain on pressure/motion; swollen = synovitis, not bony enlargement. pga helpText: Patient global: How active has your arthritis been during the last week? 0 = not active, 100 = extremely active.
findings.research: Prevoo ML et al. Arthritis Rheum. 1995 PMID 7818570; EULAR DAS28 documentation (28-joint set and PGA 0–100 mm)
findings.do_not_change: DAS28-ESR vs CRP formulas, 0.56√TJC + 0.28√SJC coefficients, remission <2.6 / LDA ≤3.2 / MDA ≤5.1 / HDA >5.1

findings.name: CDAI (RA)
findings.current: TJC28/SJC28 as in DAS28. PGA and EGA are 0–10 with no stems. Pearl correctly warns not to use 0–100.
findings.problem: Same missing 28-joint list. Patient and evaluator globals have no operational question, so 0–10 vs 0–100 mix-ups persist and the construct is undefined.
findings.suggested_change: Same 28-joint helpText as das28. pga: Considering all the ways your arthritis affects you, how have you been? 0 = best, 10 = worst (not 0–100). ega: Evaluator/physician global of current RA activity, 0 = none to 10 = worst imaginable.
findings.research: Aletaha D, Smolen JS CDAI methods; ACR/EULAR 28-joint count
findings.do_not_change: sum TJC+SJC+PGA+EGA, ≤2.8 / ≤10 / ≤22 / >22 bands

findings.name: SDAI (RA)
findings.current: Same globals/joints as CDAI. CRP already helpText mg/dL (not mg/L).
findings.problem: Identical 28-joint and global-stem gap. CRP unit is already scorable.
findings.suggested_change: Reuse CDAI 28-joint + PGA/EGA helpText. Keep CRP mg/dL note.
findings.research: Smolen JS et al. Rheumatology. 2003 PMID 12595618; ACR/EULAR SDAI remission ≤3.3
findings.do_not_change: CDAI+CRP sum, ≤3.3 / ≤11 / ≤26 / >26, CRP in mg/dL

findings.name: Thompson Test (Achilles Rupture)
findings.current: Thompson labeled calf squeeze: NO plantar flexion of the foot. Matles: increased resting dorsiflexion of injured foot (prone). Pop/gap/weak push-off are history/exam facts.
findings.problem: Maneuver details needed to avoid a false squeeze: prone, feet off end (or knees 90°), squeeze mid-calf gastrocnemius, watch the foot not toes, compare contralateral. Matles needs knees flexed 90°. Partial-tear false-negative is only in pearls.
findings.suggested_change: thompsonPos helpText: Prone, feet free. Squeeze the mid-calf (gastrocnemius) firmly; positive = no plantar flexion of that foot. Always compare the other calf. Intact plantaris/partial tear may still flex. matles helpText: Prone, both knees flexed to 90°. Positive = injured ankle hangs more dorsiflexed than the other.
findings.research: Thompson TC, Doherty JH. Acta Orthop Scand. 1962 PMID 13981206; Matles AL. Clin Orthop 1975 (knee-flexed resting posture)
findings.do_not_change: yes/no keys, Thompson-positive high-risk branch, findings count 0–5

findings.name: Gustilo-Anderson Open Fracture Classification
findings.current: I <1 cm clean; II >1 cm moderate soft-tissue no flap; IIIA adequate coverage; IIIB needs flap; IIIC arterial repair. Pearl: final grade often after debridement.
findings.problem: Wound size alone does not assign type III. High-energy, farmyard/soil, shotgun, segmental long-bone, extensive periosteal stripping, or delay often upgrade to III regardless of skin opening <1 cm.
findings.suggested_change: Keep I/II/IIIA/B/C values. helpText: assign after debridement when possible. Any high-energy mechanism, farm/soil contamination, shotgun, segmental fracture, or inadequate coverage starts at type III even if the skin wound is small. I = low-energy clean <1 cm; II = >1 cm without extensive crush; IIIA = extensive but bone coverable; IIIB = needs flap; IIIC = arterial injury requiring repair for salvage.
findings.research: Gustilo RB, Anderson JT. JBJS Am. 1976 PMID 773941; Gustilo 1984 IIIA/B/C refinement
findings.do_not_change: five option values 1–5 mapping I/II/IIIA/B/C

findings.name: Mirels Score (Pathologic Fracture Risk)
findings.current: Pain Mild (1) / Moderate (2) / Functional/mechanical (3) with no definitions. Size <1/3, 1/3–2/3, >2/3 without of cortical diameter. Site and blastic/mixed/lytic are scorable.
findings.problem: Mirels’ key pain split is non-functional (mild/moderate) vs pain aggravated by limb function (all such patients fractured in the derivation). Functional/mechanical is jargon. Size is cortical involvement of bone diameter on x-ray, not lesion length.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 1/2/3 values. pain descriptions: Mild = mild pain, not activity-limiting; Moderate = more constant pain, not clearly mechanical; Functional = pain aggravated by loading/use of the limb (mechanical insufficiency). size helpText: greatest cortical involvement as a fraction of bone diameter on AP/lateral x-ray (not craniocaudal length).
findings.research: Mirels H. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 1989 PMID 2684463 (pain aggravated by function)
findings.do_not_change: four domains 1–3, sum 4–12, ≤7 / 8 / ≥9 bands

findings.name: Neer Classification (Proximal Humerus)
findings.current: 1-part label includes ≥1 cm or 45°. 2/3/4-part do not restate the rule. The four anatomic parts appear only in result details after scoring.
findings.problem: Users count fracture lines instead of displaced segments. Need the four parts (head/articular, greater tuberosity, lesser tuberosity, shaft) and that a part counts only if displaced ≥1 cm or angulated ≥45° on the selector.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on parts: Four potential parts: articular head, greater tuberosity, lesser tuberosity, shaft. Count a part only if displaced ≥1 cm or angulated ≥45°. 1-part = none of the four meet that; 2-part = one displaced segment; 3-part = two; 4-part = three (typically head + both tuberosities relative to shaft). Head-split and dislocation are separate modifiers already on the form.
findings.research: Neer CS 2nd. JBJS Am. 1970 PMID 5455340
findings.do_not_change: parts values 1–4, headSplit/dislocation yes/no modifiers

findings.name: PECARN Pediatric C-Spine Risk Helper
findings.current: Eight yes/nos. Neck pain combines tenderness/torticollis. High-risk MVC has rollover/ejection/death examples. Diving named. AMS, substantial torso injury, predisposing condition, and focal neuro have no operational definitions.
findings.problem: 2011 PECARN CSI factors are not administrable: AMS is not a bit sleepy; substantial torso injury has a severity bar; predisposing conditions are a short list; focal findings include isolated paresthesia.
findings.suggested_change: Keep eight flags and AMS/focal red-flag branch (do not retune to 2024 Lancet PECARN prediction rule). helpText: ams = GCS <15, AVPU not A, intoxication, or other altered awareness; focal = paresthesia, numbness, weakness, or other focal deficit; torso = thoracic/abdominal/pelvic injury warranting admission or intervention; predispose = e.g. Down syndrome, cervical stenosis, os odontoideum, EDS, RA, prior cervical surgery; highRiskMvc keep examples.
findings.research: Leonard JC et al. Ann Emerg Med. 2011 PMID 21035905 (this helper’s factor list). Do not replace with Leonard 2024 Lancet Child Adolesc Health prediction rule without a scoring-logic change
findings.do_not_change: eight binary keys, redFlag = AMS or focal, count-based moderate branch

findings.name: ASIA Impairment Scale (AIS A–E)
findings.current: Option descriptions already state sacral sparing and C vs D muscle-majority rules. No how-to for S4–5, DAP, VAC, or NT muscles. Full ISNCSCI worksheet is not reprinted.
findings.problem: A vs B hinges on sacral sparing a rater cannot confirm from the UI: LT and PP at S4–5 mucocutaneous junction and/or DAP; motor incomplete also requires VAC or motor sparing >3 levels below the motor level. Untestable key muscles (NT) and ZPP omitted.
findings.suggested_change: Keep A–E values and existing descriptions. Grade helpText: complete vs incomplete = sacral sparing. Sensory sparing = LT and PP at S4–5 mucocutaneous junction and/or deep anal pressure (DAP). Motor incomplete = voluntary anal contraction (VAC) OR motor function more than three levels below the motor level on a given side. C: more than half of key muscles below NLI grade <3; D: at least half ≥3. If a key muscle is NT, do not invent a grade — document NT. Use the official ASIA worksheet for the full exam; this control only maps the AIS letter. Do not reprint copyrighted dermatome/myotome figures.
findings.research: ASIA/ISCoS ISNCSCI 2019 revision worksheet and impairment-scale definitions
findings.do_not_change: A–E option values, interpretation risk mapping

findings.name: Hasford Score (Euro / CML)
findings.current: Spleen size below costal margin cm, no helpText. Sokal in the same file already has 0 if not palpable.
findings.problem: Palpable vs imaging spleen, and midclavicular-line exam, are easy to mis-enter. One-line reminder already used next door.
findings.suggested_change: Same helpText as Sokal: Clinical exam, cm below left costal margin in the midclavicular line; 0 if not palpable.
findings.research: Hasford J et al. JNCI 1998 PMID 9625174; Sokal spleen convention (cm BCM)
findings.do_not_change: Hasford linear formula and ≤0.78 / ≤1.48 / >1.48 cutoffs

findings.name: EUTOS Score (CML)
findings.current: Same spleen input as Hasford, no helpText.
findings.problem: Same missing 0 if not palpable / MCL exam reminder.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: Clinical exam, cm below left costal margin in the midclavicular line; 0 if not palpable.
findings.research: Hasford J et al. Blood. 2011 PMID 21536864 (EUTOS)
findings.do_not_change: 4×spleen + 7×basophils, low ≤87 / high >87

findings.name: Nursing Delirium Screening Scale (Nu-DESC)
findings.current: Each item is 0 — Absent / 1 — Mild / 2 — Severe. No helpText or option.description.
findings.problem: Cannot distinguish mild vs severe or what counts as a positive item without the Gaudreau card. Missing item stems (time/place/person; pulling tubes; incoherent speech; seeing/hearing what is not there; delayed response when prodded) and the shift observation window.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0/1/2. helpText: score the current nursing shift; 0 = absent, 1 = present mild, 2 = pronounced. option.description with Gaudreau stems: Disorientation = verbal/behavioral lack of orientation to time or place or misperceiving persons; Behavior = pulling tubes/dressings or getting out of bed when contraindicated; Communication = incoherence, non-communicativeness, nonsensical/unintelligible speech; Illusion = seeing or hearing things not there / visual distortions; Psychomotor retardation = delayed responsiveness, few spontaneous actions/words, deferred reaction when prodded or unarousable.
findings.research: Gaudreau JD et al. J Pain Symptom Manage. 2005;29:368-375 Nu-DESC items
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–2, five-item sum 0–10, positive cutoff ≥2

findings.name: Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC)
findings.current: Eight yes/no stems. LOC says RASS/SAS not 0/4. Inattention, sleep, fluctuation have no how-to. Pearls mention coma UTA but the input still scores it.
findings.problem: Cannot administer ICDSC from the UI. Missing Bergeron A–E consciousness (coma/RASS −4/−5 = stop, do not score 1), inattention cues, sleep <4 h / frequent nocturnal waking / sleeping most of the day, and 24 h fluctuation. Current LOC yes/no marks unarousable patients as altered and keeps scoring.
findings.suggested_change: Keep eight binaries. helpText: ams — 0 if RASS 0/SAS 4; 1 if drowsy (RASS −1 to −3/SAS 3) or agitated (RASS +1 to +4/SAS 5–7); if no response or only to intense pain (RASS −4/−5, SAS 1–2) record UTA and do not complete other items. inattention — difficulty following conversation/instructions, easily distracted, difficulty shifting focus. disorientation — any obvious mistake in person/place/time. hallucination — unequivocal hallucination/delusion/psychosis. psychomotor — hyperactivity requiring extra sedation or hypoactivity. speech — inappropriate/disorganized/incoherent speech or inappropriate mood. sleep — <4 h at night, frequent nocturnal waking (exclude staff/noise), or sleeping most of the day. fluctuation — any item 1–7 over 24 h (shift to shift).
findings.research: Bergeron N et al. Intensive Care Med. 2001;27:859-864; ICU ICDSC cards (LHSC/Skrobik) for A–E LOC and UTA
findings.do_not_change: eight 0/1 keys, sum 0–8, positive ≥4, 1–3 subsyndromal band

findings.name: Braden Scale for Predicting Pressure Sore Risk
findings.current: Category titles only (Completely/Very/Slightly limited; Constantly/Often/Occasionally/Rarely moist; Very poor/Probably inadequate/Adequate/Excellent; friction Problem/Potential problem). No helpText or option.description.
findings.problem: Cannot assign 1 vs 2 vs 3 vs 4 without the official Braden card. Hidden anchors: sensory (unresponsive vs pain-only vs verbal but cannot always report discomfort); moisture (linen change every turn vs ≥1×/shift vs ~1×/day); activity (walks outside room ≥twice/day and inside every 2 h vs short distances); mobility (no independent position change vs occasional slight vs frequent slight); nutrition (NPO/clears >5 d or ≤⅓ meals vs ~½ meals vs >½ vs most of every meal); friction (max assist + frequent sliding vs min assist + occasional slide).
findings.suggested_change: Keep values (friction 1–3; others 1–4). Braden Scale is copyrighted (Prevention Plus). If license allows, put official descriptors in option.description. If not, do not reprint the card; helpText on each subscale: score from the official Braden card; titles here are not sufficient to distinguish 1 vs 2 vs 3 vs 4. Optional non-verbatim reminders: moisture ≈ linen-change frequency; NPO >5 days counts as very poor nutrition.
findings.research: Bergstrom N, Braden BJ et al. 1987; official Braden Scale (Prevention Plus). Complete copyright permission if reprinting official wording.
findings.do_not_change: subscale values 1–4 (friction 1–3), total 6–23, risk bands ≤9 / 10–12 / 13–14 / 15–18 / 19–23

findings.name: Waterlow Pressure Ulcer Risk Score
findings.current: Combined sexAge: Male (1), Female (2), then 14–49 (+1 already includes sex), 50–64 combined value 3, 65–74 typical 3–4 value 4, etc. Build Average/Above average/Obese/Below average with no BMI. Neuro Diabetes/MS/CVA — use 5 vs Paraplegia 5–6. Skin single-select.
findings.problem: Official Waterlow adds sex (M 1 / F 2) plus age (14–49:1 … 81+:5). A 70-year-old woman is 2+3=5; UI offers typical 3–4 as a single 4. Male/Female options omit age. Build lacks BMI 20–24.9 / 25–29.9 / ≥30 / <20. Neuro official is 4–6 by severity. Skin findings on the printed card can stack.
findings.suggested_change: Do not change calculate() sum. Expand sexAge labels to explicit combined points (Male 14–49=2, Female 14–49=3, Male 50–64=3, Female 50–64=4, … Male 81+=6, Female 81+=7). build labels: BMI 20–24.9 (0) / 25–29.9 (1) / ≥30 (2) / <20 (3). neuro helpText: official 4–6 for diabetes/MS/CVA/motor-sensory/paraplegia — pick 4 mild / 5 moderate / 6 complete; this control only offers 5 or 6. skin helpText: official card may add multiple descriptors; this tool is highest-one-only. Waterlow card copyright Judy Waterlow.
findings.research: Waterlow J. Nurs Times. 1985; official Waterlow score card (sex+age additive; BMI build; neuro 4–6)
findings.do_not_change: ten-field sum, thresholds 10 / 15 / 20; do not split sex and age into new inputs unless a later scoring-logic change is approved

findings.name: LODS Score (Simplified)
findings.current: CV/renal/pulm/heme/hepatic are Normal (0) / Mild (1) / Moderate (3) / Severe (5). Neuro already has GCS bands. Details admit full LODS uses detailed cut-points.
findings.problem: Cannot assign 1 vs 3 vs 5 without Le Gall Table 1 (HR/SBP, urea/Cr/UOP, vent+PF, WBC/platelets, bilirubin/PT). Empty educational bins are not scorable.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0/1/3/5. Expand labels/option.description: CV 0 = HR 30–139 and SBP 90–239; 1 = HR ≥140 or SBP 70–89 or 240–269; 3 = SBP 40–69 or ≥270; 5 = HR <30 or SBP <40 (worst of HR or SBP). Pulm 0 = not MV/CPAP; 1 = MV/CPAP and PF ≥150; 3 = MV/CPAP and PF <150 (official pulm max is 3 — if the 5 option is kept, map/describe as unused). Heme 0 = WBC 2.5–49.9 and platelets ≥50; 1 = WBC 1.0–2.4 or ≥50 or platelets <50; 3 = WBC <1.0. Hepatic 0 = bili <2.0 mg/dL and PT <3 s above control; 1 = bili ≥2.0 or PT ≥3 s (official hepatic max is 1). Neuro helpText: worst GCS; if sedated, estimated pre-sedation GCS. Renal: RESEARCH exact urea mmol/L, creatinine, UOP L/24 h from Le Gall 1996 Table 1.
findings.research: Le Gall JR et al. JAMA. 1996;276:802-810 Table 1; SFAR LODS variable definitions
findings.do_not_change: 0/1/3/5 option values, six-domain sum, interpretation bands as coded. Do not add the official logistic mortality equation unless separately specified

findings.name: Norton Pressure Sore Risk Scale
findings.current: Physical Good/Fair/Poor/Very bad. Mobility Full/Slightly limited/Very limited/Immobile. Activity and incontinence already name ambulant/chairbound/bedbound and incontinence type. Mental uses published Norton words.
findings.problem: Physical good/fair/poor/very bad has no operational meaning. Mobility slightly vs very limited lacks the independent position-change rule.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 4/3/2/1. option.description: Physical 4 = good for age; 3 = medical problems, fair condition; 2 = poor, multiple or poorly controlled illness; 1 = very bad/moribund. Mobility 4 = full independent position change; 3 = frequent small changes; 2 = occasional slight changes only; 1 = no independent change. Optional mental: apathetic = disinterested; stuporous = responds only to vigorous stimulation.
findings.research: Norton D, McLaren R, Exton-Smith AN 1962; NICE CG179 Norton table reproductions
findings.do_not_change: five 1–4 domains, total 5–20, classic cutoff ≤14

findings.name: MUST Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool
findings.current: BMI >20 (0) / 18.5–20 (1) / <18.5 (2) / BMI unknown — use alternative measures per BAPEN (value 0). Weight-loss % and acute-disease >5 days already operational.
findings.problem: Unobtainable height/weight forces 0 points while telling the user to use BAPEN alternatives, without ulna-length or MUAC mapping. Thin unweighed patients will be under-scored.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/2. helpText: obese >30 still scores 0 on the BMI step. If BMI unmeasurable, estimate height from ulna length (BAPEN table); MUAC <23.5 cm suggests BMI <20 (at least 1 if also clinically thin). BAPEN: MUAC is not a standalone MUST point — do not assume unknown = 0. Optional relabel: BMI unknown — alternatives used; this choice scores 0 pending clinical estimate. MUST is BAPEN copyright (free non-commercial).
findings.research: Elia M / BAPEN MUST Explanatory Booklet (ulna length; MUAC <23.5 cm ≈ BMI <20; >32 cm ≈ BMI >30)
findings.do_not_change: BMI 0/1/2 + weight-loss 0/1/2 + acute 0/2, categories 0 / 1 / ≥2

findings.name: SCAP Score (Severe CAP)
findings.current: Altered mental status (+5). Other items already have pH, SBP, RR, PaO2/PF, BUN, age, infiltrate cutoffs.
findings.problem: España AMS is new disorientation/confusion (person, place, or time) or equivalent, not chronic baseline dementia without acute change.
findings.suggested_change: Label/helpText: Altered mental status — new disorientation to person/place/time or GCS <15 (+5). If baseline dementia, score only acute change.
findings.research: España PP et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2006;174:1249-1256
findings.do_not_change: point weights 13/11/9/6/5, severe if ≥10 or major pH/SBP

findings.name: MuLBSTA Score (Viral Pneumonia)
findings.current: Bacterial coinfection (+4). Lymphopenia already has ≤0.8 ×10⁹/L.
findings.problem: Coinfection is not any suspected bacteria. Derivation used positive respiratory/blood culture or a typical clinical + laboratory bacterial picture.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: Yes if proven (blood or respiratory culture with a bacterial pathogen) or a typical bacterial presentation with supporting labs. Do not tick for viral pneumonia alone.
findings.research: Guo L et al. MuLBSTA viral pneumonia mortality score — coinfection definition in derivation methods

findings.name: ISARIC 4C Mortality Score (COVID-19)
findings.current: Number of comorbidities 0 / 1 / ≥2 with no list. SpO2 bins numeric but not labeled room air on the input (only in pearls).
findings.problem: Knight/ISARIC count a modified Charlson set: chronic cardiac; chronic respiratory excluding asthma; chronic renal (eGFR ≤30); liver; dementia; chronic neurological; connective tissue; diabetes; HIV/AIDS; malignancy; plus clinician-defined obesity. Asthma-only should not count. SpO2 points assume room air.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on comorbid: count chronic cardiac; chronic respiratory excluding asthma; chronic renal (eGFR ≤30); liver disease; dementia; chronic neurological; connective tissue; diabetes; HIV/AIDS; malignancy; clinician-defined obesity. Do not count asthma alone. helpText on spo2: admission SpO2 on room air when feasible.
findings.research: Knight SR et al. BMJ. 2020;370:m3339 comorbidity footnote and SpO2 on room air
findings.do_not_change: age/sex/RR/SpO2/GCS/urea/CRP values, max 21, mortality bands 0–3 / 4–8 / 9–14 / 15–21

findings.name: IMPROVE VTE Risk Score
findings.current: Known thrombophilia; Active/current cancer; Immobilized ≥7 days. Prior VTE, paralysis, ICU, age >60 are scorable.
findings.problem: Which thrombophilias count, what active cancer is, and that immobilized means bed/chair confinement (including days before admission) are hidden.
findings.suggested_change: helpText only. thrombophilia: documented hereditary (FVL, PT G20210A, AT/PC/PS) or acquired (APLS) — not family history alone. cancer: current/under treatment, diagnosed within ~6 months, metastatic, or palliative. immobile: confined to bed or chair ≥7 consecutive days including immediately before admission.
findings.research: Spyropoulos AC et al. Chest. 2011;140:706-714 IMPROVE VTE model

findings.name: Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI)
findings.current: Disease names only (Moderate–severe CKD, Mild liver disease, Diabetes without end-organ damage, Solid tumor localized, AIDS). Age-adjusted CCI computed from age. Pearls say score highest diabetes/liver/tumor tier.
findings.problem: Users will tick ordinary CKD, HIV without AIDS, diet-only diabetes, remote skin cancer, or any CHF history. Charlson 1987: CKD = Cr >3 mg/dL or dialysis/transplant/uremia; mild liver = cirrhosis without portal HTN or chronic hepatitis; moderate–severe liver = portal HTN/varices/failure; DM +1 = insulin or oral agents not diet alone; +2 = retinopathy/neuropathy/nephropathy; tumor +2 = treated in last 5 years exclude non-melanoma skin; AIDS ≠ HIV; MI documented; CHF symptomatic treatment-responsive; PVD claudication/bypass/gangrene or untreated aneurysm ≥6 cm.
findings.suggested_change: helpText / slightly longer labels, keep yes/no weights. Quote those operational definitions. Optional cva: TIA or stroke with minor/no residua (hemiplegia is the separate +2 item).
findings.research: Charlson ME et al. J Chronic Dis. 1987;40:373-383 methods definitions (Cr >3 mg/dL; 5-year tumor window)
findings.do_not_change: weights, mutually exclusive dm/liver/cancer logic, age points 50–59:1 … ≥80:4

findings.name: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score (Marshall)
findings.current: PAR bins ≤10 / 10.1–15 / 15.1–20 / 20.1–30 / >30 / high-dose pressors. helpText: PAR = HR × CVP / MAP; if CVP unknown, approximate by shock severity / vasopressor need. Other domains already numeric.
findings.problem: Cannot compute PAR without CVP/RAP. Approximate by shock severity is not a Marshall rule; high-dose pressors as score 4 is an unofficial surrogate.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–4. Strengthen helpText: PAR = HR (beats/min) × CVP (mmHg) ÷ MAP (mmHg). Example: HR 100, CVP 12, MAP 70 → PAR 17.1 → 2 points. If no CVP, this domain cannot be scored from vitals alone — do not invent a pressor-dose table; high-dose pressors is an educational surrogate for PAR >30 only.
findings.research: Marshall JC et al. Crit Care Med. 1995;23:1638-1652 (PAR = HR × RAP/MAP)
findings.do_not_change: 0–4 per domain, PF/Cr/bili/plt/GCS bins, total 0–24

findings.name: Sepsis-3 Septic Shock Helper
findings.current: Adequate fluid resuscitation given. Vasopressors for MAP ≥65 and lactate >2 are explicit.
findings.problem: Adequate is the hidden cutoff. Sepsis-3 leaves volume unspecified; SSC operationalizes ~30 mL/kg crystalloid (or clinically adequate preload) before the shock label.
findings.suggested_change: Label/helpText: Adequate volume resuscitation (e.g. ~30 mL/kg crystalloid unless fluid-intolerant / already volume-replete). Do not change the AND logic.
findings.research: Singer M et al. JAMA 2016 Sepsis-3; Evans L et al. Crit Care Med. 2021 SSC hour-1 30 mL/kg
findings.do_not_change: infection AND vasopressors AND lactate >2 AND fluids logic; lactate threshold >2

findings.name: DRIP Score (Drug-Resistant Pneumonia)
findings.current: Prior DRP, poor functional status, gastric acid suppression, wound care, MRSA colonization — no time windows or operational definitions. Abx 60 d, hosp 60 d, LTCF, tube feed already specified.
findings.problem: Webb: prior DRP within 1 year; MRSA colonization within 1 year; poor function = Karnofsky <70 or nonambulatory; acid suppression = PPI or H2RA; wound care = skilled wound care. Without those, poor functional status and acid suppression are guessed.
findings.suggested_change: helpText/longer labels, keep 2/1 weights. priorDrp: MRSA or Pseudomonas infection in the past 1 year. mrsaCol: documented MRSA colonization in the past 1 year. poorFunc: Karnofsky <70 or nonambulatory / dependent for ADLs. acidSuppression: PPI or H2-blocker (e.g. within 14 days). woundCare: active skilled wound care (e.g. within 30 days). Optional ltc: skilled nursing/LTC, not assisted living.
findings.research: Webb BJ et al. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2016;60:2652-2663 (prior DRP 1 yr; Karnofsky <70 or nonambulatory; H2/PPI)
findings.do_not_change: major +2 / minor +1, threshold ≥4

findings.name: Riker Sedation-Agitation Scale (SAS)
findings.current: Labels already include operational fragments (noxious stimuli; physical stimuli only; follows simple commands; restraints; pulling lines, thrashing). No option.description.
findings.problem: 5 vs 6 and 2 vs 3 are the usual mis-scores. Official Riker: 5 calms to verbal limits; 6 does not calm despite frequent verbal reminding. 3 awakens to voice/gentle shaking then drifts; 2 arouses to physical stimuli but does not follow commands.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1–7. option.description with Riker 1999 wording (7 climbing bedrail/striking staff; 6 frequent verbal limits + restraints; 5 anxious, attempting to sit, calms to verbal; 3 verbal/gentle shake then drifts; 2 spontaneous movement possible but no commands).
findings.research: Riker RR et al. Crit Care Med. 1999;27:1325-1329
findings.do_not_change: ordinal 1–7 passthrough, target SAS 3–4 messaging

findings.name: SAPS II
findings.current: Point bands already in helpText on nearly every physiologic input. Admission type is Scheduled surgical / Medical / Unscheduled surgical with no 24 h rule. GCS helpText is points only.
findings.problem: Le Gall: scheduled surgical = operation planned ≥24 h in advance; unscheduled = emergency. GCS if sedated = estimated pre-sedation (worst 24 h).
findings.suggested_change: helpText on admit: scheduled = surgery planned ≥24 hours ahead; unscheduled surgical = emergency operation; medical = no surgery this admission. helpText on gcs: worst in first 24 h; if sedated/intubated, estimated GCS before sedation (do not assign verbal 1 solely for the tube).
findings.research: Le Gall JR et al. JAMA. 1993;270:2957-2963 SAPS II definitions
findings.do_not_change: official point bands, chronic 0/9/10/17, admit 0/6/8, logistic formula

findings.name: TST Interpretation by Risk Group
findings.current: mm number + long risk-group labels (5/10/15 mm lists). Pearls already say measure induration not erythema at 48–72 h.
findings.problem: The administering rule (palpate induration, not erythema; read 48–72 h) is not on the input the user fills.
findings.suggested_change: induration helpText: measure induration (palpable firmness), not erythema, at 48–72 hours after Mantoux placement. Two-step testing if serial screening (booster).
findings.research: CDC / ATS targeted tuberculin testing (5/10/15 mm; reading technique)
findings.do_not_change: 5/10/15 mm group logic, BCG/IGRA context flags

findings.name: RACE Scale (Prehospital LVO)
findings.current: Face/arm/leg are Absent–Mild–Moderate/severe or Normal-to-mild–Moderate–Severe with no maneuver or hold times. Gaze Absent/Present. Agnosia ‘recognizes arm and impairment’ without prompts. Aphasia already names close eyes + make a fist.
findings.problem: Cannot administer RACE from the UI. Official scoring needs smile/show teeth; arm 90° sitting or 45° supine scored by hold >10 s; each leg 30° supine scored by hold >5 s; gaze present if cannot shift past midline; agnosia prompts ‘Whose arm is this?’ and ‘Can you move your arm?’. Mild vs moderate/severe is otherwise guesswork — same class of failure as NIHSS 1b/1c.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0–2 / 0–1. Face helpText: ask to show teeth or smile; 0 symmetrical, 1 slightly asymmetrical, 2 completely asymmetrical. Arm: extend 90° sitting or 45° supine, palms up, weaker arm; 0 upholds >10 s, 1 <10 s, 2 cannot raise / drops immediately. Leg: supine raise 30°; 0 upholds >5 s, 1 <5 s, 2 cannot raise. Gaze: if forced to one side, ask to look the other way; present = cannot shift past midline. Agnosia (left hemiparesis): show paretic arm ‘Whose arm is this?’ then ‘Can you move your arm?’; 0 recognizes arm AND weakness, 1 asomatognosia OR anosognosia, 2 both.
findings.research: Pérez de la Ossa N et al. Stroke. 2014; racescale.org table; NJ/SC EMS RACE scoring cards
findings.do_not_change: option values, cortical-branch logic by hemiparesis side, sum 0–9, cutoff ≥5

findings.name: C-STAT (Cincinnati Stroke Triage Assessment Tool)
findings.current: LOC label is ‘incorrect on ≥1 of 2 orientation questions OR fails ≥1 of 2 commands’ with no questions or commands. Gaze is preference/conjugate deviation present. Arm already says cannot hold against gravity for 10 s.
findings.problem: NIHSS 1b/1c-class failure: cannot score LOC without the two questions (age, month) and two commands (close eyes; open and close the hand / make a fist). Gaze lacks the cannot-cross-midline rule.
findings.suggested_change: Keep yes/no and weights (gaze 2, arm 1, loc 1). loc helpText: Questions — What is your age? What month is it? Commands — Close your eyes. Make a fist / open and close your hand. Score Yes if ≥1 question wrong OR ≥1 command failed (this tool’s coded rule). Do not silently switch to AND wording used on some EMS cards. Gaze helpText: present if conjugate deviation; cannot shift gaze past midline.
findings.research: Katz BS et al. Stroke. 2015 (CPSSS/C-STAT); AHA ASLS C-STAT checklist (age, month, close eyes, open/close hands)
findings.do_not_change: 2+1+1 weights, ≥2 cutoff, keep coded OR (not AND) for the LOC item

findings.name: bCAM Simplified (Brief Confusion Assessment)
findings.current: Four yes/no features. F2 mentions e.g. months backwards / digit span errors but not the task or error rule. F4 is illogical answers / unclear flow with no questions or command. F1 has no time window. In-app cam-icu already prints the exam; bCAM does not.
findings.problem: Cannot administer bCAM from the UI. Official F2 is months backwards December to July (>1 error or cannot complete). F4 is four yes/no questions plus a two-step finger command (≥2 errors). F1 is acute change or fluctuation over the prior 24 h from baseline.
findings.suggested_change: Keep four booleans and F1+F2 and (F3 or F4) logic. F1 helpText: acute change from baseline or fluctuating course over the past 24 h (nurse/family/chart). F2: ‘Name the months backwards from December to July’; inattention = any error, >15 s pause/perseveration, or cannot start. F3 optional: any RASS other than 0; if unarousable do not diagnose this round. F4 Set A: Will a stone float on water? Are there fish in the sea? Does 1 lb weigh more than 2 lb? Can you use a hammer to pound a nail? Then ‘Hold up this many fingers’ (show 2); ‘Now the same with the other hand’ (do not demonstrate). Disorganized = ≥2 errors. Do not reprint a copyrighted CAM worksheet beyond published bCAM prompts.
findings.research: Han JH et al. Ann Emerg Med. 2013; Vanderbilt bCAM Training Manual / flowsheet 2015 (copyright Vanderbilt/HELP — keep to published bedside prompts)
findings.do_not_change: four yes/no keys, positive = F1 AND F2 AND (F3 OR F4)

findings.name: LAMS (Los Angeles Motor Scale)
findings.current: Facial droop Absent/Present; arm Absent / Drifts down / Falls rapidly; grip Normal / Weak / No grip. No how-to, no 10 s hold.
findings.problem: LAMS is the LAPSS motor exam. Without smile/show teeth, palms-up 10 s drift, and grip as a handshake, drifts down vs falls rapidly is not standardized.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1 and 0/1/2. Face helpText: smile and show teeth; present = partial or complete unilateral droop. Arm: eyes closed, both arms out palms up 10 s; 0 no drift; 1 drifts down but does not hit the bed in 10 s; 2 falls rapidly or cannot be lifted. Grip: handshake 0 equal strong; 1 weak but some grip; 2 no grip / no movement.
findings.research: Nazliel B et al. Stroke. 2008; LAPSS motor items / LAMS EMS cards
findings.do_not_change: 0–5 sum, common cutoff ≥4

findings.name: FAST-ED Scale
findings.current: Face Normal/Mild/Moderate-to-severe; speech Absent/Mild/Severe-mute; eye Absent/Partial/Forced. No show-teeth, no 10 s arm hold, no speech prompt, no how to test gaze or extinction. Arm and denial labels are closer to NIHSS.
findings.problem: Mild vs moderate/severe face and mild vs severe speech are NIHSS mappings, not bedside findings. Cannot distinguish partial vs forced gaze without a pursuit exam. Denial names extinction vs not recognizing the hand but not how to apply bilateral simultaneous stimulation.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–2 values as coded. Face: show teeth or smile (NIHSS face mapping). Arm helpText: eyes closed, arms out palms up 10 s. Speech: name 3 objects and follow a 1-step command or repeat a sentence; 0 normal; 1 mild–moderate but some meaningful speech; 2 mute, global aphasia, or incomprehensible. Eye: follow finger full left–right; partial = cannot cross midline; forced = locked, cannot overcome. Denial: visual or tactile BSS; then ‘Whose arm is this?’
findings.research: Lima FO et al. Stroke. 2016 Table 1 (NIHSS mapping); EMS FAST-ED cards
findings.do_not_change: five-item 0–2 values as coded, sum, ≥4 cutoff. Do not collapse face to the original paper’s 0–1 without a scoring-logic change

findings.name: CTA Spot Sign Helper (ICH Expansion)
findings.current: Spot sign = ≥1 focus of contrast within hematoma, discontinuous from vessels. SBP still markedly elevated / hard to control. Anticoagulation or coagulopathy with no INR/platelet number. Volume ≥30 mL and 6 h window already numeric.
findings.problem: Common operational rules (≥120 HU, discontinuous from outside vessels, any morphology, no matching NCCT calcium) are missing so mimics get scored. Markedly elevated SBP and coagulopathy have no cutoff.
findings.suggested_change: Keep booleans/weights. spotSign helpText: arterial-phase CTA ≥1 focus of contrast pooling in the hematoma, discontinuous from vessels, attenuation ≥120 HU (or ≥2× hematoma), any size/morphology; exclude calcium on NCCT. bpUncontrolled: e.g. SBP still ≥150–180 mmHg or not at local ICH target (often SBP <140). anticoag: warfarin/DOAC/heparin, or INR >1.4 or platelets <100 ×10⁹/L (local reversal thresholds supersede).
findings.research: Demchuk AM et al. Lancet Neurol. 2012 PREDICT; common ≥120 HU + discontinuous-from-vessel definitions; AHA ICH BP targets
findings.do_not_change: spot = 2 points, clinical tally, CTA-absent branch

findings.name: 4AT Delirium Screen
findings.current: Alertness Normal vs Clearly abnormal (with <10 s sleepiness). AMT4 already lists age, DOB, place, year. Attention is months backwards with ≥7 months. Acute change Yes/No with no window.
findings.problem: Cannot finish the exam from the UI. Missing what clearly abnormal looks like; the months-backwards script (start at December, one prompt); Item 4’s 2-week / last-24-h rule (without it, chronic dementia scores 4).
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/4, 0–2, 0/4 values. Alertness: 0 = fully alert or sleepy <10 s after waking then normal; 4 = drowsy, hypervigilant, restless, agitated, or combative even if fluctuating. Attention: ‘Please tell me the months backwards, starting at December’; one prompt allowed; 0 = ≥7 months; 1 = starts but <7 or refuses; 2 = untestable. Acute: significant change or fluctuation in alertness, cognition, or other mental function (e.g. paranoia, hallucinations) arising over the last 2 weeks and still evident in the last 24 h (informant/staff/notes).
findings.research: Bellelli G et al. Age Ageing. 2014; www.the4at.com user guide / printable form (free to reproduce with attribution)
findings.do_not_change: item values, sum 0–12, bands 0 / 1–3 / ≥4

findings.name: AD8 Dementia Screening Interview
findings.current: Eight reasonably full stems. Change-from-prior is only in pearls. No informant-vs-self note on the inputs.
findings.problem: AD8 scores change over several years, not lifelong traits. Without that stem, a lifelong poor memory or always-homebody hobby pattern is over-scored.
findings.suggested_change: Add shared helpText or prefix: Has there been a CHANGE in the last several years caused by thinking/memory problems? Yes = change; No = no change. Prefer an informant. Keep the eight stems; optional modest expansions (q4 TV remote/microwave; q6 bills, taxes, checkbook). Do not reprint beyond published AD8 items without Washington University permission.
findings.research: Galvin JE et al. Neurology. 2005; Washington University AD8 (clinical use with attribution)
findings.do_not_change: eight yes = 1, cutoff ≥2

findings.name: PC-PTSD-5 Screen
findings.current: Trauma gate is ‘Lifetime trauma exposure criterion.’ Five symptom stems lack ‘in the past month.’
findings.problem: Symptoms are a past-month screen after a defined DSM-5 trauma gate. Lifetime nightmares/avoidance without the window over-calls; trauma exposure criterion is not administrable.
findings.suggested_change: Keep six yes/no. trauma helpText: NCPTSD gate — Sometimes things happen that are unusually frightening, horrible, or traumatic (serious accident/fire, physical or sexual assault, disaster, war, seeing someone killed/seriously injured, or a loved one dying by homicide/suicide). Have you ever experienced this kind of event? Prefix q1–q5 with ‘In the past month:’ using the existing stems. Optional q5 completion: for the event(s) or problems they caused.
findings.research: Prins A et al. J Gen Intern Med. 2016; VA National Center for PTSD PC-PTSD-5 (public)
findings.do_not_change: trauma gate must be true before counting 0–5, cutoff ≥3

findings.name: Opioid Risk Tool (ORT)
findings.current: Several yesNo chips show a single points value. calculate() applies sex-specific Webster weights (FH alcohol F1/M3, FH illegal F2/M3, sexual abuse F3/M0). User sees 1 for FH alcohol even when a man scores 3, and 3 for male sexual abuse that actually adds 0.
findings.problem: Point chips contradict the sex-specific math. Bedside user cannot tell which items change by sex.
findings.suggested_change: Do not change calculate() weights. helpText on sex: ORT is sex-specific. Labels/helpText: FH alcohol +1 F / +3 M; FH illegal +2 F / +3 M; FH Rx +4 both; personal alcohol +3, illegal +4, Rx +5 both; age 16–45 +1; preadolescent sexual abuse +3 F / +0 M; ADHD/OCD/bipolar/schizophrenia +2; depression +1. Prefer dropping misleading pointsYes on sex-specific items (schema allows null) so chips are not trusted.
findings.research: Webster LR, Webster RM. Pain Med. 2005 ORT table
findings.do_not_change: sex-specific sum, bands 0–3 / 4–7 / ≥8

findings.name: 2010 ACR/EULAR Rheumatoid Arthritis Classification
findings.current: Joint bins name large / small without listing joints. Serology is negative / low-positive / high-positive. High-positive >3× ULN is only in pearls. Duration ≥6 weeks is clear.
findings.problem: Cannot score the 0–5 joint domain without the small/large lists and DIP/1st CMC/1st MTP exclusions. Cannot split low vs high serology without the 3× ULN rule on the input.
findings.suggested_change: Joints helpText: Large = shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, ankles. Small = MCPs, PIPs, 2nd–5th MTPs, thumb IPs, wrists. Do not count DIPs, 1st CMC, or 1st MTP. Count a joint if tender or swollen; >10 joints needs ≥1 small. Serology: negative = ≤ULN for both RF and ACPA; low-positive = >ULN but ≤3× ULN; high-positive = >3× ULN for RF or ACPA. Optional duration: duration of synovitis, not of pain alone.
findings.research: Aletaha D et al. Ann Rheum Dis / Arthritis Rheum. 2010 Table 3 footnotes
findings.do_not_change: domain points 0–5 / 0–3 / 0–1 / 0–1, ≥6 + swollen-joint entry + no better alternative

findings.name: 2019 EULAR/ACR SLE Classification
findings.current: Options are disease words (Fever, Leukopenia, Joint involvement, Antiphospholipid antibodies) with no numbers or attribution rule. ANA ≥1:80 and proteinuria >0.5 g/24 h are already numeric. Highest item per domain is in the field label.
findings.problem: Hidden cutoffs: fever >38.3°C; WBC <4.0×10⁹/L; platelets <100×10⁹/L; joints = synovitis ≥2 joints or tenderness ≥2 + ≥30 min stiffness; aPL = medium/high aCL or anti-β2GPI or LAC. Hemolysis components and ‘item must be attributable to SLE’ are omitted.
findings.suggested_change: Keep domain maxima and points. Constitutional: fever >38.3°C, not infection. Heme: leukopenia WBC <4.0×10⁹/L; thrombocytopenia <100×10⁹/L; hemolysis = reticulocytosis, low haptoglobin, ↑indirect bili or LDH, AND positive Coombs. MSK: synovitis (swelling/effusion) in ≥2 joints, or tenderness in ≥2 joints plus ≥30 min morning stiffness. aPL: LAC and/or aCL IgA/G/M medium–high (>40 U or >99th percentile) and/or anti-β2GPI IgA/G/M. Global: count an item only if SLE is the most likely explanation; items need not be simultaneous; only the highest item per domain.
findings.research: Aringer M et al. Ann Rheum Dis / Arthritis Rheumatol. 2019 definitions table
findings.do_not_change: ANA entry, domain weights, classify if ANA + total ≥10 + ≥1 clinical domain

findings.name: 2016 ACR/EULAR Primary Sjögren Classification
findings.current: Entry is Dry eye or dry mouth. Item cutoffs (focus score ≥1, OSS ≥5, van Bijsterveld ≥4, Schirmer ≤5 mm/5 min, UWS ≤0.1 mL/min) are already numeric. Exclusions only in pearls.
findings.problem: Official entry is a positive answer to ≥1 AECG dryness question (or ESSDAI ≥1), not undifferentiated sicca. Without the five questions, entry is over-called. Exclusion list is easy to miss.
findings.suggested_change: entrySicca helpText: positive if daily dry eyes >3 months, sand/gravel sensation, tear substitutes >3×/day, daily dry mouth >3 months, or needs liquids to swallow dry food (AECG questions) — or ESSDAI ≥1. Apply exclusions first (head/neck radiation, active HCV, AIDS, sarcoid, amyloid, GVHD, IgG4-RD). Optional: note OSS and van Bijsterveld are alternative ocular-staining methods (do not change calculate() additivity).
findings.research: Shiboski CH et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2016; AECG sicca questions
findings.do_not_change: weights 3/3/1/1/1/1, ≥4 + sicca entry

findings.name: 2013 ACR/EULAR Systemic Sclerosis Classification
findings.current: PAH and/or ILD with no test. Raynaud and abnormal nailfold capillaries unnamed. Skin/fingertip options are otherwise named; proximal-to-MCP helpText is present.
findings.problem: 2013 definitions: PAH by RHC (or equivalent echo) and ILD by HRCT or PFTs — not a clinical impression. Raynaud is biphasic/triphasic color change; nailfold is dilated loops/dropouts on capillaroscopy.
findings.suggested_change: pahIld helpText: PAH documented by RHC (or echo meeting local PAH criteria) and/or ILD on HRCT or restrictive/low-DLCO PFTs. raynaud: episodic biphasic or triphasic digital color change (white/blue/red), witnessed or convincing history. nailfold: dilated capillary loops and/or avascular dropouts on capillaroscopy (or high-magnification dermatoscope).
findings.research: van den Hoogen F et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2013 item definitions
findings.do_not_change: mutually exclusive skin + fingertip points, other weights, ≥9

findings.name: 2012 ACR/EULAR Polymyalgia Rheumatica Classification
findings.current: Scoring items present (stiffness >45 min numeric). Required setting age ≥50 + bilateral shoulder aching + abnormal CRP/ESR is only in description/pearls — not an input (unlike GCA/GPA). Ultrasound abnormal shoulder/hip undefined.
findings.problem: User can classify PMR without the mandatory clinical setting. Abnormal US is a specific list (subdeltoid bursitis / biceps tenosynovitis / GH synovitis; hip synovitis / trochanteric bursitis).
findings.suggested_change: Add three entry yes/no (or one combined) with helpText: required to classify: age ≥50 AND bilateral shoulder aching AND CRP or ESR above ULN — not point-scored. US helpText: abnormal shoulder = subdeltoid bursitis, biceps tenosynovitis, and/or glenohumeral synovitis; abnormal hip = coxofemoral synovitis and/or trochanteric bursitis. Keep 4 vs 5 threshold selector.
findings.research: Dasgupta B et al. Arthritis Rheum. 2012
findings.do_not_change: item weights, clinical ≥4 vs US ≥5 logic. Adding non-scoring entry checkboxes does not change points

findings.name: 2022 ACR/EULAR Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis Classification
findings.current: Seven clinical/lab yes/no with good eosinophil cutoff. Unlike sibling GPA/MPA calculators, no small/medium-vessel vasculitis diagnosed and mimics excluded entry. Hematuria has no dipstick/RBC definition.
findings.problem: 2022 EGPA is applied only after a clinical vasculitis diagnosis. Without an entry gate, asthma + eosinophilia (8 points) classifies EGPA in patients who never had vasculitis. Hematuria is a subtracting item with no operational floor.
findings.suggested_change: Add the same non-scoring entry yes/no used in GPA/MPA. hematuria helpText: dipstick ≥1+ or >5 RBC/HPF, not explained by infection/stone (published item is hematuria).
findings.research: Grayson PC et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2022 (entry: small/medium-vessel vasculitis)
findings.do_not_change: signed weights, ≥6 threshold

findings.name: 2022 ACR/EULAR Giant Cell Arteritis Classification
findings.current: ESR/CRP, age, sudden visual loss, jaw claudication are scorable. Abnormal temporal artery examination, halo sign, and bilateral axillary involvement have no exam/imaging anchors.
findings.problem: Cannot mark abnormal TA without pulse/tenderness/cord. Halo sign is homogeneous hypoechoic wall edema on TA US, not any US abnormality. Axillary item is bilateral wall thickening/stenosis/occlusion.
findings.suggested_change: abnormalTA helpText: absent or diminished pulse, tenderness, or cord-like thickening of a temporal artery. tabHalo: TAB with vasculitis (mononuclear infiltrate ± giant cells), or halo sign = homogeneous hypoechoic mural thickening of the temporal artery on US. axillary: bilateral axillary artery wall thickening, stenosis, or occlusion on US/CTA/MRA.
findings.research: Ponte C et al. Arthritis Rheumatol. 2022
findings.do_not_change: item weights, age ≥50 AND ≥6

findings.name: 2022 ACR/EULAR Takayasu Arteritis Classification
findings.current: Number of affected arterial territories 0/1/2/≥3 with no list (pearls name some vessels). Paired artery involvement undefined. Age ≤60 and BP ≥20 mmHg are clear.
findings.problem: Territories are a closed 9-vessel set. Paired involvement is vasculitis of both members of a paired branch set. Without the list, 1 vs ≥3 is not scorable.
findings.suggested_change: territories helpText: count luminal damage (stenosis/occlusion/aneurysm) among 9 territories: thoracic aorta, abdominal aorta, mesenteric, left carotid, right carotid, left subclavian, right subclavian, left renal, right renal. pairedArteries: both arteries of a paired set (e.g. both carotids, both subclavians, or both renals).
findings.research: Grayson PC et al. Ann Rheum Dis / Arthritis Rheumatol. 2022 (nine-territory composite; paired branch arteries)
findings.do_not_change: sex/clinical/imaging weights, age ≤60 AND LVV imaging AND ≥5

findings.name: CASPAR Psoriatic Arthritis Classification (2006)
findings.current: Nail dystrophy and juxta-articular new bone are bare yes/no. Entry says joint/spine/enthesis. Current psoriasis already 2 vs history 1.
findings.problem: Nail dystrophy is onycholysis, pitting, or hyperkeratosis. Juxta-articular new bone is ill-defined ossification near joint margins of hands or feet (not osteophytes). Inflammatory articular disease is synovitis/enthesitis/spondylitis, not mechanical pain.
findings.suggested_change: nail helpText: onycholysis, pitting, or hyperkeratosis (current). juxtaBone: ill-defined ossification near joint margins on hand/foot radiographs (not osteophytes). entry: inflammatory joint, spine, or entheseal disease (synovitis, spondylitis, or enthesitis) — not degenerative pain. Optional RF: negative by any method except latex (typically nephelometry).
findings.research: Taylor W et al. Arthritis Rheum. 2006 CASPAR
findings.do_not_change: psoriasis 2/1/1/0 mutually exclusive bins, other +1, ≥3 + entry

findings.name: ASAS Axial Spondyloarthritis Classification (2009)
findings.current: All SpA features are unlabeled yes/no. Entry (back pain ≥3 months, onset <45) is present. HLA-B27 is a lab fact.
findings.problem: Inflammatory back pain, MRI/x-ray sacroiliitis, NSAID response, family history, and elevated CRP each have published operational rules. A yes on IBP or sacroiliitis without those rules is not ASAS-scorable.
findings.suggested_change: ibp helpText: ASAS IBP if ≥4 of 5 — onset <40 y, insidious, improves with exercise, no improvement with rest, night pain (better on getting up). sacroiliitis: radiographic modified New York (bilateral ≥grade 2 or unilateral ≥grade 3) or MRI bone-marrow edema highly suggestive of SpA (ASAS: ≥2 lesions on one slice or 1 lesion on ≥2 slices). nsaidResponse: back pain much better within 24–48 h of full-dose NSAID. familySpA: 1st- or 2nd-degree relative with AS/axSpA, psoriasis, acute uveitis, reactive arthritis, or IBD. crp: above lab ULN, attributed to SpA. Optional arthritis: synovitis diagnosed by a physician.
findings.research: Rudwaleit M et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2009 parts I–II; ASAS MRI sacroiliitis definition
findings.do_not_change: imaging arm = sacro + ≥1 feature; clinical arm = HLA-B27 + ≥2 other; entry required

findings.name: ASAS Peripheral Spondyloarthritis Classification (2011)
findings.current: Preceding infection with no organism/time window. IBP and enthesitis unlabeled (axial calculator has the same IBP gap; here enthesitis is not limited to heel).
