findings.problem: Category-A preceding infection is the reactive-arthritis window (urethritis/cervicitis or diarrhea within ~1 month). IBP needs the ASAS 4/5 rule. Enthesitis here is any enthesis, not only heel.
findings.suggested_change: infection helpText: usually urethritis/cervicitis or acute diarrhea within 1 month before arthritis (reactive-arthritis pattern). ibp: same ASAS 4/5 helpText as axSpA. enthesitis: physician-diagnosed enthesitis at any site (not only heel).
findings.research: Rudwaleit M et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2011 peripheral SpA criteria
findings.do_not_change: entry AND (≥1 cat A OR ≥2 cat B)

findings.name: 2017 EULAR/ACR Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy Classification
findings.current: Skin options are names only (Gottron papules / Gottron sign / heliotrope). Weakness pattern items are otherwise specific. Tool already warns it scores the single highest lesion.
findings.problem: Papules vs sign vs heliotrope change the weight (e.g. ~2.1 vs 3.3 vs 3.1 without biopsy). A user who cannot picture the rashes will pick the wrong highest lesion.
findings.suggested_change: option.description: Gottron papules = erythematous to violaceous papules over DIP/PIP/MCP extensor surfaces; Gottron sign = macular erythema over knuckles/elbows/knees without papules; heliotrope = violaceous periorbital rash ± edema. Keep highest-only helpText. Optional enzymes: CK, LDH, AST, or ALT above ULN, not explained by liver disease alone.
findings.research: Lundberg IE et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2017 Table 2 / glossary
findings.do_not_change: path-specific weights, highest-skin-only behavior, thresholds 5.5 / 6.7 (probable) as coded

findings.name: 2023 ACR/EULAR Antiphospholipid Syndrome Classification
findings.current: Moderate- vs high-titer and provoked / high-risk CVD / suspected vs established microvascular are category names. Evidence text cites ELISA 40–79 vs ≥80 but that is not on the inputs. No entry clinical + lab within 3 years. Persistent LAC undefined.
findings.problem: Cannot choose moderate vs high without unit cutoffs; cannot mark provoked VTE or high-risk CVD without the paper’s risk-factor lists; cannot separate suspected vs established microvascular; cannot mark persistent LAC without the 12-week repeat.
findings.suggested_change: Keep domain options and additive isotypes as coded (do not fix the known highest-cluster simplification). Titers helpText: moderate ELISA ~40–79 U; high ≥80 U (or lab 99th percentile). LAC persistent = positive on two occasions ≥12 weeks apart. VTE/arterial: RESEARCH official high-risk VTE vs provoked lists and high-risk CVD profile from the 2023 table. Microvascular: suspected = livedo/livedo racemosa, aPL nephropathy, alveolar hemorrhage without histopathology; established = biopsy- or unequivocal imaging-proven. Optional entry note: ≥1 clinical and ≥1 lab criterion within 3 years of each other.
findings.research: Barbhaiya M et al. Arthritis Rheumatol. 2023 definitions/supplement
findings.do_not_change: clinical ≥3 AND lab ≥3; do not collapse solid-phase isotypes unless a scoring-logic change is separately approved

findings.name: Sydney (2006) APS Classification
findings.current: Obstetric morbidity (Sydney definitions) with no list. Thrombosis unlabeled. aCL medium or high titer without GPL/MPL. Persistence ≥12 weeks is present.
findings.problem: The three obstetric clauses, exclusion of superficial vein thrombosis, and titer floors are the actual criteria. A yes on obstetric morbidity is not Sydney-scorable.
findings.suggested_change: obstetric helpText: ≥1 unexplained death of a morphologically normal fetus ≥10 weeks; or ≥1 premature birth <34 weeks due to eclampsia/severe pre-eclampsia or placental insufficiency; or ≥3 consecutive unexplained embryonic losses <10 weeks (anatomic/hormonal/chromosomal causes excluded). thrombosis: objectively confirmed arterial, venous, or small-vessel thrombosis; exclude superficial venous thrombosis. acl: IgG or IgM >40 GPL/MPL or >99th percentile. b2gpi: IgG or IgM >99th percentile.
findings.research: Miyakis S et al. J Thromb Haemost. 2006
findings.do_not_change: ≥1 clinical AND ≥1 lab AND persistent ≥12 weeks

findings.name: ICBD 2013 Behçet Disease Classification
findings.current: Seven yes/no names. ISG in the same file at least lists eye and skin types; ICBD does not. Pathergy has no method.
findings.problem: Ocular/skin/neuro/vascular are not any lesion. Pathergy is a specific 24–48 h needle test. Oral/genital aphthosis should be recurrent ulcers, not a single sore.
findings.suggested_change: ocular: anterior/posterior uveitis or retinal vasculitis (cells in vitreous count). oral/genital: recurrent oral/genital aphthous ulcers (minor, major, or herpetiform), observed or reliable history. skin: erythema nodosum, papulopustular, or acneiform lesions observed by a physician. neuro: parenchymal (meningoencephalitis) or vascular CNS Behçet — not isolated headache. vascular: venous or arterial thrombosis or aneurysm (including pulmonary artery). pathergy: 20–22 G needle, oblique intradermal forearm; read at 24–48 h; positive = papule ≥2 mm.
findings.research: International Team for the Revision of ICBD. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2014

findings.name: ISG 1990 Behçet Disease Classification
findings.current: Recurrent oral ulceration (required). Evidence summary states ≥3 episodes in 12 months, but the input does not. Pathergy unlabeled. Eye/skin lists are better than ICBD.
findings.problem: ISG oral item is at least three episodes in 12 months. Pathergy technique omitted (same as ICBD).
findings.suggested_change: oral label/helpText: recurrent oral ulceration — minor/major/herpetiform aphthae at least 3 times in 12 months (mandatory). pathergy helpText: same 20–22 G, 24–48 h, papule ≥2 mm as ICBD. Optional genital: aphthous ulceration or scarring, documented by physician or patient.
findings.research: International Study Group for Behçet’s Disease. Lancet. 1990
findings.do_not_change: oral mandatory + ≥2 of genital/eye/skin/pathergy

findings.name: SAH Vasospasm / DCI Risk Window
findings.current: mFisher 1–4 labels say thin vs thick SAH ± IVH. No millimeter/cistern rule. Day window helpText exists.
findings.problem: Thin vs thick is the whole grade. Juniors still need the Frontera rule of thumb.
findings.suggested_change: mFisher helpText: thick = cisternal blood completely filling ≥1 cistern or vertical layer ≥1 mm; thin = all blood <1 mm. IVH = any intraventricular blood.
findings.research: Frontera JA et al. Neurosurgery. 2006 modified Fisher
findings.do_not_change: day bands, mFisher 0–4 values, nimodipine/secured flags

findings.name: Graduated Return-to-Play (Concussion)
findings.current: Options are official stage titles. Full activity examples live only in calculate() output after a stage is chosen.
findings.problem: Stage 2 vs 3 vs 4 (no resistance vs running vs progressive resistance, still no contact) is the decision. A one-line option.description would make the picker itself scorable.
findings.suggested_change: Add option.description from CISG: 1 = daily activities that do not provoke symptoms; 2 = walking/stationary bike, no resistance; 3 = running/skating drills, no head impact; 4 = complex training ± resistance, still no contact; 5 = normal training including contact after medical clearance; 6 = competition if stage 5 was asymptomatic.
findings.research: McCrory P et al. BJSM 2017; Patricios JS et al. BJSM 2023 RTP stages
findings.do_not_change: six stages, 24 h / RTL / clearance gates

findings.name: ESSDAI (Sjögren Activity)
findings.current: Each domain is No activity / Low / Moderate / High with level × weight chips. No helpText or option.description. Biological correctly maxes at 2; CNS still offers unused Low.
findings.problem: Cannot assign low vs moderate vs high without Seror Table 3 (fever °C, node cm, 28-joint synovitis, CK×ULN, cytopenia bins, IgG, DLCO/FVC, proteinuria). CIWA-style ordinals.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–2/0–3 values and level×weight. helpText: score current Sjögren activity not damage/infection. option.description from Seror Table 3: Constitutional Low = fever 37.5–38.5°C and/or night sweats and/or involuntary 5–10% weight loss; Moderate = fever >38.5 or loss >10%. Lymph Low = nodes ≥1 cm (≥2 cm inguinal); Moderate = ≥2 cm (≥3 cm inguinal) ± splenomegaly; High = current B-cell malignancy. Glandular Low = parotid ≤3 cm; Moderate = >3 cm. Articular Low = peripheral arthralgia + AM stiffness >30 min; Moderate = 1–5/28 synovitis; High = ≥6/28. Cutaneous Low = EM; Moderate = limited vasculitis/purpura feet-ankles or SCLE; High = diffuse vasculitis/ulcers. Pulmonary Low = cough or ILD without dyspnoea/normal PFT; Moderate = NYHA II or DLCO 40–69% or FVC 60–79%; High = NYHA III–IV or DLCO <40% or FVC <60%. Haematological Low = neutrophils 1000–1500 and/or Hb 10–12 and/or Plt 100–150 or lymph 500–1000 (autoimmune only). Biological Low = clone or IgG 16–20 g/L; Moderate = cryo or IgG >20 or recent hypocomplement/IgG fall. RESEARCH renal/muscular/PNS/CNS full Table 3; CNS official has no level 1 (describe Low as not used).
findings.research: Seror R et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2010;69:1103 Table 3; Seror 2015 ESSDAI/ESSPRI user guide
findings.do_not_change: domain weights, maxLevel 2 vs 3, level×weight sum 0–123, bands <5 / 5–13 / ≥14; do not drop CNS level-1 from the select

findings.name: BILAG-2004 (Domain Grades)
findings.current: A–E letters: Never / Inactive prior / Mild / Moderate / Severe. No helpText. Pearls admit the glossary is required.
findings.problem: A–C are mild/moderate/severe with no organ rules. Cannot grade a domain without the copyrighted 97-item BILAG-2004 glossary. D vs E is the only operational pair. UI looks administrable and is not.
findings.suggested_change: Keep A–E values. Do not reprint the glossary. helpText: assign letters only from a completed official BILAG-2004 worksheet — do not grade from mild/moderate/severe intuition. option.description: A = would typically start high-dose steroids/IS for that organ; B = moderate therapy change; C = mild stable; D = previous involvement now inactive; E = never involved.
findings.research: Isenberg DA et al. Rheumatology 2005 BILAG-2004; official BILAG-2004 glossary (University of Birmingham, copyright — point to the form)
findings.do_not_change: nine domains, A–E values, any-A / any-B / C-only / D–E classification; do not add A=12 numeric conversion

findings.name: BASMI (2-step)
findings.current: Five numeric fields; 2-step conversion cutoffs already in helpText. No manoeuvre, landmarks, or L/R averaging method.
findings.problem: Bins are scorable; the exam is not. User still needs an ASAS/Jenkinson card to produce tragus-to-wall, modified Schober, side flexion, cervical rotation, and intermalleolar distance.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/2 cutoffs. Expand helpText: tragus — heels/buttocks/scapulae against wall, feet ~30 cm, chin tucked, rigid ruler, mean L/R. schober — mark lumbosacral junction (dimples of Venus) and 10 cm above (classic also 5 cm below); flex fully; score the increase. cervical — supine goniometer on forehead, mean L/R. sideFlex — fingertip-to-floor or skin-distraction difference, mean L/R, no trunk rotation. imd — supine, knees extended, abduct; medial malleoli distance.
findings.research: Jenkinson TR et al. J Rheumatol. 1994 BASMI; ASAS/ASIF BASMI measurement SOP
findings.do_not_change: 2-step 0/1/2 bins, five-item sum 0–10, bands 0–2 / 3–5 / 6–10; do not switch to linear BASMI-10

findings.name: ADA Type 2 Diabetes Risk Test
findings.current: Normal / Overweight / Obese / Very obese band. helpText names the ADA height-weight chart but gives no BMI or lb numbers. Age, GDM, family, HTN, activity are operational.
findings.problem: Cannot choose overweight vs obese vs very obese without the official chart or BMI equivalents.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–3. Expand weight helpText: official ADA uses height-specific lb chart (diabetes.org/diabetes/risk-test). Approximate BMI if no chart: <25 = 0; 25–29.9 = 1; 30–39.9 = 2; ≥40 = 3 (CDC/digital ADA). Optional: put those BMI bands on the option labels. Do not add a height field.
findings.research: ADA Diabetes Risk Test (diabetes.org); Bang H et al. Ann Intern Med. 2009; CDC how-your-test-is-scored BMI mapping
findings.do_not_change: age/sex/GDM/family/HTN/activity points, weight 0–3, ≥5 increased-risk threshold

findings.name: FINDRISC Diabetes Risk Score
findings.current: Family = No / Second-degree only (3) / First-degree (5). High glucose = Ever found to have high blood glucose. Age, BMI, waist cm, activity ≥30 min, veg, BP meds already numeric.
findings.problem: First- vs second-degree relatives are not listed. High-glucose omits official examples (health exam, illness, pregnancy), so GDM/stress hyperglycaemia may be missed.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/3/5 and 0/5. Relabel family: No (0); Yes — grandparent, aunt, uncle, or first cousin only (3); Yes — parent, brother, sister, or child (5). highGlu helpText: ever found to have high blood glucose (health examination, during an illness, or during pregnancy).
findings.research: Lindström J, Tuomilehto J. Diabetes Care. 2003; official FINDRISC questionnaire (THL)
findings.do_not_change: point weights (waist 0/3/4, activity +2, veg +1, BP meds +2, glucose +5, family 0/3/5), max 26, 10-year risk bands

findings.name: NIDA Quick Screen
findings.current: Four Never→Daily frequency selects. Alcohol stem has ≥5 men / ≥4 women. Tobacco / nonmedical Rx / illegal drugs have no examples and no past-year patient stem.
findings.problem: Nonmedical prescription and illegal-drug items are not administrable without NIDA examples (opioids/stimulants/sedatives; marijuana/cocaine/heroin/meth/hallucinogens/MDMA).
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–4 values. helpText: In the PAST YEAR, how often have you used…. rx: nonmedical = reasons/doses other than prescribed or someone else’s Rx; includes opioid painkillers, stimulants, sedatives/benzodiazepines. illegal: e.g. marijuana/cannabis, cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine, hallucinogens, MDMA/ecstasy.
findings.research: NIDA Quick Screen V1.0 / NM-ASSIST clinician resource (nida.nih.gov)
findings.do_not_change: 0–4 frequency codes, any-domain > Never = positive, max-frequency display

findings.name: SLICC/ACR Damage Index (SDI)
findings.current: Domain item counts with short helpText lists. Six-month rule only in description/pearls. Gonadal failure has no age cutoff. ESRD=3 is mentioned for renal.
findings.problem: User is asked to count items but missing ≥6-month/irreversible rule on inputs, which items may be scored twice (CVA, MI, AVN), ESRD as exclusive 3 for the renal domain, and gonadal failure = secondary amenorrhea before age 40.
findings.suggested_change: Keep domain maxes. Shared helpText: irreversible damage ≥6 months (or an irreversible event); do not score current activity. Expand domain helpText from Gladman 1996: renal GFR <50% (1), proteinuria ≥3.5 g/24 h (1), ESRD = 3 for the domain not additive; neuro CVA up to 2 if events >6 months apart; gonadal = secondary amenorrhea before 40; diabetes ≥6 months regardless of treatment; malignancy each distinct site max 2, exclude dysplasia. RESEARCH remaining ocular/pulmonary/CV/PVD/GI/MSK/skin item names.
findings.research: Gladman D et al. Arthritis Rheum. 1996;39:363–369 SLICC/ACR Damage Index

findings.name: SLE-DAS (Jesus 2019)
findings.current: Proteinuria >500 mg/24 h, Plt <100, WBC <3, localized rash above the neck, and low C3/C4 are operational. Remaining organ yes/nos are names only.
findings.problem: Heavily weighted items (NPSLE, vasculitis, cardiopulmonary, myositis, serositis, haemolysis) have no definitions. Haemolysis is Coombs+LDH+low haptoglobin, not any anaemia. Arthritis vs SJC dual entry is unexplained.
findings.suggested_change: Keep binaries and coefficients. helpText: arthritis = SLE inflammatory arthritis this visit (still enter SJC28 — both terms are in the formula). hemolytic = anaemia + positive direct Coombs + raised LDH + low haptoglobin. serositis = pleuritis/pericarditis (pain >1 day, rub, or effusion). myositis = proximal weakness + CK/EMG/biopsy, not steroid/statin. RESEARCH Suppl Table S2 for NPSLE, systemic vs mucocutaneous vasculitis, alopecia vs damage, oral/nasal ulcers.
findings.research: Jesus D et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2019;78:365–371 and supplementary Tables S1–S2
findings.do_not_change: 17-item weights, ln(Prot/Plat/WBC) only when flags are Yes, cutoffs ≤2.08 / ≤7.64

findings.name: Lupus Low Disease Activity State (LLDAS)
findings.current: Major organ activity (CNS, vasculitis, nephritis, myositis, etc.); Intolerance of standard IS/antimalarials. SLEDAI number, PGA ≤1 helpText, and prednisone dose are OK.
findings.problem: Franklyn also excludes haemolytic anaemia and GI activity; etc. hides them. Criterion 5 is well-tolerated standard maintenance therapy — patients on no IS can still meet LLDAS.
findings.suggested_change: Keep Yes=fail polarity. majorOrgan helpText: renal, CNS, cardiopulmonary, vasculitis, myositis, fever, haemolytic anaemia, or GI lupus activity — any fails LLDAS even if SLEDAI ≤4. intoleranceIS helpText: fail if current standard maintenance antimalarial/IS/approved biologic is not tolerated; not on IS/HCQ is allowed (answer No); investigational drugs do not count.
findings.research: Franklyn K et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2016;75:1615–1621 LLDAS
findings.do_not_change: AND of six criteria, SLEDAI ≤4, PGA ≤1, prednisone ≤7.5 mg/d

findings.name: DORIS SLE Remission
findings.current: Clinical SLEDAI (exclude serology) with no list of which items to drop. PGA and prednisone numeric; serology-positive correctly allowed.
findings.problem: Clinical SLEDAI = SLEDAI-2K minus only low complement and increased DNA binding. Users may subtract rash/arthritis or forget to drop serology.
findings.suggested_change: cSledai helpText: SLEDAI-2K minus the two serology items only (low complement and increased anti-dsDNA/DNA binding). All clinical items must be 0. Optional PGA helpText: DORIS is PGA <0.5 on the 0–3 SELENA scale (0.5 fails).
findings.research: van Vollenhoven RF et al. Lupus Sci Med. 2021;8:e000538 DORIS 2021
findings.do_not_change: cSLEDAI === 0, PGA < 0.5, complete pred = 0 vs on-tx ≤5, serology not in the AND

findings.name: BVAS v3 (Organ Point Totals)
findings.current: Number boxes 0–system max. Only general lists items (no weights). Description/pearls say enter precomputed points.
findings.problem: Empty organ buckets. New vs persistent items score differently on the official form. Cannot produce a system total without the BVAS v3 worksheet; inputs do not say they are transcription fields.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–max number entry (do not explode 56 items). helpText on every system: transcribe the weighted subtotal from a completed official BVAS v3 form; persistent vs new/worse have different weights. On general, add item weights if license allows (myalgia 1, arthralgia/arthritis 2, fever ≥38.0 2, weight loss ≥2 kg 2) or drop the partial list. RESEARCH item names for the other eight systems from Mukhtyar 2009 / official form.
findings.research: Mukhtyar C et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2009 BVAS v3; official BVAS v3 form (Oxford/Luqmani, typically licensed)
findings.do_not_change: nine system maxima, sum of entered subtotals, educational 0 / 1–7 / 8–15 / ≥16 bands

findings.name: Vasculitis Damage Index (VDI)
findings.current: Organ item counts with typical maxima. Only other has example helpText. ≥3-month rule is in the description only.
findings.problem: Full VDI is 64 dichotomous items. Empty counts are not administrable. Pearls name hearing loss, nasal-bridge collapse, GFR decline but those are not on the matching fields.
findings.suggested_change: Keep count entry. Shared helpText: irreversible items ≥3 months; do not score active BVAS lesions. Per-domain helpText with Exley item names, or transcribe from the official VDI form: ENT hearing loss/nasal-bridge collapse/chronic sinusitis/subglottic stenosis; renal GFR ≤50%/proteinuria ≥0.5 g/d/ESRD; other premature gonadal failure, marrow failure, diabetes, malignancy, chemical cystitis.
findings.research: Exley AR et al. Arthritis Rheum. 1997 Vasculitis Damage Index (64-item glossary)
findings.do_not_change: organ maxima as coded, sum, bands 0 / 1–2 / ≥3

findings.name: Five-Factor Score (revised 2011)
findings.current: Age >65, Cr ≥150 µmol/L (1.7 mg/dL), and ENT-absence helpText are operational. Cardiac insufficiency/cardiomyopathy and GI involvement have no severity.
findings.problem: GI in FVSG is bleeding, perforation, infarction, or pancreatitis — not mild pain. Cardiac is vasculitis-related cardiomyopathy/insufficiency, not incidental CAD.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1. gi helpText: vasculitis-related GI involvement — bleeding, perforation, infarction, or pancreatitis (not isolated mild pain). cardiac helpText: cardiomyopathy or cardiac insufficiency attributable to vasculitis. RESEARCH exact 2011 methods wording.
findings.research: Guillevin L et al. Medicine (Baltimore). 2011;90:19–27; 1996 FFS GI footnote
findings.do_not_change: five binary +1 items, ENT-absence always live, 0 / 1 / ≥2 mortality bands

findings.name: Modified Rodnan Skin Score (mRSS)
findings.current: 17 named sites. Options Uninvolved / Mild thickening / Moderate thickening / Severe (hidebound). No pinch method.
findings.problem: 1 vs 2 vs 3 needs the Khanna pinch/fold technique. Hidebound on 3 confuses tethering with thickness (Khanna 2017 scores thickness, not tethering).
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–3 and 17 sites. Shared helpText: pinch the centre of the area (index+thumb or two thumbs over bone); score thickness not tethering; same examiner serially. option.description: 0 = fine wrinkles, no thickness; 1 = definite thickness, fold easy, fine wrinkles OK; 2 = difficult fold, wrinkles lost; 3 = unable to pinch a fold (thickness, not isolated hidebound tethering).
findings.research: Khanna D et al. J Scleroderma Relat Disord. 2017 mRSS standardization; Clements 1993; SCTC Rodnan training

findings.name: ESSPRI (Sjögren Patient Index)
findings.current: Three 0–10 VAS numbers, no recall window, no 0/10 verbal anchors.
findings.problem: Official ESSPRI is last 2 weeks; 0 = no symptom, 10 = worst imaginable. Without the window patients mix today vs chronic sicca.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on each (or once): last 2 weeks; 0 = no dryness/fatigue/pain, 10 = worst imaginable; ESSPRI is the mean of the three. Optional label suffix (last 2 weeks).
findings.research: Seror R et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2011 ESSPRI; 2015 ESSDAI/ESSPRI user guide
findings.do_not_change: mean of three 0–10 scores, PASS ≤5

findings.name: BASFI (10-item)
findings.current: Short stems (Putting on socks without help, Looking over your shoulder, …) on 0–10 numbers. No 0/10 anchors, no past-week window.
findings.problem: This is the item administrator (a total-only BASFI exists elsewhere). Calin stems and 0 = easy / 10 = impossible are missing; several without-aids / from-lying / one-foot-per-step details stripped.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 10 numeric 0–10 inputs and the mean. Shared helpText: past week; 0 = easy, 10 = impossible. Expand labels to Calin 1994 wording (socks/tights without help or aids; bend from waist to pick up a pen without an aid; high shelf; armless dining chair without hands; off the floor from lying on your back; stand 10 min without discomfort; 12–15 steps without rail, one foot per step; look over shoulder without turning the body; physically demanding activities e.g. physiotherapy/gardening/sports; full day’s activities at home or work).
findings.research: Calin A et al. J Rheumatol. 1994 BASFI
findings.do_not_change: 10-item mean 0–10, bands <4 / 4–7 / ≥7

findings.name: PASDAS (PsA Disease Activity Score)
findings.current: LEI is a bare 0–6 number. Globals 0–100 mm, CRP mg/L, and SF-36 PCS helpText are otherwise adequate. SF-36 correctly total-only.
findings.problem: Leeds Enthesitis Index sites are unnamed, so a user without a precomputed LEI cannot fill the box.
findings.suggested_change: lei helpText: LEI 0–6 tenderness at 6 sites — bilateral lateral epicondyle of humerus, medial femoral condyle, Achilles insertion; 1 if tender. Do not substitute SPARCC/MASES counts.
findings.research: Healy/Helliwell Leeds Enthesitis Index; Helliwell GRACE PASDAS
findings.do_not_change: GRACE formula, VAS 0–100, CRP mg/L, VLDA ≤1.9 / LDA ≤3.2 / high ≥5.4

findings.name: PECARN Head Injury (Simplified)
findings.current: Age <2 vs ≥2. High-risk: 'GCS = 14 or other signs of AMS'; 'Palpable skull fracture (or basilar signs if ≥2y)'. Intermediate mashed: 'LOC ≥5 sec (<2y) or any LOC/vomiting/severe HA/severe mechanism (≥2y)' and 'Non-frontal hematoma (<2y) or history of vomiting/severe HA etc.'
findings.problem: Cannot apply PECARN from the UI. AMS, basilar signs, and severe mechanism are undefined; 'etc.' is a protocol-card tell. Age-specific predictors are OR-bundled so <2y and ≥2y lists bleed (vomiting/HA on both loc and nonfrontal).
findings.suggested_change: Keep five yes/no keys and 0/1/2 branching. gcs14 helpText: PECARN AMS = GCS 14 or agitation, somnolence, repetitive questioning, slow response to verbal communication. palpable: <2y palpable skull fracture; ≥2y hemotympanum, raccoon eyes, Battle sign, CSF oto/rhinorrhea. loc: Yes if <2y LOC ≥5 s, ≥2y any LOC, OR severe mechanism — MVC ejection/death of passenger/rollover; unhelmeted pedestrian/bicyclist struck by motor vehicle; fall >3 ft (<2y) or >5 ft (≥2y); head struck by high-impact object. nonfrontal: drop 'etc.'; label 'Non-frontal hematoma (<2y) or vomiting / severe headache (≥2y)'. notActing helpText: <2y only. Age helpText: blunt trauma, GCS 14–15, within 24 h; exclude trivial injury and GCS ≤13.
findings.research: Kuppermann N et al. Lancet 2009;374:1160–1170 PECARN ciTBI rule (AMS and severe-mechanism footnotes)
findings.do_not_change: keys, yes/no values, high-risk = gcs14 OR palpable → 2, age-specific intermediate OR logic, very-low-risk = 0. Do not add new scored inputs

findings.name: Pediatric GCS
findings.current: Eye 4 Spontaneous / 3 To speech / 2 To pain / 1 None. Verbal mixes infant+child ('5 — Coos/babbles / oriented'). Motor mixes '6 — Normal spontaneous / obeys' and '5 — Withdraws to touch / localizes'. No helpText, no option.description, no untestable path.
findings.problem: Cannot administer pGCS from the UI: which column by age; pain-stimulus method; what oriented/obeys mean; infant motor 5 is withdraws-to-touch not localization; intubated VT; eyes untestable from swelling (C). Same gap as adult GCS, worse because two developmental scales are collapsed.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 4/3/2/1, 5–1, 6–1. Do not add a numeric VT. Verbal helpText: infant descriptors if preverbal/<2 y; child if talking; oriented = name, place, month; ETT/tracheostomy = record VT, do not assign 1 for the tube. Verbal descriptions: 5 coos/babbles or oriented; 4 irritable cry or confused sentences; 3 cries to pain / inappropriate words; 2 moans to pain / incomprehensible; 1 none (exclude tube). Motor helpText: infant 6 = normal spontaneous, 5 = withdraws to touch; child 6 = two-part command, 5 = localizes (hand above clavicle); trapezius/supraorbital for localization; fingernail-bed for flexion vs extension; best arm. Eye: Teasdale 2014 spontaneous → sound → pressure; C/NT if lids swollen, not 1.
findings.research: Reilly PL et al. Childs Nerv Syst 1988 paediatric GCS; James/PALS-ATLS infant vs child table; Teasdale 2014 glasgowcomascale.org stimulus and NT/C/T
findings.do_not_change: option values 1–4 / 1–5 / 1–6, calculate() E+V+M sum, bands ≤8 / 9–12 / 13–15

findings.name: BODE Index (COPD)
findings.current: mMRC options are only '0–1 (0)', '2 (1)', '3 (2)', '4 (3)'. BMI, FEV1 %, and 6-minute-walk already have numeric bins.
findings.problem: Cannot assign mMRC 2 vs 3 vs 4 without the MRC grade card. '0–1' also hides that grades 0 and 1 are different questions collapsed only for BODE points.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0–3. option.description (or expanded labels): 0–1 (0) = grade 0 breathless only with strenuous exercise, grade 1 short of breath hurrying on the level or walking up a slight hill; 2 (1) = walks slower than same-age peers on the level or stops at own pace; 3 (2) = stops after ~100 m or a few minutes on the level; 4 (3) = too breathless to leave the house or breathless dressing/undressing. helpText: modified MRC; pick worst applicable grade, then the BODE point bin.
findings.research: Celli BR et al. NEJM 2004 BODE table; Fletcher/MRC dyspnea scale; GOLD mMRC wording
findings.do_not_change: BMI/FEV1/6MWD cutoffs, dyspnea values 0–3, sum 0–10, quartile bands 0–2 / 3–4 / 5–6 / 7–10

findings.name: Ottawa Ankle Rules
findings.current: Tenderness 'posterior distal 6 cm' lateral/medial malleolus, navicular, base of 5th. Walk 'Unable to bear weight 4 steps both immediately AND in ED'. Zone pain unlabeled anatomically. No helpText.
findings.problem: Official palpation is posterior edge or tip of distal 6 cm, not the anterior ankle. 4 steps = transfer weight twice onto each foot; limping still counts as able. Malleolar vs midfoot zone (pain prerequisite) is undefined.
findings.suggested_change: Keep yes/no keys. postLat/postMed: bone tenderness along the posterior edge or tip of the distal 6 cm (not ATFL/anterior joint). walk helpText: unable to take 4 steps both immediately AND in the ED (4 steps = 2 complete transfers onto each foot; limping allowed); if 4 steps in either setting, score No. malleolarPain: pain in malleolar zone (distal fibula/tibia/talus). midfootPain: midfoot zone (navicular, cuboid, cuneiforms, metatarsal bases). Palpate bone, not soft tissue, at navicular and base of 5th.
findings.research: Stiell IG et al. JAMA 1993/1994 Ottawa Ankle Rules (posterior edge or tip; 4-step definition)
findings.do_not_change: zone select, AND logic (zone pain + tenderness or walk), ankle vs foot x-ray split

findings.name: Ottawa Knee Rules
findings.current: Isolated tenderness of fibular head; isolated tenderness of patella; unable to bear weight 4 steps both immediately AND in ED. Age ≥55 and flex to 90° already explicit.
findings.problem: Same undefined 4-step test as Ottawa Ankle. Isolated patellar tenderness means no other bony tenderness of the knee. Fibular-head tenderness is not required to be isolated — paired wording misleads.
findings.suggested_change: walk helpText as Ottawa Ankle (2 transfers per foot, limping allowed; unable both immediately AND in ED). patella: patellar tenderness only if no other bony tenderness of the knee. fibula: tenderness of the fibular head (need not be the sole site).
findings.research: Stiell IG et al. JAMA 1997 Ottawa Knee Rule
findings.do_not_change: five binary OR → x-ray yes/no

findings.name: NEXUS C-Spine Criteria
findings.current: Five yes/nos: midline posterior cervical tenderness; evidence of intoxication; altered level of alertness; focal neurologic deficit; painful distracting injury. No operational definitions.
findings.problem: Hoffman's methods sheet defines each criterion. Without it, altered alertness, intoxication, and especially distracting injury are not reproducible.
findings.suggested_change: helpText only. midline: pain on palpation of posterior midline from nuchal ridge to T1, or any cervical spinous process (lateral/paraspinal does not count). ams: GCS ≤14; disoriented to person/place/time/events; cannot remember 3 objects at 5 min; delayed/inappropriate response. intox: recent ingestion, exam evidence (odor, slurred speech, ataxia), or tests showing alcohol/drugs affecting alertness (e.g. BAL >0.08%). distracting: long-bone fracture; visceral injury needing surgical consult; large laceration/degloving/crush; large burns; or any injury causing acute functional impairment if judged able to mask neck pain. focal: any new motor or sensory deficit.
findings.research: Hoffman JR et al. Ann Emerg Med 1998 NEXUS physician instruction sheet; Hoffman JR et al. NEJM 2000
findings.do_not_change: five OR → image vs clinically clear

findings.name: Canadian C-Spine Rule
findings.current: One yes/no bundles age≥65 OR dangerous mechanism OR paresthesias. Low-risk lists the five ROM-allowing factors but not rear-end exclusions. Rotate: unable to actively rotate neck 45° left AND right.
findings.problem: Dangerous mechanism is the pocket-card list (fall ≥3 ft/5 stairs, axial load/diving, MVC >100 km/h, rollover, ejection, motorized recreational vehicle, bicycle collision). Simple rear-end excludes pushed into oncoming traffic, bus/large truck, rollover, high-speed impact. 45° is active, patient-performed, both directions.
findings.suggested_change: Keep three yes/nos and algorithm order. highRisk helpText: Yes if age ≥65 or paresthesias or dangerous mechanism (fall ≥3 ft/1 m or 5 stairs; axial load e.g. diving; MVC >100 km/h ~62 mph, rollover, or ejection; motorized recreational vehicle; bicycle collision). lowRisk: any of simple rear-end (with those exclusions), sitting in ED, ambulatory at any time, delayed not-immediate neck pain, absence of midline C-spine tenderness. rotate: patient actively rotates 45° left and 45° right; Yes (unable) if either side fails; do not test if high-risk or no low-risk factor.
findings.research: Stiell IG et al. JAMA 2001 Canadian C-Spine Rule figure footnotes
findings.do_not_change: high-risk → image; else no low-risk → image; else unable 45° → image; else clear. Yes/no keys

findings.name: Parkland Burn Formula
findings.current: TBSA burned unit %. Weight clear. Interpretation correctly clocks first 8 h from the burn.
findings.problem: Parkland %TBSA is partial- plus full-thickness only. Superficial/first-degree erythema is commonly included and inflates volume.
findings.suggested_change: Label 'TBSA burned (2nd + 3rd degree)'. helpText: exclude first-degree/superficial burns; use Rule of Nines, Lund-Browder, or palm≈1% of the patient's palm including fingers.
findings.research: Baxter/Parkland formula teaching; ABA burn-size convention (partial + full thickness)
findings.do_not_change: 4 × kg × %TBSA, half in first 8 h from injury, LR note

findings.name: Rule of Nines (Adult TBSA)
findings.current: Whole-region yes/nos (Head & neck 9%, Right arm 9%, …). Interpretation after scoring mentions palm≈1% and pediatric difference. No input helpText.
findings.problem: Checking Yes assigns the entire region. Partial burns cannot be entered, and first-degree is not excluded. Palm/fraction reminder appears only after a (often wrong) total.
findings.suggested_change: Do not add numeric fraction inputs. helpText on first region (or each): Adult Wallace nines; check Yes only if the entire region is partial- or full-thickness burn; for partial regions leave No and add a mental fraction of the listed % (patient palm including fingers ≈1%); exclude first-degree; children use Lund-Browder. Optional label suffix '(entire region)'.
findings.research: Wallace AB Lancet 1951 rule of nines; ABA TBSA 2nd/3rd only
findings.do_not_change: 9/18/9/18/1 weights and sum

findings.name: Westley Croup Score
findings.current: Retractions None/Mild/Moderate/Severe. Air entry Normal/Decreased/Markedly decreased. LOC Normal (0) / Altered (5). Stridor and cyanosis (none / agitation / at rest) already usable.
findings.problem: Mild vs moderate vs severe retractions have no exam anchors. Westley LOC is disoriented (5) vs normal including sleep (0) — 'Altered' can wrongly score a sleeping child 5.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0–3 / 0–2 / 0 or 5. Retractions descriptions: mild = slight intercostal; moderate = intercostal + subcostal ± tracheal tug; severe = accessory muscles, nasal flaring, or abdominal paradox. Air entry: decreased = reduced but audible; markedly decreased = barely audible / silent chest. Consciousness labels: 'Normal, including sleep (0)' / 'Disoriented (5)'. helpText: asleep but rousable is 0.
findings.research: Westley CR et al. Am J Dis Child 1978; Merck/EBMcalc Westley LOC wording (normal including sleep vs disoriented)
findings.do_not_change: domain values (cyanosis 0/4/5, stridor 0/1/2), sum 0–17, coded mild ≤2 / moderate 3–5 / severe ≥6 bands

findings.name: 4Ts Score for HIT
findings.current: Thrombocytopenia and timing already quote % fall, nadir, and day-5–10 windows. Thrombosis: 'New thrombosis / skin necrosis / acute systemic reaction (2)'. Other: None apparent / Possible / Definite with no examples.
findings.problem: Other causes is the hard 4T and has zero anchors. Acute systemic reaction is specifically an IV UFH bolus reaction, not any fever.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0/1/2. other helpText: Definite (0) e.g. surgery/IABP/CVVH within 72 h, confirmed bacteremia/DIC, chemotherapy, or another drug known to drop platelets; Possible (1) competing cause plausible; None apparent (2) no alternative. thrombosis helpText: 2 = new confirmed thrombosis, skin necrosis, or acute systemic reaction after IV UFH bolus (fever, chills, HTN, tachycardia, dyspnea); 1 = progressive/recurrent thrombosis, non-necrotizing skin lesions, or suspected unproven thrombosis. Optional timing helpText: day 0 = day heparin started.
findings.research: Lo GK et al. J Thromb Haemost 2006 4Ts; Cuker A et al. 4Ts teaching tables
findings.do_not_change: 0–2 per domain, sum 0–8, bands 0–3 / 4–5 / 6–8

findings.name: Padua Prediction Score (VTE Risk)
findings.current: Several items already have numbers (≤1 month, Age ≥70, BMI ≥30). Active cancer, Reduced mobility, Known thrombophilic condition, Ongoing hormonal treatment do not.
findings.problem: Barbar definitions hidden: active cancer = metastases and/or chemo/radiotherapy in 6 months; reduced mobility = anticipated bed rest with bathroom privileges ≥3 days; thrombophilia is a specific list; hormone = estrogen OCP/HRT.
findings.suggested_change: helpText. cancer: local or distant metastases and/or chemotherapy or radiotherapy in the previous 6 months. reducedMob: anticipated bed rest with bathroom privileges (limitation or order) for at least 3 days. thrombophilia: antithrombin, protein C or S deficiency, factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A, or antiphospholipid syndrome. hormone: ongoing estrogen (OCP, HRT) or similar hormonal therapy.
findings.research: Barbar S et al. J Thromb Haemost 2010 Padua model definitions
findings.do_not_change: point weights (3/3/3/3/2/1…), high risk ≥4

findings.name: Caprini Score (VTE Risk)
findings.current: Many items include points and some cutoffs (BMI ≥25, Major surgery >45 min, stroke <1 mo). Minor surgery, Medical patient bedrest, Family history of VTE, Pregnancy/postpartum lack duration / which relatives.
findings.problem: Cannot score minor vs major without the 45-min split. Full Caprini bed rest >72 h is 2 points; this 1-point item needs a duration. Family history is first-degree. Postpartum window usually <1 month.
findings.suggested_change: helpText/labels, keep listed weights. minor surgery = elective surgery <45 min; major already >45 min. bedrest: currently on bed rest (this 1-point item; Caprini also has >72 h as 2 — not separately scored here). familyVte: first-degree relative with VTE. pregnancy: currently pregnant or postpartum <1 month.
findings.research: Caprini JA Dis Mon 2005 RAM; subsequent surgical Caprini checklists
findings.do_not_change: listed item weights, age 1/2/3, interpretation bands. Do not add omitted Caprini items

findings.name: STOP-BANG Sleep Apnea Screen
findings.current: Snoring loudly; Tired/daytime sleepiness; Observed apnea; Pressure (treated HTN). BMI >35, age >50, neck >40 cm/16 in, male are numeric/clear.
findings.problem: Official STOP questions have operational examples (heard through a closed door / partner elbows you; falling asleep while driving or talking; choking/gasping; have or treated for HTN — untreated still counts).
findings.suggested_change: Expand labels to Chung wording; values stay yes/no 1 point. Snore: snore loudly (heard through closed doors, or partner elbows you)? Tired: often tired, fatigued, or sleepy in the daytime (e.g. falling asleep while driving or talking)? Observed: anyone observed you stop breathing, or choke/gasp during sleep? Pressure: high blood pressure (have, or being treated)?
findings.research: Chung F et al. Anesthesiology 2008 STOP; Chung F et al. BJA 2012 STOP-Bang
findings.do_not_change: eight binary points, 0–2 / 3–4 / ≥5 bands. Do not switch neck to sex-specific 17 in/16 in unless scoring is intentionally updated

findings.name: Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME)
findings.current: Dose per administration unit mg; Doses per day; fentanyl option 'Fentanyl patch (mcg/hr → special)' factor 2.4. Methadone 'complex — approx 4–12' with value 4.
findings.problem: CDC 2.4 already converts patch mcg/h → MME/day. Users will enter 25 'mg' × 3 doses × 2.4 or 25 × 24 h. Methadone factor is not a single 4.
findings.suggested_change: dose helpText: oral mg per dose for tablets/liquids; for fentanyl patch enter patch strength in mcg/h and set doses/day = 1 (CDC MME/day = mcg/h × 2.4); do not use this tool to switch opioids. Methadone option helpText: CDC methadone MME is dose-stratified (4/8/10/12); this tool uses 4 as a lower-bound approximation — verify the CDC table.
findings.research: Dowell D et al. MMWR 2022 CDC opioid guideline conversion table
findings.do_not_change: listed factors, daily × factor, 50 / 90 MME bands

findings.name: Finnegan NAS Score (Simplified)
findings.current: Some items have numbers (sleep <3/<2/<1 h, fever bands, RR >60). Cry None/Excessive/Continuous; Moro Normal/Hyperactive/Markedly hyperactive; tremors mild vs mod–severe without body-part anchors. Yawning/sneezing >3–4 have no interval. No observation-window helpText.
findings.problem: Cannot administer Finnegan from the UI: scoring interval (q3–4 h after feeds), cry duration, Moro/tremor exam anchors, yawning/sneezing count per interval, excoriation from rubbing not diaper rash.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values. First-item helpText: score ~q3–4 h after feeding; observe the interval. Cry: excessive high-pitched = hard to console; continuous = throughout the interval / >5 min despite consoling. Moro: hyperactive = jittery hands/feet during Moro with some rest; markedly = jitteriness without rest. Tremors: mild = hands or feet only; mod–severe = arms or legs. yawning/sneezing: >3–4 episodes during this scoring interval. excoriation: skin breakdown from rubbing (chin, nose, elbows, knees, toes), not diaper dermatitis. increasedTone: resistance to passive ROM / head lag as on local FNAST card.
findings.research: Finnegan LP et al. Addict Dis 1975; FNAST instruction sheet (Academy of Neonatal Nursing); MOTHER NAS tremor/Moro operationalizations
findings.do_not_change: item point weights, sum, <8 / ≥8 bands, simplified-educational disclaimer in interpretation

findings.name: Step-by-Step (Febrile Young Infant)
findings.current: Ill-appearing / clinical suspicion of severe infection with no PAT/appearance anchors. Labs numeric (engine applies PCT ≥0.5, CRP >20, ANC >10). Leukocyturia 'positive UA / dipstick LE or nitrite per local def.' Age ≤21 d only in calculate().
findings.problem: Step 1 gestalt gate is not administrable. Age ≤21 d is a hard fail the age field does not announce.
findings.suggested_change: illAppearing helpText: ill/toxic on Pediatric Assessment Triangle (appearance, work of breathing, circulation) or clinician suspicion of invasive infection — not a well, playful infant. ageDays helpText: age ≤21 days automatically fails the low-risk pathway. leukocyturia: LE or nitrite positive on dipstick (or lab UA per local definition). Optional PCT/CRP/ANC helpText stating fail cutoffs 0.5 ng/mL, 20 mg/L, 10 ×10³/µL.
findings.research: Mintegi S et al. / Gomez B et al. Step-by-Step Pediatrics / Arch Dis Child validations
findings.do_not_change: sequential fail logic (ill OR ≤21 d OR UA OR PCT≥0.5 OR CRP>20 OR ANC>10)

findings.name: Bishop Score
findings.current: Dilation cm and effacement % are numeric bins. Station −3 / −2 / −1/0 / +1/+2. Consistency Firm/Medium/Soft. Position Posterior/Mid/Anterior. No helpText.
findings.problem: Original Bishop station is relative to ischial spines (not the −5 to +5 ACOG scale). Firm/medium/soft and cervical position have no one-line exam reminder.
findings.suggested_change: helpText: station = cm relative to ischial spines (original Bishop, not modified −5…+5). Consistency: firm ≈ nasal tip, medium ≈ chin, soft ≈ lips. Position: cervical os in the vagina — posterior / mid-position / anterior.
findings.research: Bishop EH Obstet Gynecol 1964 pelvic scoring
findings.do_not_change: 0–3 / 0–2 bins, sum, unfavorable ≤5

findings.name: Gestational Age & Naegele Due Date
findings.current: LMP year/month/day with no statement that LMP is the first day of the last period.
findings.problem: Using last day of flow systematically shortens GA / EDD.
findings.suggested_change: helpText on LMP day: first day of the last menstrual period (not last day of bleeding).
findings.research: Naegele's rule / Lawson ANZJOG 2021 review
findings.do_not_change: +280-day EDD math, week+day display

findings.name: Naegele's Rule (EDD from LMP)
findings.current: Same LMP split plus Cycle length default 28. Cycle adjustment is good; LMP still unlabeled as first day.
findings.problem: Same first-day pitfall as gestational-age.
findings.suggested_change: LMP helpText: first day of LMP. Cycle helpText: EDD shifts by (cycle − 28) days.
findings.research: Naegele's rule; ACOG dating (early US preferred if uncertain LMP)
findings.do_not_change: 280 + (cycle−28) formula

findings.name: Epworth Sleepiness Scale
findings.current: Eight situations slightly clipped (Sitting inactive in public; As a passenger for 1 hour; Lying down to rest in afternoon; In car, stopped in traffic for minutes). 0–3 doze-chance anchors are present.
findings.problem: Official ESS parentheticals missing. ESS is copyrighted (M.W. Johns) — do not invent fuller wording if unlicensed.
findings.suggested_change: If licensed: restore official 8 stems + chance-of-dozing 0–3. If not: keep current stems; helpText 'Official ESS © M.W. Johns — use a licensed form for diagnosis; this is an educational total.' Do not expand into a verbatim unlicensed copy.
findings.research: Johns MW Sleep 1991; M.W. Johns ESS copyright / permission
findings.do_not_change: 8 items × 0–3, total 0–24, interpretation bands

findings.name: Yale Observation Scale (Febrile Child)
findings.current: Item labels already carry McCarthy 1/3/5 observational anchors. No how-to-observe helpText.
findings.problem: Original scale is scored by watching the child before undressing or invasive exam, usually in a parent's arms. Without that, testers score a crying child after labs.
findings.suggested_change: Single helpText on the first item: observe before undressing, otoscopy, or labs; child with caregiver; score what you see, not history; does not replace age-based infant fever pathways.
findings.research: McCarthy PL et al. Pediatrics 1982 observation scales

findings.name: ABC Score (Upper GI Bleed)
findings.current: Altered mental status yes/no with no GCS/disorientation rule. ASA options are 'ASA 1/2/3/≥4' titles only. Urea mmol/L shows BUN conversion only on the <10 band; albumin is g/L with no g/dL; creatinine µmol/L shows ~1.1 mg/dL only on the lowest band.
findings.problem: Cannot apply AMS or ASA class from the UI. Laursen ABC comorbidity points depend on mental status and ASA; users still need an AMS operational definition and ASA I–V examples. US labs report BUN mg/dL, albumin g/dL, and creatinine mg/dL, so incomplete dual-unit labels invite the wrong urea/albumin/Cr band.
findings.suggested_change: Keep point values. ams helpText: 'Altered = GCS <14 or new disorientation/confusion at presentation (same operationalization as AIMS65-style UGIB scores; RESEARCH confirm Laursen 2021 case-report form).' asa helpText or option.description: I healthy; II mild systemic disease; III severe systemic disease with functional limitation; ≥4 constant threat to life / moribund. Dual-label remaining lab bands in helpText: urea 10 mmol/L ≈ BUN 28 mg/dL, 20 mmol/L ≈ BUN 56; albumin 40/30 g/L = 4.0/3.0 g/dL; creatinine 100/150 µmol/L ≈ 1.1/1.7 mg/dL. Pearls already note BUN ≈ urea × 2.8 — lift that onto the urea field.
findings.research: Laursen SB et al. Gut 2021 ABC score methods; ASA PS definitions; Saltzman AIMS65 GCS <14 as the usual UGIB AMS anchor
findings.do_not_change: option values (age 0/1/2, urea 0/2/4, albumin 0/2/5, Cr 0/1/2, AMS +2, cirrhosis +2, malignancy +4, ASA 0/1/3/5), sum, ≤3 / 4–7 / ≥8 bands

findings.name: SBO Strangulation Risk Features
findings.current: Elevated lactate or base deficit (no number). SIRS / systemic toxicity (no criteria). Leukocytosis (WBC >10–12k) as a range. Pain, fever ≥38 °C, HR >100, peritonitis, and CT ischemia examples are already operational.
findings.problem: Cannot tick lactate, SIRS, or leukocytosis without a cutoff. Educational feature-count still needs the numbers a junior would look up (lactate mmol/L, SIRS 4-item list, a single WBC threshold).
findings.suggested_change: helpText only; keep yes/no. lactate: 'Typically lactate >2 mmol/L or worsening base deficit; normal lactate does not exclude early ischemia (already in pearls).' sirs: 'Yes if ≥2 of T <36 or >38 °C; HR >90; RR >20 or PaCO2 <32 mmHg; WBC <4 or >12 ×10³/µL or >10% bands.' leukocytosis: pick one teaching cutoff, e.g. WBC >12 ×10³/µL (drop the 10–12k span).
findings.research: Bone SIRS 1992; Jancelewicz / classic SBO ischemia series; surgical teaching reviews of strangulation signs
findings.do_not_change: eight binary keys, 0–8 count, 0–1 / 2–3 / ≥4 interpretation bands

findings.name: Modified Marshall Organ Failure (Pancreatitis)
findings.current: PaO2/FiO2, creatinine mg/dL, and SBP/fluid/pH bins are numeric and match Atlanta. No CKD/chronic-hypoxemia exception. No FiO2 estimate for patients without an ABG. No helpText.
findings.problem: Revised Atlanta scores acute change: a dialysis patient with baseline Cr 3.0 must not be labeled renal failure 2 on the absolute bin. Non-ventilated patients cannot compute PaO2/FiO2 without an FiO2 estimate from O2 L/min.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–4 values. renal helpText: 'Use acute creatinine. Pre-existing CKD: score further rise from that patient’s baseline (Atlanta); do not assign ≥2 solely for a chronically elevated Cr.' resp helpText: 'PaO2 mmHg / FiO2 (fraction 0.21–1.0). If no ABG, estimate FiO2: RA 0.21; NC 2 L ~0.27, 4 L ~0.30–0.36, 6 L ~0.40; NRB ~0.60–0.95 (Atlanta conversion table).' cv helpText: 'Score off inotropes for 0; fluid-responsive = SBP recovers with volume.'
findings.research: Banks PA et al. Gut 2013 revised Atlanta modified Marshall table and CKD footnote; MDCalc Marshall (pancreatitis)
findings.do_not_change: 0–4 domain values, failure = any organ ≥2, 48 h persistent-failure messaging in interpretation

findings.name: Mannheim Peritonitis Index (Simplified)
findings.current: Organ failure yes/no with no MPI definition (pearls even say confirm locally). Diffuse generalized peritonitis unlabeled beyond the words. Age >50, female, malignancy, >24 h, non-colonic origin, and exudate type are scorable.
findings.problem: Organ failure is worth 7 points and is unscorable without Linder’s kidney/lung/shock/ileus table. Diffuse vs localized is >2 quadrants intraoperatively — not stated.
findings.suggested_change: Keep weights. organFailure helpText: 'MPI organ failure if any: kidney Cr >177 µmol/L (>2.0 mg/dL) or urea >16.7 mmol/L or oliguria <20 mL/h; lung PaO2 <50 mmHg or PaCO2 >50 mmHg; shock (hypo- or hyperdynamic, SBP <90 without inotropes); intestinal obstruction/paralysis ≥24 h or complete mechanical obstruction.' diffuse helpText: 'Generalized = purulent/fecal contamination of >2 abdominal quadrants (not a single-quadrant abscess).'
findings.research: Linder MM et al. Chirurg 1987 MPI; subsequent validation tables reproducing organ-failure footnotes
findings.do_not_change: weights (age 5, female 5, OF 7, malignancy 4, duration 4, non-colonic 4, diffuse 6, exudate 0/6/12), <21 / 21–29 / ≥30 bands

findings.name: Boey Score (Perforated Peptic Ulcer)
findings.current: Major concurrent medical illness yes/no with no disease list. Shock already has SBP <90 or poor perfusion. Delay >24 h is explicit.
findings.problem: Boey’s first factor is a defined comorbidity cluster, not any outpatient diagnosis. Users will over-call well-controlled HTN/DM or under-call severe organ disease.
findings.suggested_change: Keep binary 0/1. medicalIllness helpText: 'Major medical illness in Boey series: severe cardiac, pulmonary, renal, or hepatic disease, or disseminated malignancy — not well-controlled mild comorbidity.' Optional: note original shock was often SBP <100 mmHg; do not change the on-screen <90 unless a formula audit revisits it.
findings.research: Boey J et al. Ann Surg. 1987;205:22-32 risk-factor definitions
findings.do_not_change: three binary points, 0–3 bands, historical mortality text

findings.name: POSSUM Surgical Risk (Simplified Educational)
findings.current: Operation magnitude Minor / Moderate / Major / Major+ with no procedure examples. Respiratory 'limiting dyspnea' has no stair-flight anchor. Cardiac (edema/warfarin, JVP/cardiomegaly), SBP, HR, GCS, and age bands are already numeric or Copeland-like.
findings.problem: Cannot assign 1 vs 2 vs 4 vs 8 surgical points without the Copeland magnitude table (same gap as p-possum in this app). Limiting dyspnea is one flight of stairs in POSSUM.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1/2/4/8. opMagnitude option.description: Minor = hernia, varicose veins, minor perianal/scrotal; Moderate = appendectomy, cholecystectomy, mastectomy, TURP; Major = laparotomy, bowel resection, CBD exploration, major amputation, peripheral vascular; Major+ = aortic, APR, Whipple, liver resection, esophagectomy. resp helpText: 'Limiting dyspnea = one flight of stairs or moderate COPD; rest dyspnea also includes fibrosis/consolidation on CXR.'
findings.research: Copeland GP et al. Br J Surg 1991 POSSUM; Whiteley P-POSSUM; JAMA Surgery POSSUM magnitude tables
findings.do_not_change: option values 1/2/4/8, emergency handling in calculate(), educational (not logistic) total and disclaimer

findings.name: Surgical Risk Helper (ACS-NSQIP style educational)
findings.current: ASA class I–V roman numerals only. Functional status Independent / Partially dependent / Totally dependent with no ADL definition. Age number and procedure-intensity examples are adequate.
findings.problem: Cannot assign ASA without I–V meaning. NSQIP functional status is assistance from another person for ADLs, not 'a bit frail.'
findings.suggested_change: Keep values. asa helpText: 'I healthy; II mild systemic disease; III severe systemic disease; IV constant threat to life; V moribund, not expected to survive without operation.' functional helpText: 'NSQIP: Independent = no assistance from another person for any ADL (devices OK); Partially dependent = some help with ADLs (bathing, dressing, feeding, toileting, transfer); Totally dependent = total assistance for all ADLs. Score the baseline before this illness.'
findings.research: ACS NSQIP User Guide functional-status definitions; ASA PS classification; Bilimoria KY et al. JACS 2013
findings.do_not_change: agePts 0/1/2/3, ASA numeric add, emergency +2, functional 0–2, procedure 0–3, educational bands

findings.name: ASA Physical Status Classification
findings.current: Official titles only (I Normal healthy … VI brain-dead). Operational examples (smoker, BMI, well- vs poorly-controlled DM, MI/CVA time windows, dialysis, sepsis) live only in calculate() after a class is chosen. Emergency (E) definition appears only in the result.
findings.problem: II vs III vs IV cannot be assigned reliably from titles. That is the known ASA inter-rater problem the official example list was written to fix. Examples after scoring do not help the rater choose.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1–6. Move ASA House examples onto option.description (text already in calculate() is close): II current smoker, social alcohol, pregnancy, BMI 30–40, well-controlled DM/HTN, mild lung disease; III poorly controlled DM/HTN, COPD, BMI ≥40, alcohol dependence, pacemaker, reduced EF, ESRD on dialysis, MI/CVA/TIA/stents >3 months; IV recent (<3 months) MI/CVA/TIA/stents, ongoing ischemia, severe valve/EF, sepsis, DIC, ARDS, or ESRD not on regular dialysis; V ruptured aneurysm, massive trauma, intracranial bleed with mass effect. emergency helpText: 'E = delay would significantly increase threat to life or body part.'
findings.research: ASA House of Delegates Statement on ASA Physical Status Classification (examples list, asahq.org)
findings.do_not_change: values 1–6, E modifier logic (asa <6), interpretation bands

findings.name: HEAVEN Difficult Airway Criteria
findings.current: Hypoxemia already states SpO2 ≤93% at attempt. Extremes of size is 'pediatric, obese, acromegaly, etc.' with no age/BMI. Exsanguination is 'anemia / shock affecting O2 reserve' with no Hb. Anatomic, vomit/blood, and neck items list examples.
findings.problem: 'Pediatric' is not ≤8 years; a 12-year-old or BMI 32 vs 40 will be scored inconsistently. Exsanguination in the validation papers is suspected anemia that would accelerate apneic desaturation, not any shock.
findings.suggested_change: Keep six binaries. extremes helpText: 'HEAVEN: age ≤8 years or clinical obesity (some in-hospital series use BMI >35); acromegaly also counts.' exsanguination helpText: 'Suspected acute blood loss or chronic anemia that could accelerate desaturation during RSI apnea (one in-hospital series used Hb <10 g/dL).'
findings.research: Davis DP et al. Air Med J 2017 derivation; Nausheen/Kuzmack HEAVEN validation (age ≤8 or clinical obesity; SpO2 ≤93% at first laryngoscopy)
findings.do_not_change: six equal yes/no criteria, 0 / 1–2 / ≥3 interpretation

findings.name: MACOCHA Score (ICU Intubation Difficulty)
findings.current: Mallampati III or IV yes/no with no class structures or technique. Coma unlabeled. Severe hypoxemia unlabeled. Mouth opening <3 cm is explicit; OSA, cervical mobility, non-anesthesiologist are clinical facts. Pearls note Mallampati may be hard in ICU.
findings.problem: Mallampati is 5 of 12 points and cannot be administered from the UI (what is visible; sitting, tongue out, no phonation). De Jong coma is GCS ≤8; severe hypoxemia is SpO2 <80% — users will substitute GCS <8 or SpO2 <90%.
findings.suggested_change: Keep weights 5/2/1. mallampati helpText: 'Modified Mallampati, mouth fully open, tongue out, no phonation. III = only soft palate + base of uvula; IV = hard palate only. ICU: estimate in a cooperative supine patient if sitting is impossible; if unassessable, do not guess III/IV.' coma: 'GCS ≤8.' hypoxemia: 'SpO2 <80% (De Jong).'
findings.research: De Jong A et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2013;187:832-839 Table 1; Samsoon/Young Mallampati
findings.do_not_change: weights (Mallampati 5, OSA 2, others 1), 0–12 sum, <3 / ≥3 threshold

findings.name: CATCH Rule (Pediatric Head CT)
findings.current: High-risk GCS <15 at 2 h, open/depressed fracture, worsening headache, and dangerous-mechanism examples are operational. 'Any sign of basal skull fracture' lists no signs. Irritability on examination is undefined. Large boggy hematoma is named but not sized (CATCH itself does not use a cm cutoff).
findings.problem: Basal skull is a medium-risk CATCH item that this app’s Canadian CT Head lists (hemotympanum, raccoon, CSF leak, Battle) and CATCH omits. Irritability is inconsolable/persistent on exam, not a fussy toddler who calms with the parent. Pearls already admit simplified wording.
findings.suggested_change: Keep seven binaries. boggy (basal skull) helpText: 'Hemotympanum, raccoon eyes, CSF otorrhea/rhinorrhea, or Battle sign.' irritability helpText: 'Persistent irritability on ED exam, not consolable; CATCH inclusion also used persistent irritability in children <2 years as a minor-head-injury entry criterion.' Optional whenToUse reminder: age <16, GCS 13–15, injury within 24 h with LOC/amnesia/disorientation/vomiting/irritability.
findings.research: Osmond MH et al. CMAJ 2010 CATCH (and CATCH2 basal-skull footnote)
findings.do_not_change: high vs medium grouping, any-high → CT, medium → consider CT, calculate() counts

findings.name: CHALICE Rule (Pediatric Head Injury)
findings.current: LOC >5 min, amnesia >5 min, ≥3 vomits, NAI, seizure, GCS <14 (<15 if <1 y), penetrating/depressed/tense fontanelle, and >5 cm bruise if <1 y are operational. Basal skull signs unnamed. Focal neurology unnamed. Abnormal drowsiness has no 'in excess of expected' qualifier. Dangerous mechanism omits pedestrian/cyclist/occupant and the >40 mph RTC definition.
findings.problem: Cannot examine for CHALICE basal-skull or focal-neuro items from the UI. Drowsiness will over-call post-injury sleepiness. High-speed RTC without the Dunning definition is guessed.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 12 binaries. basalSigns helpText: 'Blood or CSF from ear/nose, panda/raccoon eyes, Battle sign, hemotympanum, facial crepitus, or serious facial injury.' focalNeuro: 'Any motor, sensory, coordination, or reflex abnormality.' drowsiness: 'Drowsiness in excess of that expected by the examining doctor (Dunning).' dangerousMech: 'High-speed RTC (>40 mph / >64 km/h) as pedestrian, cyclist, or occupant; fall >3 m; high-speed projectile/object.'
findings.research: Dunning J et al. Arch Dis Child. 2006 CHALICE definitions; NICE NG232 evolved wording (do not replace CHALICE items with NICE)
findings.do_not_change: any-positive → CT logic, 12 keys, interpretation

findings.name: VExUS Score (Venous Congestion)
findings.current: IVC only <2 vs ≥2 cm. Hepatic S>D / S<D antegrade / S reversal. Portal pulsatility <30 / 30–49 / ≥50%. Intrarenal continuous / biphasic / monophasic. No helpText, no option.description, no probe site, no PF formula.
findings.problem: Cannot acquire or grade VExUS from the UI: IVC site/phase, hepatic S vs D vs S reversal, portal pulsatility fraction (Vmax−Vmin)/Vmax, interlobar biphasic vs D-only monophasic. Grade 2 vs 3 (one vs ≥2 severe patterns) is only in calculate().
findings.suggested_change: Keep IVC 0/1 and vein grades 0/1/2. helpText + option.description: IVC max AP ~1–2 cm from RA–IVC junction (or just distal to HV inflow), long+short axis, largest quiet-breathing diameter (typically end-expiration); <2 cm = VExUS 0 without organ Doppler. Hepatic PW (middle HV): S=systolic antegrade, D=diastolic antegrade; 0=S>D; 1=S<D still antegrade; 2=S reversal. Portal right PV mid-axillary, PF=(Vmax−Vmin)/Vmax×100 for the 30/50% bins. Intrarenal interlobar corticomedullary: 0=continuous; 1=discontinuous biphasic (separate S and D); 2=monophasic D-only. Optional pearl: grade 1=only mild; 2=one severe; 3=≥2 severe with dilated IVC.
findings.research: Beaubien-Souligny W et al. Ultrasound J. 2020 PMID 32270297 IVC ≥2 cm gateway and organ-pattern table; Kidney Medicine 2022 VExUS pearls (hepatic S/D, portal PF, monophasic intrarenal)
findings.do_not_change: IVC 0/1 gateway, hepatic/portal/intrarenal values 0–2, grade 0 if IVC<2 else 1/2/3 by severeCount, interpretation bands

findings.name: LDL / Non-HDL Goal Helper (ASCVD Risk Tier)
findings.current: Low / Borderline-intermediate / High primary / Clinical ASCVD / Very high risk ASCVD (multiple events / high-risk features). helpText only on optional LDL. No 10-year % or Table 4 feature list.
findings.problem: Cannot assign the tier from the UI. AHA/ACC low/borderline/intermediate/high are PCE <5 / 5–<7.5 / 7.5–<20 / ≥20. Clinical ASCVD is a specific event list. Very high-risk is multiple major events or 1 major + multiple high-risk conditions — 'high-risk features' is not operational.
findings.suggested_change: Keep option values and LDL/non-HDL goal numbers. helpText on riskTier: Low = 10-year ASCVD <5%; borderline 5–<7.5%; intermediate ≥7.5–<20% (this helper uses the same <100/<130 goals for both); high primary ≥20%. Clinical ASCVD: ACS, MI, stable/unstable angina, coronary or other arterial revascularization, stroke, TIA, or atherosclerotic PAD including aortic aneurysm. Very high-risk: ≥2 major events or 1 major + multiple high-risk conditions. Major: ACS within 12 mo, MI, ischemic stroke, symptomatic PAD (claudication + ABI <0.85 or prior revasc/amputation). High-risk conditions: age ≥65, HeFH, prior CABG/PCI outside the major event, DM, HTN, CKD eGFR 15–59, current smoking, LDL ≥100 on max statin+ezetimibe, history of HF.
findings.research: Grundy SM et al. Circulation 2019 / JACC 2018 cholesterol guideline Table 4 very high-risk; 10-year PCE risk categories in the same document
findings.do_not_change: option values low/intermediate/high/ascvd/very_high; goal pairs 100/130, 70/100, 55/85; gap-to-goal math

findings.name: AKIN AKI Staging
findings.current: Cr options name ×1.5–1.9, +0.3 mg/dL, ×2–2.9, ×≥3 or ≥4.0 with acute ↑≥0.5 or RRT. UO already has mL/kg/h × hours. whenToUse mentions 48 h; the Cr field does not. No helpText.
findings.problem: AKIN’s defining addition vs RIFLE is an abrupt Cr rise within 48 hours after volume optimization, obstruction excluded. A slow CKD rise can be staged as 1 from the labels. Stage 3 'acute ↑≥0.5' lacks mg/dL on the 0.5.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 0–3 and RRT override. helpText on crStage: AKIN requires the creatinine increase within 48 h (optimize volume; exclude obstruction). Stage 1 = absolute ↑ ≥0.3 mg/dL or ×1.5–1.9 vs baseline (lowest recent Cr). Stage 3 = ×≥3, or Cr ≥4.0 mg/dL with acute rise ≥0.5 mg/dL, or RRT. Optional UO helpText: consecutive hours, preferably Foley, mL/kg/h using current weight.
findings.research: Mehta RL et al. Crit Care. 2007 PMID 17331245 AKIN 48-hour window and stage table
findings.do_not_change: option values 0–3, Math.max(cr, uo), RRT forces stage 3

findings.name: Renal Angina Index (Simplified)
findings.current: Risk examples ICU / transplant / diabetes+sepsis / vent+vasoactives. Injury Cr % change and FO 5/10/15% bins. No FO% formula, no 8–12 h clock, no worse-of-Cr-vs-FO note.
findings.problem: Cannot compute the FO injury arm without FO% = [(intake − output L) / ICU admission weight kg] × 100. Adult 'diabetes + sepsis' is not Basu (ICU=1; transplant=3; vent AND inotrope/vasopressor=5). Original RAI is scored ~8–12 h after ICU admission.
findings.suggested_change: Keep values 1/3/5 and 1/2/4/8 and RAI ≥8. risk helpText: Original pediatric RAI (Basu): 1=ICU admission; 3=solid-organ or stem-cell transplant; 5=mechanical ventilation AND inotrope/vasopressor. This adult educational map: 5 if vent+vasoactives/septic shock; 3 if transplant or multiple comorbidities (e.g. DM+sepsis); 1=ICU/general risk. Score at ~8–12 h of ICU admission. injury helpText: Use the worse of Cr change vs FO. FO% = [(fluid in L − fluid out L) / ICU admission weight kg] × 100. Cr bins vs baseline already on labels.
findings.research: Basu RK et al. Pediatr Nephrol 2012 / Kidney Int 2014 RAI derivation (risk 1/3/5 × injury 1/2/4/8, FO% formula, 12 h timing)
findings.do_not_change: risk × injury product, positive threshold ≥8, option values

findings.name: Furosemide Stress Test (FST)
findings.current: Dose, weight, 2-h UOP, naïve ~1 mg/kg vs exposed ~1.5 mg/kg. 200 mL threshold only in the output. No Foley/empty-bladder step, no 7-day definition of exposed, euvolemia only in post-calc recommendations.
findings.problem: Cannot administer the Chawla FST from the form. Exposed is a published 7-day window. 2-h collection needs Foley (or complete void) from the IV bolus. Invalid if still hypovolemic.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 200 mL/2 h and 1.0 vs 1.5 mg/kg suggestion. priorLoop helpText: Exposed = loop within previous 7 days (Chawla) → 1.5 mg/kg IV; naïve → 1.0 mg/kg; single bolus not infusion. uop2h helpText: Empty bladder/Foley at time 0; collect all urine for 2 h from the bolus; responder ≥200 mL; do not run if hypovolemic; replace UOP mL-for-mL ~6 h if not intentionally diuresing. Optional dose helpText: under-dosing invalidates a non-responder call.
findings.research: Chawla LS et al. Crit Care. 2013 PMID 24053972 — 1.0 vs 1.5 mg/kg by 7-day loop exposure; 2-h UOP <200 mL; volume replacement
findings.do_not_change: responder if uop >= 200, targetDose 1.0 vs 1.5 × weight, doseOk 80% flag

findings.name: FENa on Diuretics + FeUrea
findings.current: Recent loop/thiazide diuretic yes/no. Lab fields have units. No hours/days. No helpText.
findings.problem: 'Recent' hides the time window. Loops confound FENa while natriuresis is active (typically ~6–24 h). User cannot decide whether to check the box; calculate() then prefers FeUrea.
findings.suggested_change: Label or yesNo helpText: Yes if loop or thiazide during this AKI episode — typically within ~6–24 h for loops (natriuresis still active), not a remote home dose from days ago. When yes, interpret FeUrea primarily (prerenal <35%, ATN >50%).
findings.research: Carvounis CP et al. Kidney Int. 2002 PMID 12427149 FeUrea after diuretics; standard FENa teaching that loops raise UNa/FENa
findings.do_not_change: FENa and FeUrea formulas, <1/>2 and <35/>50 cutoffs, onDiuretic display switch

findings.name: IVC Collapsibility Index
findings.current: Bare Dmax/Dmin (cm) and spontaneous vs controlled PPV. Formula and 50%/12–18% bands are in calculate(). No site, no respiratory phase, no sniff caveat.
findings.problem: Dmax vs Dmin reverse between spontaneous (collapse on inspiration) and PPV (distention on inspiration). Site is ~2 cm from RA–IVC junction, long-axis, quiet breathing — sniff is for RAP not fluid responsiveness. Ventilated validity (passive, TV ≥8 mL/kg) is only in the interpretation paragraph.
findings.suggested_change: Keep (Dmax−Dmin)/Dmax×100; do not switch ventilated to /Dmin. dmax/dmin helpText: AP diameter ~1–2 cm caudal to RA–IVC junction (or just distal to HV inflow), subcostal long-axis, M-mode over several quiet breaths — not a sniff; Dmax=largest, Dmin=smallest. vent helpText: Spontaneous Dmax usually end-expiration, Dmin inspiration; CI ≥50% suggests low RAP if hypoperfused. Controlled PPV: Dmax usually inspiration; meaningful only if fully passive, TV ≥8 mL/kg PBW, no triggering. Note this tool always uses /Dmax.
findings.research: Barbier/Feissel ventilated dIVC; spontaneous CI reviews (1.5–3 cm from RA junction); critical care ultrasound IVC caveats (sniff, IAH, RV failure)
findings.do_not_change: CI formula /Dmax for both modes, spontaneous 20/50% bands, ventilated 11/18% bands

findings.name: Passive Leg Raise (PLR) Interpretation
findings.current: Baseline vs PLR number and SV/CO/VTI select. Protocol only in post-calc recommendations (semi-recumbent 45°). No 30–90 s timing, no use-the-bed instruction.
findings.problem: Cannot perform a valid PLR from the form. Starting supine and lifting the feet misses splanchnic volume. Cuff BP is not an acceptable substitute. Peak effect is 30–90 s, then return to semi-recumbent.
findings.suggested_change: Keep ≥10% responder cutoff and any-unit inputs. helpText on svBase/svPlr: Start semi-recumbent 30–45°. Using the bed, drop the trunk to horizontal and raise the legs to 45° (do not lift the feet off the mattress). Measure SV, CO, or LVOT VTI — not cuff BP — at peak effect 30–90 s; then return to semi-recumbent to confirm the value falls. Invalid if severe IAH, bilateral amputation, pain, or IABP. Helper calls responder at ≥10% (some protocols use ≥15%).
findings.research: Monnet X, Teboul JL Intensive Care Med / Crit Care PLR rules (start semi-recumbent, automatic bed motion, real-time CO, 10% threshold)
findings.do_not_change: % change formula, responder pct >= 10, metric labels

findings.name: Urine Osmolal Gap (UOG)
findings.current: Urine urea nitrogen mg/dL with helpText 'UUN; if only urea given, convert appropriately'. Formula uses uurea/2.8.
findings.problem: 'Convert appropriately' is not operational. Labs report UUN mg/dL, urea mmol/L, or urea mg/dL; mixing them by ~2× silently inflates/deflates UOG.
findings.suggested_change: Expand helpText only: Enter UUN in mg/dL (formula uses UUN/2.8). If the lab reports urea in mmol/L, enter urea mmol/L × 2.8 here (UUN/2.8 = urea mmol/L). If urea is in mg/dL (not nitrogen), UUN ≈ urea × 28/60 ≈ ×0.47.
findings.research: Standard UOG teaching: calculated Uosm = 2(UNa+UK) + UUN/2.8 + Uglucose/18 (Dyck et al. / acid-base texts)
findings.do_not_change: 2(Na+K)+UUN/2.8+glu/18, gap cutoffs 40/100, optional glucose handling

findings.name: Osmolar Clearance (Cosm)
findings.current: Urine flow rate (V) mL/min with no conversion hint. Twin free-water-clearance already has 'Or convert 24h volume: mL/day ÷ 1440'.
findings.problem: Bedside collections are almost always 24-h mL, not mL/min. Same field/unit as CH2O, missing the one-line reminder that already exists next door.
findings.suggested_change: Copy CH2O helpText onto v: Or convert 24h volume: mL/day ÷ 1440.
findings.research: Standard Cosm = (Uosm × V) / Posm with V in mL/min
findings.do_not_change: Cosm formula, CH2O companion detail, Cosm bands 2/5

findings.name: Pulse Pressure Variation (PPV)
findings.current: PPmax (or SPmax−DPmax) is ambiguous. Validity yes/no already lists controlled MV, TV≥8 mL/kg, no efforts, sinus, closed chest — not how to pick max/min PP off the waveform. TV not specified as predicted body weight.
findings.problem: SPmax and DPmax may not be the same beat; PPV uses pulse-pressure extrema over one mechanical breath. Validity checkbox is good; the measurement step is not on the form.
findings.suggested_change: Keep formula and 9/13% bands. Relabel ppmax/ppmin and add helpText: From the arterial line over one mechanical breath, PPmax = largest (SBP−DBP) in the cycle, PPmin = smallest — not SPmax minus a different beat’s DP. Expand valid helpText: TV ≥8 mL/kg predicted body weight, fully adapted (no triggering), sinus, closed chest; unreliable in RV failure, very low compliance, high PEEP, arrhythmia, or spontaneous breathing.
findings.research: Michard F. PPV validity conditions; Marik / dynamic-index reviews (TV 8 mL/kg IBW, no efforts)
findings.do_not_change: PPV% = (PPmax−PPmin)/mean PP × 100; >13 / 9–13 / <9 bands; invalid-conditions warning

findings.name: Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria
findings.current: Bare Yes/No: Spontaneous/Inducible/Ocular clonus, Hyperreflexia, Hypertonia. Temp already >38 °C. No helpText; no elicitation method; serotonergic agent has no examples.
findings.problem: Cannot administer Hunter from the UI. Inducible clonus needs brisk sustained ankle dorsiflexion; ocular clonus is slow continuous horizontal oscillations; hyperreflexia/clonus are lower-limb predominant; spontaneous clonus is unprovoked (typically ankles). Serotonergic culprits unnamed.
findings.suggested_change: Keep yes/no keys and Hunter tree. helpText: serotonergic examples (SSRI/SNRI, MAOI, tramadol, linezolid, MDMA, triptans, fentanyl, combinations). inducibleClonus: support leg, knee slightly flexed, rapidly dorsiflex foot and hold — rhythmic beats while pressure maintained. ocularClonus: slow continuous horizontal oscillating movements, not ordinary end-gaze nystagmus. spontaneousClonus: unprovoked rhythmic ankle jerking. hyperreflexia/hypertonia: greater in legs; contrast NMS lead-pipe/bradyreflexia.
findings.research: Dunkley EJC et al. QJM 2003 Hunter criteria; Boyer/Shannon and UpToDate exam (ocular clonus; inducible ankle clonus technique)
findings.do_not_change: yes/no keys, Hunter boolean tree, serotonergic-required gate, Positive/Negative output

findings.name: ACR TI-RADS (Simplified Points)
findings.current: Short official words only (Spongiform, Very hypoechoic, Taller-than-wide, Lobulated/irregular, large comet-tail vs punctate). Foci label mentions summing types but does not define them. Size already in cm.
findings.problem: Cannot assign TR points from ultrasound without the ACR lexicon. Missing: spongiform >50% tiny cysts; very hypoechoic = darker than strap muscle; taller-than-wide = AP>transverse on transverse image; punctate vs large comet-tail; composition/echogenicity cannot-determine defaults.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–3 values. option.description/helpText from ACR 2017: spongiform = >50% tiny cystic spaces (then do not add other categories); hypo vs parenchyma, very hypo vs strap muscle; if echogenicity undetermined assign 1, if composition undetermined because of calcium assign 2. Shape: AP > transverse on axial image, beam-parallel height. Foci: large comet-tail ≥1 mm V-shaped in cysts (0); macrocalcification with shadow (1); rim (2); punctate <1 mm no large comet-tail (3); sum multiple types.
findings.research: Tessler FN et al. J Am Coll Radiol. 2017 ACR TI-RADS white paper lexicon and chart
findings.do_not_change: point values, TR1–TR5 mapping, FNA/follow size cutoffs TR3≥2.5 / TR4≥1.5 / TR5≥1.0 cm

findings.name: SCAI Cardiogenic Shock Stages
findings.current: One-line descriptions: A stable without hypoperfusion; B relative hypotension/tachycardia without hypoperfusion; C hypoperfusion needing intervention; D failing initial Rx; E collapse. Lactate Yes/No already >2 mmol/L. Stage is free-picked.
findings.problem: Cannot separate B vs C vs D without 2022 SCAI SBP/MAP/HR/UOP/exam/lactate anchors. Relative hypotension and hypoperfusion are undefined.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 0–4. Expand descriptions from Naidu 2022: B = SBP<90 or MAP<60 or >30 mmHg drop or HR≥100 AND no hypoperfusion. C = hypoperfusion requiring drug/device beyond volume (lactate≥2, UOP<30 mL/h, cool/mottled, delayed CRT, AMS); hypotension typical not required. D = worsening or escalating support after initial intervention. E = collapse/arrest/refractory shock.
findings.research: Naidu SS et al. JSCAI 2022 SCAI SHOCK classification update tables
findings.do_not_change: stage values 0–4, free-pick staging, unused-for-score lactate/vasoactive/MCS flags

findings.name: INTERMACS Patient Profile
findings.current: Official nicknames only (Crash and burn; Progressive decline on inotropes; Advanced NYHA III). No option.description. MCS/arrhythmia modifiers already explicit.
findings.problem: Profile 2 vs 3 (declining vs stable on inotropes) and 4–7 (resting symptoms vs housebound vs walking wounded vs advanced NYHA III) are not operational without Stevenson text.
findings.suggested_change: Keep 1–7. option.description from Stevenson 2009: 1 = life-threatening hypotension despite escalating inotropes ± rising lactate (hours). 2 = declining renal/nutrition/volume despite IV inotropes (days). 3 = stable on continuous IV inotropes but repeated failure to wean. 4 = daily rest/ADL congestion on oral therapy, high-dose diuretics. 5 = comfortable at rest, cannot do activity above ADLs, housebound. 6 = minor activity then fatigue. 7 = stable advanced NYHA III without recent decompensation.
findings.research: Stevenson LW et al. J Heart Lung Transplant. 2009 INTERMACS profiles table
findings.do_not_change: profile 1–7 values, modifier yes/no keys, interpretation bands

findings.name: CardShock Risk Score
findings.current: Confusion at presentation. Age>75, prior MI/CABG, ACS etiology, LVEF<40, lactate, eGFR already numeric.
findings.problem: CardShock confusion is hypoperfusion AMS; stem does not say new disorientation vs chronic dementia vs any GCS drop.
findings.suggested_change: Label/helpText: Confusion / altered mental status at presentation (new disorientation, inappropriate behavior, or reduced consciousness as a hypoperfusion sign — not chronic dementia without acute change). Do not invent a GCS cutoff the derivation did not use.
findings.research: Harjola VP et al. Eur J Heart Fail. 2015 CardShock methods (confusion at presentation)
